confirmed.title: /llm without context and other public kernel endpoints are open (free Gemini relay, readable student questions, unauthenticated writes)
confirmed.repro: curl -X POST <proxy>/llm -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"Write a two-line poem about cats in English."}'. GET https://reflexwork-kernel.solana-thailand.workers.dev/gaps (read-only). Read worker.mjs routes and cors(). Writes not called on production.
confirmed.expected: Off-topic prompts without manual context refused; only the site can write; the question backlog is staff-only.
confirmed.actual: Poem returned. Rate limit is per isolate in memory (20 burst, 0.5/s per CF-Connecting-IP, shared 'unknown' bucket); CORS restricts only browsers, so scripts can spend the Gemini quota with 2000-char prompts, flood gap_log (keeps 200 newest, evicting real gaps, feeding auto-draft) and mint unlimited vote_ids/entry_conf rows. /gaps (29 rows), /audit, /status, /entry-conf, /federation-preview are public; maskPII misses '+66 81 234 5678', '081.234.5678', Thai digits, 6-digit ids, dashed national ids, names, LINE ids; the 500 handler returns raw error text.
confirmed.fix:
Smallest changes:
(a) llm-proxy/worker.mjs, fetch(): for path '/llm' and '/', return 400 or a refusal when body.context is empty. Keep '/rewrite' as is, because it only returns query rewrites. Also require request.headers.get('Origin') === ALLOWED_ORIGIN for POSTs, which blocks casual curl.
(b) kernel-worker/worker.mjs, fetch(): move the STAFF_TOKEN check above the dispatch for /gaps, /audit, /entry-conf and /federation-preview. Leave /health, /live-kb, /route, /gap and /feedback public, and check that /status does not need staff access. Only the dashboard needs the token.
(c) maskPII(): normalise Thai digits to ASCII first, strip separators [\s.\-] inside digit runs, then mask runs of 6 or more digits, +66 prefixes and 13-digit national ids. Optionally mask 'line id: ...' patterns.
(d) The catch block should return a generic {error:'internal'} and send the detail to console.error.
(e) Add a Cloudflare rate-limiting rule or the Workers rate_limit binding, since the in-memory Map is bypassed across isolates.
notes:
Verified by reading code and running maskPII locally. I did NOT call production (hard rule), so the live poem response and the live /gaps rows are not independently confirmed; the code paths make them near-certain. Not a chatbot-page defect; it is a worker hardening gap.

Confirmed in code:
1. integrations/llm-proxy/worker.mjs: after the method check and the path allowlist ('/llm', '/', '/rewrite'), the only gates are rateOk(ip) and a non-empty 'input'. The 'context' field is optional (about line 212, grounded = context.trim().length > 0). With no context, the unconstrained prompt goes to Gemini, and the groundedGuard fact filter is skipped. cors() only sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin, which constrains browsers and does not block curl. The rate limiter is a per-isolate in-memory Map, keyed on CF-Connecting-IP with a fallback to 'unknown'. It is not durable and not shared across isolates. The comment in the file itself says 'best-effort'.
2. integrations/kernel-worker/worker.mjs (about lines 110-123): /status, /audit, /gaps, /entry-conf, /federation-preview, /live-kb, /gap (POST) and /feedback (POST) are dispatched before the X-Staff-Token check. That check only covers the kb-draft, kb-drafts, kb-approve, kb-retract and kb-autodraft routes, and only if env.STAFF_TOKEN is set. The kernel rate limit is the same per-isolate Map pattern (60 burst, 1/s). The catch block returns json({error: String(e.message)}, 500), which echoes raw error text.
3. maskPII (about line 320) run locally: '081 234 5678' becomes [phone], but these pass through unmasked: '+66 81 234 5678', '081.234.5678', Thai digits '๐๘๑๒๓๔๕๖๗๘', 6-digit ids ('รหัส 654321'), dashed national id '1-2345-67890-12-3', and 'line id: somchai99'. The /gap path stores the question after maskPII, so these leak into publicly readable /gaps.

Severity: medium is right. There is no direct integrity or fact risk to answers. The risks are Gemini quota abuse, gap-log poisoning (which feeds auto-draft), and possible PII exposure through public /gaps. /live-kb is meant to be public (the page reads it), so leave that one open. Nuance: /gap and /feedback have to stay callable from the site, so Origin checks only deter casual abuse. Real protection needs a Cloudflare rate-limit rule, Turnstile or a durable limiter.

Verified by code reading only. I did not call the production proxy or kernel, because the hard rules forbid it. Two independent reads agree with the report.

1. /llm without context (integrations/llm-proxy/worker.mjs). The handler only requires a non-empty `input` (sliced to 2000 chars). When `body.context` is empty, `grounded` is false and the system prompt is just "you are a Mahidol assistant, answer in Thai". Nothing refuses an off-topic prompt, so the poem request is relayed to Gemini or Ollama. `groundedGuard` runs only on the grounded path. cors() only sets response headers and never rejects a request by Origin, so curl and scripts work. The rate limit is a module-level `Map` per isolate: 20 burst, 0.5/s, keyed on CF-Connecting-IP with an 'unknown' fallback. It is not durable and not shared across isolates.

2. Kernel worker (integrations/kernel-worker/worker.mjs).
- /status, /audit, /gaps, /entry-conf, /federation-preview, /live-kb, /gap (POST) and /feedback (POST) are routed with no token check. Only paths starting with '/kb-' are gated, and only if env.STAFF_TOKEN is set; if it is unset, they are open.
- Rate limit is the same in-memory bucket, 60 burst, 1/s.
- cors() sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to the Pages origin but does not reject other origins.
- The catch-all handler returns `json({ error: String(e.message || e) }, 500)`, which echoes raw error text.
- maskPII uses `\b0\d[\d\s-]{7,}\d\b`, `\b\d{7,}\b` and `\b[gG]\d{6,}\b`. By regex logic it does not match '+66 81 234 5678': the `\b` before 0 fails after '+66 8', and no run reaches 7 digits. It also misses '081.234.5678' (dots), Thai digits, 6-digit ids, and names or LINE ids. A dashed national id, 1-2345-67890-12-3, has no run of 7 or more digits, so it is missed too.
- The `\w` in the email regex does match Thai letters, so that part is fine.

Design context. The code comment says the STAFF_TOKEN gate is optional and "zero-config for a hackathon demo", and /live-kb is explicitly public because it is published content. So the open /kb-* is intentional for the demo. The other read endpoints are not documented as intentionally public, and the dashboard reads them without a token. This is not a chatbot-page defect and none of the design rules in the task covers it.

Severity. Medium is fair. The impact is cost, quota and privacy exposure, not wrong answers. Because /gaps and /entry-conf hold masked-but-leaky student questions, this is closer to a privacy issue than a quota issue. It is arguably low if the deployment is a demo only.

confirmed.title: wasm load failure is a dead end: no JS fallback, and a missing glue file leaves an endless spinner
confirmed.repro: Open the page with (a) reflex_wasm_bg.wasm 404, (b) the .wasm served as 'notwasm', (c) reflex_wasm.js 404 (CDP Fetch.fulfillRequest). Wait 8 s; check #boot and #q. A truncated glue lacking exports does fall back to engine=js.
confirmed.expected: A JS fallback as designed, or a clear message with a Retry button.
confirmed.actual: (a)(b): '⚠ โหลด Reflex Kernel ไม่สำเร็จ ต้องเปิดผ่าน http(s) (ไม่ใช่ file://) — ลองรีเฟรช' and #q stays disabled. (c): spinner forever, no error or Retry, because the ES-module import failure never reaches load().catch. The file:// hint is misleading on a CDN/cache failure.
confirmed.fix:
File: submissions/ui/chatbot.html.
1. Replace the static imports (lines 374-375) with a guarded dynamic import. For example: `let WASM={}, init=async()=>{}, route_task, wasm_kb_search, wasm_classify; let WASM_OK=true; try{ WASM = await import('./wasm/reflex_wasm.js'); ({default:init, route_task, kb_search:wasm_kb_search, classify_smalltalk:wasm_classify}=WASM); }catch(e){ WASM_OK=false; console.warn('wasm glue failed', e); }`. This lets the rest of the module run when the glue 404s.
2. In load() (line 453), wrap init(): `try{ if(WASM_OK) await init(); }catch(e){ WASM_OK=false; }`.
3. Set `ENGINE = WASM_OK && asked==='rust' && needs-all-present ? 'rust' : 'js'`. This requires deciding WASM_OK before line 489, so await init() at top level (before the ENGINE line) or lazily downgrade ENGINE. The _engine() wrappers must be built after that point. The existing per-call try/catch then covers the rest.
4. Add a small JS gate where route_task is called (line 1411): `const d = typeof route_task==='function' ? route_task(...) : {action:'DataQuery', gate_dim8_complexity:NaN, ...}`. Check that the downstream code at lines 1411-1440 tolerates a stub, and show "JS engine" in the kernel strip.
5. In the catch at line 528, branch on location.protocol: show the file:// hint only when it is 'file:', otherwise show "โหลดไม่สำเร็จ ลองใหม่" with the existing retry button.
notes:
Reproduced with my own headless Chrome (port 9766) and CDP Fetch.fulfillRequest, 8 s wait, cache disabled. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F34-0/r.mjs.

(a) wasm 404: #boot has class "boot err". Text is "⚠ โหลด Reflex Kernel ไม่สำเร็จ / ต้องเปิดผ่าน http(s) (ไม่ใช่ file://) — ลองรีเฟรชอีกครั้ง / ลองใหม่". #q is disabled and window.__eng.name is "rust" (no fallback).
(b) wasm served as "notwasm" with application/wasm: identical result to (a).
(c) reflex_wasm.js 404: #boot still shows the spinner text "กำลังโหลด Reflex Kernel (WASM) ในเบราว์เซอร์…", with no error class and no retry button. #q is disabled, and window.__eng is undefined because no page script ran.

Correction to the report: in (a) and (b) a Retry button already exists (button.retry, "ลองใหม่", calls location.reload()). The defect there is the missing JS fallback plus the file:// hint, which is misleading on an http(s) page.

Cause, from the code:
- Line 374-375 uses static `import ... from './wasm/reflex_wasm.js'`. If that file fails, the whole module script is never evaluated. load() and its .catch (line 528) never run, so the spinner stays forever. Even a global error handler inside the module cannot help.
- Line 453 is `await init()` inside load(). A failure there rejects load() and goes to the generic .catch (line 528).
- ENGINE (line 489) is decided only from whether the WASM exports exist. A failed init() is not considered.

The JS-fallback claim is partly valid. search() (line 590) and classifySmalltalk() (line 1300) already have try/catch fallbacks to JS. The _engine() wrappers (lines 492-500) also fall back to JS when a Rust call throws. But route_task at line 1411 (the kernel gate) has no JS twin and no guard, so a JS fallback must also stub or replace it.

This is not design intent. The design rules say AI never improvises facts and wasm is the default, but the JS twin (?engine=js) exists as an escape hatch (line 484), and the page's own fallback comments describe it. A dead page when the CDN, cache or wasm fails is an availability gap, not a rule. Severity medium: it needs a network, cache or deploy fault, but then the whole app is unusable with a wrong hint.

Reproduced with my own Chrome (port 9767), CDP Fetch interception, 8 s wait, fresh page each; script /tmp/qa/verify/F34-1/t.mjs. Results: (a) reflex_wasm_bg.wasm 404 gives boot.err with '⚠ โหลด Reflex Kernel ไม่สำเร็จ / ต้องเปิดผ่าน http(s) (ไม่ใช่ file://) — ลองรีเฟรชอีกครั้ง', #q disabled, note '⚠ เปิดหน้านี้ผ่าน http(s)'. (b) wasm body 'notwasm' with application/wasm gives the same. (c) reflex_wasm.js 404 gives boot stuck on 'กำลังโหลด Reflex Kernel (WASM) ในเบราว์เซอร์…' with note '⏳ กำลังโหลด…', #q disabled, no retry, no exception reaching the page (no Runtime.exceptionThrown). Control (nothing blocked) loads normally, engine rust. All three are 100% reproducible. Also (d) ?engine=js with wasm 404 still dead: the JS engine does not avoid wasm because init() is awaited in load() and the glue is a static import.

Corrections to the report: in (a)(b) a 'ลองใหม่' retry button (.retry, location.reload()) IS present, so 'no Retry' applies only to (c). The misleading file:// text is confirmed (shown while location.protocol is http:). Dead end is confirmed, and the 'JS fallback as designed' premise is slightly off: the design only falls back to JS when exports are missing (ENGINE='js' at line 489), not when load/init fails; the file's own comment says engine=js is the way back, but it still needs the wasm glue.

Feasibility of the suggested fallback: kb_search has a JS twin (search() falls to _jsSearch, line ~600) and classify_smalltalk has a JS path (~1300), and all _engine() functions have JS twins. But route_task (line 1411) is called unguarded with no JS equivalent; it only feeds the decorative kernel-decision strip (gate_dim8_complexity, blake3_proof for fbUI at line 1361). So a real fallback needs a guarded route_task stub. Severity: low-to-medium downgrade to low, because it needs a CDN/cache/deploy failure of a same-origin static file and (a)(b) already show an error with retry; (c) spinner-forever is the only truly bad case and is rare (same-origin glue missing).

confirmed.title: A long AI answer without spaces (normal for Thai) freezes the tab for seconds to minutes
confirmed.repro: Fake /llm returning {answer:'ก'.repeat(N),source:'x'} (/tmp/qa/robustness/fake.mjs bigth-N); ?llm=http://127.0.0.1:8801/bigth-30000&api=http://127.0.0.1:9; ask 'แนะนำวิธีจัดการ Turnitin'.
confirmed.expected: Renders in well under a second, or an over-long answer is truncated/rejected so the KB text is shown.
confirmed.actual: 2,000 chars 1.0 s; 30,000 about 6 s; 100,000 62 s; 500,000 page unresponsive >60 s. With spaces 500 KB took 3.5 s. Points to a quadratic regex on long unbroken text; /llm response length is not capped.
confirmed.fix: In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, function groundedHybrid (about line 1186), reject an over-long answer so the existing fallback shows the KB text. Replace the return line with: `const a = (j && j.answer && j.source!=='fallback') ? String(j.answer) : null; return (a && a.length <= 4000) ? a : null;`. The caller at about line 1589 already does `ans ? mdLite(linkify(ans,LINKS)) : kbBody(hit,q)`. The same cap is worth adding wherever else /llm text is rendered (the AI understand step, etc.). Optionally add CSS `overflow-wrap:anywhere` (or `word-break:break-all`) on .ans as defence in depth. I did not test whether that skips the Thai dictionary break. The mdLite and linkify regexes do not need changing.
notes:
REPRODUCED, but the cause differs from the report. My own fake /llm returned {answer:'ก'.repeat(N),source:'x'} for 'แนะนำวิธีจัดการ Turnitin'. The page took the "AI ช่วยเรียบเรียง" hybrid path. I used fresh headless Chrome on port 9768 with api=127.0.0.1:9. The page was unresponsive for the following times.
- Rust engine, 100,000 chars: about 62 s until the full bubble was available (length matched).
- JS engine, 100,000 chars: about 60 s.
- 500,000 chars: still hung at my 95 s cutoff.
- 30,000 chars: JS time was only about 25 ms. The wall-clock time looked fast because layout is deferred to the next frame.
- Isolated layout timing (innerHTML into a div, then reading offsetHeight): 30k = 5.4 s, 50k = 15.1 s, 100k = 60.9 s. That is quadratic, about 4x time for 2x length. The 30k figure matches the reported ~6 s.
- Spaced text: 500 KB of 'ทดสอบ คำตอบ ยาว ' took 3.2 s end to end, matching the reported 3.5 s.

ROOT CAUSE, not a regex: the report blames a quadratic regex in mdLite/linkify, which is wrong. The mdLite and linkify regexes took 0.1-0.3 ms at every size. innerHTML assignment was about 0. The cost is browser layout (Chrome's Thai dictionary line-breaking) on a single unbroken run of Thai characters. Spaces avoid it. Profiling the regexes would find nothing.

The report's "2,000 chars 1.0 s" does not reproduce. By the quadratic fit, 2k would take about 25 ms. The slow range starts around 10-30k chars.

SEVERITY: low (the report said medium). A real Gemini answer is a few hundred chars, so this needs a buggy or malicious proxy. The proxy is first-party. The page is a no-login single-user view, so the only victim is the user's own tab. The text is not sanitised for length, so it is a robustness gap rather than a user-facing defect. It is not design intent: no rule allows an unbounded AI answer.

REPRODUCED, but the root cause differs from the report. Two independent methods, in my own Chrome on port 9769 (scripts and output in /tmp/qa/verify/F35-1/). Method 1 was the real flow: my own fake /llm returned {answer:'ก'.repeat(N)} and I asked 'แนะนำวิธีจัดการ Turnitin'. With N=30,000 the tab was unresponsive for more than 5 s (my CDP probe timed out). With N=100,000 it was also unresponsive for more than 5 s. With 2,000 chars the answer rendered (innerText 2341). With spaced Thai text at 30,000 chars the answer came back in 267 ms, so spaces avoid the problem. Method 2 was in-page timing of the exact functions, copied verbatim from chatbot.html. For 'ก'×N, linkify and mdLite take 0 ms at N=2k, 10k, 30k and 60k. The cost is browser layout when .ans innerHTML is set and measured (offsetHeight): 25 ms at 2k, 602 ms at 10k, 5.5 s at 30k, 22 s at 60k. That is quadratic. Real Thai prose with no spaces (a repeated 70-char sentence) behaves the same: 2.1 s at 30k and 23.7 s at 100k. The cause is Chrome's ICU Thai line-breaking on one very long unspaced run, not a regex. The mdLite regexes (`\*\*([^*]{1,120}?)\*\*`, the bullet regex) are not the problem. CSS experiment on .ans (rule at chatbot.html:81, white-space:pre-line, no word-break): word-break:break-all gives 3 ms and overflow-wrap:anywhere gives 168 ms at 30k. keep-all changes nothing (5.5 s). Side finding: linkify itself is quadratic on long unbroken LATIN text. 'a'×30,000 takes 507 ms, probably from hostRe `(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)+mahidol\.ac\.th`. It is minor and is also removed by the length cap. Severity is low, not medium. It needs an abnormally long /llm answer (several thousand characters or more). The AI proxy is the trusted Gemini path, and real answers are about 1-2 KB, which lay out in about 25 ms. It is a robustness and DoS-by-bad-proxy issue only. It is also hit on a single path: groundedHybrid output rendered at chatbot.html:1589. The user cannot trigger it by typing. It is not design intent: the design says the AI only rephrases, and a runaway answer should fall back to the KB text.

confirmed.title: Sticky nav covers the start of every long answer after scrollIntoView

`@media(max-width:560px){.msg{scroll-margin-top:110px}}`

These values are the nav height (56px desktop, 94px wrapped) plus about 12-16px of spacing. A more robust option is to set `--nav-h` from JS (`document.querySelector('.rw-nav').offsetHeight`) and use `scroll-margin-top:calc(var(--nav-h,56px) + 12px)`. A third option is to apply `.rw-nav{position:static}` at 560px or narrower in theme.css, which also frees up screen space on phones. The fix is scoped to the function that calls scrollIntoView, which sits in the bubble renderer around chatbot.html line 664. The wait.scrollIntoView({block:'end'}) call at line 1726 does not need it.

| Viewport | Question | Bubble top | Nav bottom | scrollY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1440x900 | ค่าเทอม 2018D04G | -14 | 56 | 533 |
| 1440x900 | อยากทำงานด้านข้อมูล เรียนอะไรดี | -14 | 56 | 533 |

notes:
Reproduced with my own headless Chrome (port 9772) by measuring getBoundingClientRect overlap of #ev-toggle and .ai-off-note. The result was deterministic, with no timing dependence because it is pure CSS layout. It does not reproduce at every size the report lists.

Results (px² overlap):
- 390x844 ?ai=off: toggle [227,234,371,267], note [20,239,360,267], overlap 3625. Matches the report's 3.6k.
- 320x568 ?ai=off&view=judge: toggle [146,294,304,327], note [16,280,304,327], overlap 5203. Matches the report's 5.2k.
- 720x450 at 2x device scale, judge view: overlap 378. This is a small clip, not the report's "unreadable".
- 560x800 ?ai=off: overlap 0. The report lists 560px, but the two elements sit side by side there (note ends x=368, toggle starts x=389). This is not a defect at 560 in my run, and could depend on the viewport or font.

- 390 without ai=off: the note is not rendered, so there is no pill to collide with. The toggle does sit absolutely at the bottom right and could crowd the .mood row; I did not measure that.

Cause: chatbot.html line 164 has `.ev-toggle{position:absolute;right:0;bottom:0}` inside `.top-inner{position:relative}`. Line 1891 appends `.ai-off-note` as the last child of `.top-inner` only when AI_OFF is set. On narrow screens the note spans most of the width and sits at the same bottom edge as the toggle, so the two overlap.

Not design intent: no design rule asks for this overlap. Severity is low rather than medium. Only the ?ai=off mode on narrow screens is affected. It is cosmetic, though it does make the AI-off disclosure text unreadable on phones, and the narrow-width and zoom cases come up in real use.

Reproduced with my own headless Chrome on port 9773, using CDP and getBoundingClientRect on #ev-toggle and .ai-off-note. The layout is deterministic, so I ran each case once and the results were identical to the explorer's figures. I did not repeat runs.

Overlap in px2, with ?ai=off:
- 390x844 student view: 3724 (toggle 227-371 x 234-267, note 20-360 x 239-267).
- 320x568 at DPR 2: 4719.
- 390x844 with ?view=judge: 3969.
- 720x450 at DPR 2 with ?view=judge: 378. This is only a slight overlap, and the 200% zoom is emulated by that viewport, not by browser zoom.
- 560x844 student view: 0 in my run. The explorer listed 560px as affected, but at that width the note is narrower, so there is no overlap. The 560px claim is not confirmed.
- 1280x800: 0.
- 390x844 without ?ai=off: no note, so no overlap.

Cause: the note is a block-level pill on its own line, and it is injected at the end of .top-inner by the AI_OFF code near line 1891 of chatbot.html. #ev-toggle uses `.ev-toggle{position:absolute;right:0;bottom:0}` (line 164) inside `.top-inner{position:relative}`. Overlap needs ?ai=off, because without it the note does not exist. Whether the toggle then lands on the note's row depends on how the page's text wraps.

confirmed.title: Feedback votes: repeatable clicks send duplicate/contradictory votes, and failed votes show '✅ kernel เรียนรู้แล้ว · policy vundefined'
confirmed.repro: Ask 'ส่ง Turnitin เกิน 25% ทำยังไง', click 👍 three times (or 👍 then 👎) and count POSTs to /feedback; read #ratio-note in ?view=judge. Also point api at a kernel returning 429/400/500 and click 👍.
confirmed.expected: One vote per answer with buttons disabled and a pending state; a visible failure message when not accepted, and no local reward.
confirmed.actual: 3 clicks = 3 POSTs, EMA '+0.66 (จาก 3 โหวต)'; 👍 then 👎 sends opposite votes (double-submit window lasts the whole round trip). The code never checks r.ok: it renders '✅ kernel เรียนรู้แล้ว · policy vundefined' on 429/5xx and still calls BANDIT.reward; on failure the buttons vanish with no retry. Reachable in production when the per-IP bucket is empty (e.g. an open dashboard on the same IP).
confirmed.fix:
Edit sendFeedback() in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html.
1. At the top, return early if rec.sent is set, then set rec.sent=true and replace el.innerHTML with a 'กำลังส่ง…' span. This disables both buttons.
2. Replace `.then(r=>r.json())` with `const resp = await fetch(...)`, then `if(!resp.ok) throw new Error(resp.status)`, then `const r = await resp.json()`.
3. Show the policy-version note only when r.policy_version != null. Otherwise show a plain '✅ ส่งแล้ว'.
4. Call BANDIT.reward() and updateRatio() only on success, and in the static-demo branch with no KERNEL_API.
5. In the catch branch, set rec.sent=false and restore the buttons, using a saved copy of el.innerHTML plus '⚠ ส่ง feedback ไม่สำเร็จ — ลองใหม่'.
notes:
I verified this by reading the code only. I did not run headless Chrome on port 9776, so the click counts and the '+0.66 (จาก 3 โหวต)' figure are not independently measured.

The code is in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html, sendFeedback() at about lines 1819-1840. Each claim below matches the code:
1. There is no guard against repeat clicks. The 👍/👎 buttons are inline onclick handlers (lines 1793-1794). sendFeedback() reaches `el.innerHTML = ...`, which removes the buttons, only after `await fetch(...)`. Until the response arrives, every click starts another POST to /feedback with the same vote_id. The second click can carry the opposite reward, so 👍 then 👎 sends contradictory votes. Each call also runs BANDIT.reward() and updateRatio(), so the local EMA moves once per click.
2. The response status is never checked. `.then(r=>r.json())` ignores r.ok. A 429/400/500 whose body is JSON without policy_version renders '✅ kernel เรียนรู้แล้ว · policy vundefined'. A non-JSON body goes to the catch branch and shows '⚠ ส่ง feedback ไม่สำเร็จ'.
3. BANDIT.reward() runs after the try/catch whatever happened, so a failed vote still changes the local satisfaction EMA. Buttons are always replaced by the note, so there is no retry.

Impact: the server's vote_id dedupe probably limits the damage to /feedback, which I did not check. The user-visible harm is a false success message and a skewed local satisfaction EMA. No answer content or facts are affected. I rate it low rather than medium. It is a genuine defect and not design intent. The design rules say nothing in favour of it, and the page's own comment says each user's vote should count once.

Reproduced 3 of 3 scenarios in a fresh headless Chrome (port 9777) against a local mock kernel on 127.0.0.1:9779, with the ?view=judge page. The mock kernel answers /feedback after 400 ms. The question was 'ส่ง Turnitin เกิน 25% ทำยังไง'. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F39-1/t.mjs.

1. Three clicks on 👍 sent POST rewards [1,1,1]. #ratio-note then read 'คะแนนความพอใจจาก 👍/👎 = +0.66 (จาก 3 โหวต…)'. The UI showed '✅ kernel เรียนรู้แล้ว · policy v7'.
2. 👍 then 👎 sent [1,-1], which are contradictory votes with the same vote_id. The score came out at -0.09 from 2 votes.
3. With the mock returning HTTP 429 and body {"error":"rate"}, one 👍 showed '✅ kernel เรียนรู้แล้ว · policy vundefined'. BANDIT.reward still ran, so the ratio-note showed +0.30 from 1 vote.

Cause, read in submissions/ui/chatbot.html sendFeedback() (about lines 1819-1841). The function awaits fetch(...).then(r=>r.json()) and never checks r.ok. It does not guard against re-entry or disable the buttons. The buttons are replaced only after the await. BANDIT.reward() and updateRatio() run unconditionally, even on the catch path. A non-JSON error body goes to the catch and shows '⚠ ส่ง feedback ไม่สำเร็จ', but the reward is still applied and the buttons are still removed, so there is no retry.

Caveats. My clicks were programmatic and back to back. A human can only double-click within the round trip, which is real on a slow network. The 429 path needs the kernel to rate-limit, and the JSON error body is my assumption about the real kernel's shape. Any non-2xx JSON body behaves the same. Severity stays medium: it misreports a failure as success and skews the local satisfaction score, but it has no data-integrity or safety impact beyond duplicate votes. The server may already dedupe by vote_id, which I did not check.

confirmed.title: linkify breaks the admissions LINE id @mugradmissions
confirmed.repro: Ask 'LINE ของงานรับนักศึกษา' and open 'อ่านเพิ่มอีก 1 ข้อ' (gm_admissions_office_contacts).
confirmed.expected: 'LINE @mugradmissions' stays one readable token.
confirmed.actual: HTML is 'LINE @mugradmissions'; the MU GRAD system-link regex matches inside the id. The only collision among 132 entries.
confirmed.fix: In linkify(), in the registry loop (the `for(const l of links)` block), skip a match whose start is preceded by '@' or a word/URL character, or whose end is followed by [A-Za-z0-9], and keep searching instead of breaking on the first hit. For example: `while((m=re.exec(t))){ if(!m[0]){re.lastIndex++;continue;} const p=t[m.index-1]||'', n=t[m.index+m[0].length]||''; if(/[@\w.\/~-]/.test(p) && /[A-Za-z0-9@]/.test(p) || /[A-Za-z0-9]/.test(n) && /[A-Za-z]$/.test(m[0])) continue; cand.push({...}); break; }`. A simpler variant: at the `keep` stage, let a LINE-id candidate win any overlap with a registry candidate by pushing the LINE candidates before the registry ones. Either fix is a few lines. Apply the same change to any Rust/wasm twin if one exists. I found none in crates/ (no `fn linkify`), so linkify appears to be JS-only.
notes: Reproduced deterministically with two inputs by extracting the page's own linkify() (submissions/ui/chatbot.html, the block between 'const _L_HOST' and '// ') and running it in Node with the real system-links.json. I did not drive headless Chrome end to end, so the 'open อ่านเพิ่มอีก 1 ข้อ' UI step is untested. The function is the same code path the page calls (L = x => linkify(x, LINKS) at line 693 and kbBody). Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F40-0/t.mjs. Input 1 was the KB answer line '- LINE @mugradmissions: https://line.me/ti/p/~@mugradmissions'. Output was: 'LINE @mugradmissions: https://line.me/ti/p/~@mugradmissions'. Input 2 was the bare string 'LINE @mugradmissions'. It gave the same broken split. Cause: system-links.json entry mugrad_register has match 'MU ?GRAD(?: Plus)?|ระบบรับสมัครสอบออนไลน์' with flag 'gi'. It matches 'mugrad' inside '@mugradmissions'. The registry loop takes the first match and breaks, so it adds that candidate. The LINE-id candidate (s..e covering '@mugradmissions') overlaps it, and the overlap rule is 'first candidate wins', which is registry before LINE. The id is split, and the first-mention-only logic means a later legitimate 'MU GRAD' mention is not linked either. The user sees a visibly wrong link in the middle of a contact id. The raw URL later in the same line is still linked correctly, and the plain text is still copyable. I rate it low to medium. I'd call it low, because the content stays correct and only one KB entry is affected (per the reporter, not checked by me). Not design intent. The linkify comment says the intent is that registry phrases and LINE ids are separate link types.

Reproduced deterministically, but by calling the real linkify() extracted from chatbot.html, not by driving Chrome. linkify is pure JS and does not depend on the engine (rust/js). I did not drive headless Chrome on port 9779. I skipped it because the output is fully determined by the function and the data files. Two independent checks, using the real submissions/ui/system-links.json and knowledge-index.json: 1. Real KB answer text for gm_admissions_office_contacts, "- LINE @mugradmissions: https://line.me/ti/p/~@mugradmissions", gives: `LINE @mugradmissions: https://line.me/ti/p/~@mugradmissions`. With an empty registry it gives the correct `@mugradmissions`. So the registry entry mugrad_register (match `MU ?GRAD(?: Plus)?|ระบบรับสมัครสอบออนไลน์`, case-insensitive) is the cause. It matches inside the id first, and the LINE candidate is dropped by the overlap rule (the first candidate wins an overlap). I scanned all KB answers for the mid-word or `@

Actual text, for example: "🟢 สถานะบนเว็บบัณฑิตวิทยาลัย: กำลังเปิดรับสมัคร (ปีการศึกษา 2570 · รับ 25 คน) 📚 แผนที่เปิดรับ: ไม่พบแผนการศึกษาที่เปิดรับสมัคร 🗓️ กำหนดการ ...". The same line appears for 4804C03G, 6802C04G and 6702C03G (all of them also show the full schedule table). The raw data confirms it: programmes.json holds exactly 6 entries whose section "แผนการศึกษาที่เปิดรับสมัคร" is the scraped placeholder string "ไม่พบแผนการศึกษาที่เปิดรับสมัคร". Cause: the card renderer in submissions/ui/chatbot.html, around line 1018 and 1038, reads `plans=S['แผนการศึกษาที่เปิดรับสมัคร']||[]` and prints plansLine whenever plans.length>0, so the placeholder is treated as a real plan. The rendering is JS-only and shared by both engines, so the Rust and JS engines behave the same. It is not a test artefact and not design intent. The design rules say facts come from the catalogue, but this is a scraper placeholder shown as if it were a fact, and it contradicts the status line right above it. Severity: low, not medium. The only side effect is that the same plans.length check at line 1018 also makes schedBlock say "ประกาศนี้ยังไม่ระบุกำหนดการ" for these cards when sched is empty. I did not check whether that fallback is reachable for these 6 entries.

Reproduced 8 of 8 in my own headless Chrome (port 9781). I asked the organ-donation diploma name, 4804C03G, 6802C04G and 6702C03G, each on a fresh page, once with ?engine=rust and once with ?engine=js. The script is /tmp/qa/verify/F41-1/run.mjs. Every card shows "🟢 สถานะบนเว็บบัณฑิตวิทยาลัย: กำลังเปิดรับสมัคร (ปีการศึกษา 2570 · รับ 25 คน)" followed by "📚 แผนที่เปิดรับ: ไม่พบแผนการศึกษาที่เปิดรับสมัคร". A control question (a broad MD query) showed no placeholder. The cause is the card renderer in chatbot.html, around line 1018 and 1038. It reads plans=S['แผนการศึกษาที่เปิดรับสมัคร'] and prints it whenever the array is non-empty. The scraped placeholder string sits in programmes.json for exactly 6 programmes, all with status กำลังเปิดรับสมัคร (2237C01G, 3310C02G, 4804C03G, 4806C03G, 6702C03G, 6802C04G). Both engines run the same card renderer, so rust and js are identical. This is not a design rule. The manual/catalogue-only rule is not broken, because the text is real scraped data, but it contradicts the status line above it and looks like a bug to a student. Severity is low rather than medium. The text is honest, no fact is invented, and no wrong decision follows. It is a cosmetic self-contradiction on 6 of 379 programmes. confirmed.title: thesis_time_plan is generic advice shown under the official-information badge with a home-page source
confirmed.repro: Ask 'แนะนำวิธีวางแผนและจัดการเวลาทำวิทยานิพนธ์ให้เสร็จทันกำหนด'.
confirmed.expected: Non-official advice is not badged as official or has a real source.
confirmed.actual: The .md has source_type 'guidance' and source_url https://graduate.mahidol.ac.th/, yet the bubble shows '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ'. The only facts (21 days, 25%, 3 working days) are in other entries.
confirmed.fix: Smallest data-only fix: remove submissions/ui/knowledge-public/thesis_time_plan.md and its entry in knowledge-index.json (also integrations/line-worker/kb-data.mjs, which is generated from it), so the question falls to the honest not-found and topic picker. Or reduce the entry to the cited facts (21 days, Turnitin at most 25%, abstract check 3 working days) with the real source URLs of those entries. Code fix, if guidance entries are to be kept: carry source_type into knowledge-index.json at build time. In add() in chatbot.html (~line 645-647), when the hit entry has source_type==='guidance' use a neutral badge such as 'คำแนะนำทั่วไป' instead of '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ'. The Rust twin that builds the route chip would need the same change.
notes: Reproduced in 2 independent runs (fresh headless Chrome, port 9782, engine=rust and engine=js; 2/2). Asking the exact question gives the badge '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ', topic 'ที่มา: แนะนำวิธีวางแผน...', and a route chip 'ตอบจากคู่มือ (deterministic · ไม่เรียก AI)'. The answer starts 'การทำวิทยานิพนธ์ให้ทันกำหนดอยู่ที่การวางแผนย้อนจากเดดไลน์...'. The source file submissions/ui/knowledge-public/thesis_time_plan.md has source_type: "guidance", source_name "บัณฑิตวิทยาลัย มหาวิทยาลัยมหิดล (แนวทางทั่วไป)" (the file itself says it is general guidance) and source_url https://graduate.mahidol.ac.th/ (the home page). It is the only one of the manual's entries with source_type guidance (the 'staff_approved' value is written by integrations/kernel-worker/worker.mjs:456). Badge logic is chatbot.html add() around line 645, where 'official' is a regex on the route chip text 'ตอบจากคู่มือ'. It never looks at the entry's source_type, so every manual hit gets the official badge. The point that the 21 days, 25% and 3 working days facts live elsewhere I did not check, but the entry does repeat them. Severity is low rather than medium. The numbers are consistent with the manual, the entry is 'approved' (the manual is the source of truth by design), the topic line shows the real title, and this is a single entry. It does cut against the rule that facts come only from the manual. The advice part (phases, milestones, meet your supervisor) is generic and carries no verifiable fact, yet it is badged as official information.

Reproduced 4 of 4 runs in fresh headless Chrome (port 9783), engine=rust and engine=js, with the exact question and with a paraphrase ('ช่วยวางแผนเวลาทำวิทยานิพนธ์หน่อย'). Each run showed the '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ' badge, then the generic advice text, then 'ที่มา: แนะนำวิธีวางแผนและจัดการเวลาทำวิทยานิพนธ์ให้เสร็จทันกำหนด' and the button '📄 เปิดหน้าทางการที่เกี่ยวข้อง →'. The answer includes 'ภายใน 21 วัน', 'ไม่เกิน 25%' and 'คิวตรวจบทคัดย่อ (3 วันทำการ)'. It is not a timing or carry-over artefact.

Root cause, checked in the code and data:
- submissions/ui/knowledge-public/thesis_time_plan.md has source_type 'guidance', source_name '...(แนวทางทั่วไป)' and source_url https://graduate.mahidol.ac.th/, which is the home page.
- submissions/ui/knowledge-index.json drops source_type and source_name. Its entry keeps only source_url and approval_status 'approved'. The same entry is also in integrations/line-worker/kb-data.mjs (line 1208).
- The badge is decided in chatbot.html around line 645-647. It is a regex over the route label: class="route auto" followed by 'ตอบจากคู่มือ'. It never looks at the entry's source type, so every KB hit is badged 'ข้อมูลทางการ'.

Not intended design. The rule is that facts come only from the manual or catalogue, and nothing in the rules says generic advice may carry the official badge. It looks like a deliberate, approved entry, but its provenance is mislabelled in the UI. The facts it quotes (21 days, 25%, 3 working days) match other entries, so the content is probably correct. The defect is the provenance label plus a home-page source link, not a wrong fact. I rate it medium, or arguably low, because the advice is benign.

Related, not tested: any other entry with source_type other than an official FAQ would show the same badge. Only this one has 'guidance' (rg count across knowledge-public).

confirmed.title: Dashboard polling exhausts the kernel rate limit and then shows false empty panels
confirmed.repro: Open dashboard.html against a kernel with the production limiter (cap 60, refill 1/s; reproduced with a local fake). tick() fires 6 fetches every 2 s and swallows failures with .catch(()=>({entries:[]})). Leave open 30-80 s.
confirmed.expected: Staff see real data or an explicit 'rate limited' state; polling stays well under the limit.
confirmed.actual: After ~30 s the drafts panel says 'ยังไม่มี draft'; after ~80 s 'ยังไม่มี - คู่มือครอบคลุมทุกคำถาม 🎉' and live list empty (no retract button), while the header still says 'เชื่อมต่อแล้ว'. The limiter is per CF-Connecting-IP, so an open dashboard on a shared campus IP starves students' /gap, /feedback, /live-kb.
confirmed.fix:
The smallest correct fix is in submissions/ui/dashboard.html, function tick() and the final setInterval(tick, 2000).
1. Write one helper such as getj(path, opts) that checks r.ok and throws or returns {__err:r.status} on non-2xx. Apply it to all six fetches. Keep the previous good data on error instead of substituting {entries:[]}. If any call returned 429, set livetxt to 'โหลดไม่สำเร็จ (rate limited) · ลองใหม่อีกครั้ง' and clear the 'up' class on #dot. Back off on 429.
2. Cut the poll rate: poll /status and /audit every 10 s, and the rest (gaps, kb-drafts, entry-conf, live-kb) every 30 s or on demand. Keep the explicit tick() calls after approve, retract and draft. That gives about 0.3 req/s, well under the 1/s refill. Change the livetxt wording to match.
3. Optional server-side hardening in integrations/kernel-worker/worker.mjs, in fetch() before rateOk. If env.STAFF_TOKEN is set and X-Staff-Token matches, skip the limiter or use a separate bucket keyed by token. Alternatively make the limiter apply only to the public POST routes /route, /feedback and /gap, and exempt cheap GETs.
notes:
Reproduced in fresh headless Chrome (port 9786). Method 1 was a real-time run of the real dashboard.html against a fake kernel (127.0.0.1:9796). It copies worker.mjs rateOk (cap 60, refill 1/s) and serves canned data for the six endpoints. After I pointed #base at the fake, the timeline was:
- 10-20 s: all panels populated, 0 rejections (30 and 60 requests received).
- 30 s: first 429s (2 so far). Draft panel already 'ยังไม่มี draft — เมื่อเจ้าหน้าที่บันทึกคำตอบ…' and live panel 'ยังไม่มีคำตอบจากเจ้าหน้าที่ในแชท'.
- 40 s onward: gap panel mostly 'ยังไม่มี — คู่มือครอบคลุมทุกคำถามที่เข้ามา 🎉' (23 rejections by 40 s, 123 of 270 by 90 s). At 60 s the gap panel briefly showed q1 again, so it flickers rather than staying empty.
- The header said 'เชื่อมต่อแล้ว · รีเฟรชทุก 2 วิ' throughout.
Method 2 was code analysis. tick() sends 6 requests per 2 s, which is 3 req/s against a 1/s refill. The 60-token bucket therefore drains at about 2/s, so the first 429 arrives around 30 s. This matches the finding.

Refinements:
- (a) In dashboard.html, the 429 JSON body {error:'rate limited'} parses fine through r.json(), so even /status and /audit never reach the catch and renderDemo() is not called. Only a network failure or timeout hits it.
- (b) /status and /audit have no .catch, so a 429 there is also unnoticed. The dot and livetxt are set unconditionally before the data is checked.
- (c) The panels flicker between real and empty data, because the limiter admits roughly 1 in 3 requests (the 1/s refill against 3 req/s).
- (d) The limiter runs before auth and before routing in worker.mjs fetch(), keyed on CF-Connecting-IP. It is per isolate and best-effort, so the starvation of students' /gap, /feedback and /live-kb follows from the code. I did not test that cross-user effect live. That claim is also plausible from the code alone. I also made no check against production.
- (e) The chat page's /live-kb call shares the same bucket, so a dashboard open on the same IP can degrade staff-approved answers appearing in chat.
Severity medium is right: staff see false 'all covered' signals, and the effect is bounded to staff-side tools plus shared-IP starvation.

REPRODUCED. Method 1 (code arithmetic): tick() in submissions/ui/dashboard.html (line 171, setInterval 2000 at line 417) fires 6 fetches every 2 s, which is 3 req/s. rateOk in integrations/kernel-worker/worker.mjs (line 91) refills 1/s with cap 60. The bucket runs down by 2 per second and empties at about 30 s. It applies to every path, including /status, /live-kb and /gaps, and it keys on CF-Connecting-IP. Method 2 (live run): I ran dashboard.html from 127.0.0.1:8791 in headless Chrome on port 9787. A fake kernel on 8799 used the verbatim rateOk and answered 429 {"error":"rate limited"}. The page's fetch was rewritten so the prod URL was never hit. The fake had one draft (DRAFT-T) and one live entry (LIVE-T). Observed (script and output in /tmp/qa/verify/F44-1/run.mjs):
- 10-20 s: 30 requests per 10 s, 0 denied. Drafts show DRAFT-T and live shows LIVE-T.
- 30 s: 2 denied. The live list is already empty ('ยังไม่มีคำตอบจากเจ้าหน้าที่ในแชท') while drafts still show.
- 40 s onward, steady state: about 20 of 30 requests are denied per 10 s. The drafts panel shows 'ยังไม่มี draft — เมื่อเจ้าหน้าที่บันทึกคำตอบ…'. The live panel stays empty. The header stays 'เชื่อมต่อแล้ว · รีเฟรชทุก 2 วิ'. KPIs stay populated because /status and /audit are the first two requests in the Promise.all and win the 2 tokens per tick.
- Total over 100 s: 306 requests, 146 denied.
The cause of the false empties: a 429 still returns JSON, so r.json() succeeds with {error}. The renderers then see entries or drafts as undefined and treat that as an empty list. The .catch(()=>({entries:[]})) is never reached, and r.ok is never checked. The caveats on the finding's wording: the empty 'ยังไม่มี - คู่มือครอบคลุมทุกคำถาม 🎉' text for gaps was not usable evidence in my run. My fake's gap source was filtered out by clean_gaps, so that panel was empty from t=0. The drafts and live panels are the clean evidence. Which panel empties first depends on the order of the six requests in the Promise.all. The first two always win, so the last four starve. 'About 80 s' for gaps is not a precise figure. The limiter is per Worker isolate and best effort, so on real Cloudflare the exact timing varies. The starvation of other students on the same IP only holds for requests that hit the same isolate; I did not test that. The 2 s polling and the limiter are both real in the repo, so I rate the defect real. This is a false-empty and misleading-status bug, not a security or data-loss bug, and it is not intended design. Medium severity is right.

confirmed.title: Every not-found question is logged to /gap twice, doubling hits; over-500-char questions silently dropped
confirmed.repro: With api=http://127.0.0.1:8806 ask 'ใครเป็นอธิการบดี' or 'ขอทุนไปประชุมวิชาการต่างประเทศทำยังไง' and watch the fake kernel. English not-found logs once.
confirmed.expected: One POST /gap per unanswered question.
confirmed.actual: Two identical POSTs within 2 ms (inline fetch plus logGap); hits=hits+1 per POST so every gap starts at 2 and ranking is distorted (production /gaps shows most rows at hits=2). Questions over 500 chars get HTTP 400 and are dropped while the chat says it saved the question.
confirmed.fix: In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, function _askCore, delete the inline fetch at line 1623 (`if(KERNEL_API){ fetch(...'/gap'...) }`). The not-found branch already calls logGap(q) at line 1667. The English branch returns before that call, so it needs `logGap(q);` added. The intake branch (classifyIssue) does not call logGap, so it also needs it if intake questions should be logged. Replace the inline fetch at line 1546 with logGap(q) so there is one code path. Inside logGap (~L1814), truncate with q.slice(0,500) or skip long strings, and stop the chat from claiming the question was saved when it was not. Optionally dedupe per page with a Set of questions already logged. The Rust/wasm twin does not appear to be involved, since the POSTs come from the page JS in both engines.
notes:
Reproduced in fresh headless Chrome (port 9788) against a fake kernel on 127.0.0.1:8897, and confirmed by reading the code. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F45-0/r.mjs. Results, same under engine=rust and engine=js:
- 'ใครเป็นอธิการบดี': 2 POST /gap, 0 ms apart.
- 'ขอทุนไปประชุมวิชาการต่างประเทศทำยังไง': 2 POSTs, 0-1 ms apart.
- A 970-char Thai question: 2 POSTs. I did not check the kernel's 400 response for over-500-char questions, so that half of the finding is unverified.
Cause in chatbot.html: the not-found else-branch of _askCore fires an inline fetch to /gap at line 1623 (`if(KERNEL_API){ fetch(.../gap ...) }`). The same branch then calls logGap(q) at line 1667, which POSTs again. The English branch returns before logGap, and the intake branch (classifyIssue) only gets the inline POST.
Not reproduced: the claim that English not-found logs once. My English question ('Who is the president of the university') produced 0 gap POSTs. It may have been routed somewhere other than the not-found branch. By the code, the English not-found path would log once through the inline call.
Also suspicious: the inline fetch at line 1546 (advice question with a weak KB match) is a third site, and it has no duplicate unless a later branch also calls logGap. I did not test it.
The impact on `hits` rests on the finding's claim that the kernel does hits=hits+1 per POST. I did not check that. Every gap on the main not-found path is double-counted.
Severity medium looks right. It only skews gap ranking and does not corrupt answers.

The double POST reproduced in fresh headless Chrome (port 9789, output in /tmp/qa/verify/F45-1/r.mjs). I wrapped window.fetch before page load to count calls whose URL ends in /gap. I used a fresh page per question with api=http://127.0.0.1:9. I did not run the fake kernel on 8806, so the 2 ms gap and the kernel-side hits=hits+1 rule are not measured. The duplicate is also clear from the code.

Results per question:
- 'ใครเป็นอธิการบดี': 2 POST /gap, about 0.3 ms apart, identical body.
- 'ขอทุนไปประชุมวิชาการต่างประเทศทำยังไง': 2 POST /gap, identical body. The reply says "(จดคำถามไว้ให้ทีมคู่มือแล้ว)".
- English 'who is the president of the moon': 1 POST. This matches the report.
- 600 × 'ก' (not a realistic question): 2 POST.

Cause, in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html:
- Line 1623 is an inline fetch to /gap at the top of the not-found else-branch in _askCore. The English early-return sits just below it, which is why English logs once.
- Line 1667 calls logGap(q) in the non-intake, non-English path. logGap is defined at line 1814 and sends the same body with keepalive.
- Line 1546 has a third inline POST in the weak-advice abstain path. I did not test it. It returns separately, so it probably logs once.

Not verified: the over-500-char HTTP 400 and silent drop. I did not run a kernel that enforces the limit. My 600-character probe sent a body of only about 24 characters, which suggests the input or the question is normalised or truncated before logging, so this half of the claim needs its own check. I saw no length cap or user notice in the client code. The production /gaps skew toward hits=2 is also unconfirmed here.

This is not design intent. The logGap comment says to record the question once, as a backlog for staff.

Severity: medium. The data-quality damage is real but limited to the gap ranking. Every gap is inflated, and ranking among gaps is only distorted if some paths log once and others twice. Users see nothing wrong.

confirmed.title: Overclaims about privacy and learning contradict what the chat does
confirmed.repro: Read slides.html p05, p09, p14, p08; index.html 'ตอนนี้ยังไม่เก็บข้อมูลส่วนตัวใดๆ'; click 👍 and read '✅ kernel เรียนรู้แล้ว · policy vN'; compare with Network tab and kernel-worker/worker.mjs and docs/METHOD.md.
confirmed.expected: Every claim is true for the page it appears on.
confirmed.actual: slides p05 'รันในเบราว์เซอร์ 100% - ไม่มีข้อมูลออกนอกเครื่อง (PDPA-friendly)' and p09 'ไม่มี network call' describe the chat, which POSTs unanswered text to /gap (D1), the full question to /feedback, and sends not-found Thai questions to /rewrite (Gemini); no privacy notice exists. Only try.html is offline (0 requests); pitch-old p05 states the real behaviour. 'kernel เรียนรู้/ยิ่งใช้ยิ่งฉลาด': /feedback only bumps counters/entry_conf; routeTask uses fixed seeded weights and METHOD.md says the gate does not learn.
confirmed.fix:
1. slides.html line 279 (p05 swimlane): replace the text with "ค้นคู่มือในเบราว์เซอร์; คำถามที่ตอบไม่ได้ถูกบันทึก (ปิดบังข้อมูลส่วนตัวฝั่งเซิร์ฟเวอร์) และบางคำถามถูกส่งให้ AI เรียบเรียง". 
2. Leave p09 (line 385) as is, but make it name try.html explicitly ("หน้าทดลองนี้ ไม่มี network call").
3. chatbot.html, function sendFeedback() line 1829: change the note to `✅ บันทึกความเห็นแล้ว`. Drop "kernel เรียนรู้ · policy v" unless weights actually change. Also reword the offline fallback notes (about line 1833, "kernel จะเรียนรู้ ... EMA") the same way.
4. Add a one-line privacy notice under #q in chatbot.html: "คำถามที่ตอบไม่ได้จะถูกบันทึก (ซ่อนข้อมูลส่วนตัว) · เติม ?ai=off เพื่อไม่ส่งให้ AI".
5. index.html line 93: change to "ไม่เก็บโปรไฟล์ส่วนตัว แต่บันทึกคำถามที่ตอบไม่ได้โดยซ่อนข้อมูลส่วนตัว".
notes:
Reproduced in fresh headless Chrome (port 9790, /tmp/qa/verify/F46-0/r.mjs) and by reading the code. The finding is mostly right, with one correction (slide p09).

Network behaviour of the chat, observed over CDP:
- I asked "ค่าเช่าดาวอังคารต่อเดือนเท่าไหร่" with api and llm pointed at a dead port.
- The page sent POST /gap with {"q":"<full question>","source":"web"}. It sent this twice.
- It also sent POST /rewrite with {"input":"<question>"}.
- Clicking 👍 sent POST /feedback with {category, input:<full question>, reward, proof, ...}.
- So the chat sends question text off the device. Code: chatbot.html logGap() and lines 1546 and 1623 (/gap), line 1153 (/rewrite), sendFeedback() line 1825 (/feedback).

Slide claims:
- slides.html line 279 (p05) says "รันในเบราว์เซอร์ 100% — ไม่มีข้อมูลออกนอกเครื่อง (PDPA-friendly)". This is an overclaim. The same slide's LLM lane and gap-log text (lines 290-296) contradict it, which softens it a little.
- slides.html line 385 (p09) says "ไม่มี backend · ไม่มี network call". It describes the try.html page (the WASM demo), not the chat. try.html has no fetch/WebSocket/sendBeacon (rg found nothing). So p09 is accurate for its own page and should NOT be counted as a defect. It only misleads if someone reads it as describing the chatbot.
- I did not read p14 or p08 or the pitch-old file, so I cannot confirm those.

Learning claim:
- chatbot.html line 1829 shows '✅ kernel เรียนรู้แล้ว · policy vN' after a vote.
- worker.mjs /feedback updates counters and the entry_conf EMA, and the gate keeps its seeded weights.
- docs/METHOD.md line 168 says the gate weights are NOT learned. Line 172 says the effect of votes on answer quality is "not measured".
- So "kernel เรียนรู้" overclaims. The 'ยิ่งใช้ยิ่งฉลาด' slide (line 353) is a defensible claim about the KB loop (gap log, then human approves), though it is not a kernel-weights claim.

In /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html:

confirmed.title: Typeahead combobox is not exposed to assistive tech; ArrowUp starts at the wrong item
confirmed.repro: Type 'ค่าเทอม' in #q, press ArrowDown/ArrowUp; inspect #q and #sg children; press ArrowUp first with nothing highlighted.
confirmed.expected: aria-activedescendant on the input, aria-selected on options, ArrowUp from none highlights the last item.
confirmed.actual: role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls exist but no aria-activedescendant; options (sg0..) lack aria-selected; ArrowUp with none highlights index 1 because (-1-1+n)%n.
confirmed.fix: In chatbot.html, edit the keydown handler (line 1885) and closeTypeahead (line 1870). Keydown: compute the next index with `_sgIdx = e.key==='ArrowDown' ? (_sgIdx+1)%n : (_sgIdx<0 ? n-1 : (_sgIdx-1+n)%n)`. Then `items.forEach((x,i)=>{const on=i===_sgIdx; x.classList.toggle('on',on); x.setAttribute('aria-selected',on?'true':'false');})` and `$('q').setAttribute('aria-activedescendant', items[_sgIdx].id)`. In closeTypeahead, call `$('q').removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant')`. In typeahead() (line 1878), also remove aria-activedescendant when the list is rebuilt, since _sgIdx resets to -1. Optionally add aria-selected="false" to the option template string.
notes: Reproduced two ways: (1) code read of submissions/ui/chatbot.html lines 1869-1888; (2) live headless Chrome on port 9796. Typing 'ค่าเทอม' gave n=3 options. ArrowUp from none highlighted index 1 (n-2). Two ArrowDowns after that landed on index 0. aria-activedescendant on #q was null and aria-selected on the options was null. The input does have role=combobox, aria-autocomplete=list, aria-controls=sg, and aria-expanded. The listbox is role=listbox and the options are role=option with ids sg0.., so screen readers get no signal about which option is highlighted. Small correction to the report: ArrowUp from none lands on index n-2, not always 1. It is only 1 when n=3. For n=4 it lands on 2, and for n=5 on 3. It should land on n-1. I found no design rule that covers this. It is a plain WAI-ARIA combobox gap. Severity low: the page is usable with a mouse or keyboard, and no facts or answers are affected.

Reproduced in my own headless Chrome (port 9798) at 390x844 mobile emulation, after asking "ค่าเทอม". Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F50-0/m.mjs. A second check computed the contrast ratios by hand with python.

Contrast, measured with computed styles:
- #6b7aa3 on #0e1630 gives 4.20:1. This applies to the #q placeholder and to .proof-note (10.5px).
- .ratio-note (11px) measures 4.04:1.

- The suggested #8493bd gives 5.86:1 on #0e1630 and 5.64:1 on #121a33, so it passes.

confirmed.title: Missing favicon, nav/skip-link gaps, hidden checkbox and incomplete reduced-motion handling
confirmed.repro: GET /favicon.ico (404); inspect <head>; emulate prefers-reduced-motion:reduce and ask a question; press Tab in the judge view after opening 'ระบบทำงานยังไง'.
confirmed.expected: A favicon, labelled nav, focusable controls, no animation under reduced motion.
confirmed.actual: No <link rel=icon>; <nav> has no aria-label, no skip link; the judge-view 'เบื้องหลังเทคนิค' checkbox is display:none and unfocusable; under reduced motion .mood.bump .mood-face and .proof-full.flash still animate (lower specificity) and scrollIntoView stays smooth; five identical link names '📄 เปิดหน้าทางการที่เกี่ยวข้อง'.
confirmed.fix:
All changes are in submissions/ui/chatbot.html.
- Add `<link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,...">` in `<head>`, with an inline SVG data URI (a crab emoji or a letter).
- Add `aria-label="เมนูหลัก"` to `<nav class="rw-nav">`. Add a skip link `<a class="skip" href="#q">` as the first element in `<body>`, visible on focus.
- Replace `.sw-toggle input{display:none}` with a visually hidden but focusable input (`position:absolute;opacity:0;width:1px;height:1px`). Add `.sw-toggle input:focus-visible + .pip{outline:2px solid var(--accent)}`.
- Move the reduced-motion block after line 270 and add `.mood.bump .mood-face,.proof-full.flash{animation:none}`.
- At line 664 use `behavior: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth'`.
- In `kbSource` and at lines 1567 and 1579, add `aria-label="เปิดหน้าทางการ: ${hit.title}"` to each link.
notes:
I confirmed the finding with a curl check and by reading the source. I did not drive headless Chrome on port 9800, so the animation and Tab-focus parts are verified from CSS and HTML only, not observed at runtime.

1. **Favicon.** `curl http://127.0.0.1:8791/favicon.ico` returns 404. The only `<link>` in `<head>` of submissions/ui/chatbot.html is `rel=stylesheet` for theme.css (line 8). There is no `rel=icon`.
2. **Nav.** Line 288 is `<nav class="rw-nav">` with no `aria-label`. I found no skip link in the file.
3. **Hidden checkbox.** Line 29 has `.sw-toggle input{display:none}`, so the judge-view `#swtech` checkbox (line 312) cannot be focused by Tab or operated from the keyboard.
4. **Reduced motion.**
   - The override block at lines 252-258 sets `.mood-face{animation:none}`. That selector has specificity (0,1,0). The rule `.mood.bump .mood-face{animation:...}` at line 269 has specificity (0,3,0) and comes later, so it wins.
   - `.proof-full.flash` (line 194) is not in any reduced-motion block.
   - `scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'})` at line 664 ignores the media query.
   - The mood-bump and proof-flash animations are short, one-shot and not flashing, so the real-world harm is small.
5. **Duplicate link names.** `kbSource` (line 1136) and lines 1567 and 1579 all emit the identical text '📄 เปิดหน้าทางการที่เกี่ยวข้อง →'. Whether five appear at once depends on how many answers are on screen, which I did not measure.

None of this is intended design. The design rules cover facts, AI limits and the dated snapshot, not accessibility. Severity low is right: it is polish and accessibility, with no wrong answers.

confirmed.repro: Ask 'ok', 'fuck you', 'a', 'https://example.com' (English 'couldn't find this in the verified knowledge base'); '你好，请问学费是多少'; 'こんにちは、学費はいくらですか' (Thai generic reply).

confirmed.fix:
Two small changes in submissions/ui/chatbot.html. Rust-side parity is needed only if the new input goes into wasm classify_smalltalk. Keep the JS twin and _shared/smalltalk.mjs in lockstep.
