Reproduced 8 of 8 on a fresh page per question, with both ?engine=rust and ?engine=js. Runs used llm and api pointed at 127.0.0.1:9, so no AI call was made. Output is in /tmp/qa/verify/F52-0/p.mjs.

Actual replies, identical in both engines:
- 'ok', 'fuck you', 'a', 'https://example.com' all got "I couldn't find this in the verified knowledge base (it's maintained in Thai). I won't guess — I've logged your question for the staff / KB team, and here's the official English FAQ and how to reach a human...".
- '你好，请问学费是多少' and 'こんにちは、学費はいくらですか' both got the Thai VOICE.notUnderstood text: "ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้ ลองกดตัวอย่างด้านล่าง..." plus Thai example chips. This differs slightly from the report, which called it a Thai generic reply with a hand-off. It is the "not understood" reply, not a staff hand-off.
- Controls 'thanks' and 'hello' went to smalltalk correctly. Only the Latin set is mishandled, because smalltalk is regex-gated and has no entry for 'ok'.

Cause:
- isEnglish() at chatbot.html:1133 is true for any text that has a Latin letter and no Thai letter. Any such input that misses the KB lands in the English hand-off at line ~1629.
- classifySmalltalk() has no feature for acks ('ok', 'okay', 'yes', 'no'), for one-letter input or for bare URLs. Its bye_lead matches only the Thai 'โอเคครับ/ค่ะ', not 'ok'.
- Chinese and Japanese text has no Latin letter, so it falls through to the Thai VOICE.notUnderstood reply.

Design check: the English hand-off is allowed by design, since English questions get an honest hand-off. But 'ok' and an insult are not questions, and the hand-off also logs them as a gap via /gap. That pollutes the staff backlog. A Thai-only reply to a Chinese or Japanese reader is poor but harmless, so I rate it low. The report is correct as a low-severity wording issue.

confirmed.title: Very long input freezes or slows the page (6k-50k chars)
confirmed.repro: Paste 6,000 'a' chars; 'lorem ipsum ' repeated to 20,000 chars; 'a ' x 10,000; 50k+ chars (/tmp/qa/security-pages/longq.mjs, longq2.mjs).
confirmed.expected: Reply in well under a second.
confirmed.actual: 6,000 'a' takes ~6 s before the English hand-off; 1k-10k chars 0.2-0.5 s; 20k ~32 s; 50k+ no answer within 40 s (tab unresponsive). 100k Thai chars answered in 0.35 s, so the cost is the Latin/English path. No crash.
confirmed.fix:
Smallest fix, in submissions/ui/chatbot.html:
1. In _askCore() at line ~1388, cap the text the logic reads: `const q=(normChat(typed)||typed).slice(0,500);`. Keep `add('u', typed)` as is, so the bubble shows the full text. Alternatively cap the input to the same length before normChat. This avoids the quadratic wasm work.
2. Optionally add `maxlength="500"` to the `<input id="q">` at line 344, to match /gap's limit. Truncating on paste is acceptable.
3. Root cause to check separately: which wasm export is quadratic on long Latin or single-letter token input. It is probably the tokeniser or n-gram scoring in the Rust search or route_task. The JS twin does not have this problem. If the Rust code is fixed, the cap is still a sensible guard.
notes:
Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9804), fresh page per case, default ?engine=rust. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F53-0/t.mjs. Timings are from clicking send to the final bot bubble:
- 'a' x6000: 5.4 s. 'a ' x5000 (10k chars): 8.1 s. 'a ' x10000 (20k chars): 32.4 s. 'lorem ipsum ' x1667 (20k chars): 0.69 s. Thai 100k chars: 0.25 s. Short English: 2 ms.
- The reply to the slow cases is the correct English hand-off, "I couldn't find this in the verified knowledge base (it's maintained in Thai)...". It is only slow, not wrong.
- The cost grows faster than linearly with length (6k took 5.4 s, 20k took 32 s). It is also specific to single-letter or space-separated Latin tokens, since lorem ipsum is cheap.
- The JS twin (?engine=js) answers the same inputs in 49 ms (6k), 90 ms (10k) and 309 ms (20k). So the cost is in the Rust/wasm path, not in the JS search. The finding says "Latin/English path" and does not mention this.
- #q has no maxlength (input.maxLength is -1). Line 344 of chatbot.html has none, and _askCore() (line 1386) takes the full text.
- I did not re-run 50k+ chars. The trend (32 s at 20k) makes the reported >40 s plausible. The wasm call runs on the main thread, which is why the tab hangs.
- This is not design intent. No DESIGN RULE allows an input to freeze the page.
- Severity stays low. It needs a deliberate paste of thousands of characters, there is no data or correctness impact, and it is a self-inflicted slowdown for the user who pastes.

confirmed.title: English 'list of programs' returns an arbitrary picker; English topic questions fall to hand-off or a wrong KB topic
confirmed.area: English handling on the programme path
confirmed.repro: Fresh page: 'list of programs', 'is clinical psychology open for application', 'interview date for clinical psychology', 'when is the interview for MSc Clinical Psychology'.
confirmed.expected: 'list of programs' opens the finder; status gets status or an honest hand-off; interview-date phrasing answers as 'clinical psychology interview' does.
confirmed.actual: 'list of programs' -> 8 programmes whose English title contains PROGRAM; the status question -> scholarship channels KB; the interview phrasings -> English hand-off.
confirmed.fix:
Smallest fix for item 1 is in `_askCore` (submissions/ui/chatbot.html:1427). Skip the resolver for finder phrases: `const prog = (pinned || (PROG.length && isFinderQuestion(q))) ? null : resolveProgramme(q, PROG);`. The finder branch at line 1464 then handles the question. Check tests/programme_resolve.test.mjs, and mirror the change in the rust/wasm path if it has its own copy of this ordering.

Items 3 and 4 are a different fix, in `resolveProgramme` (line ~868) and its Rust twin. They need an English stop-word list so that program, programme, list, date, for, when, is, open, application, interview and the are dropped before the needle and trigram match. The programme name 'clinical psychology' would then resolve. After that, English intent words need mapping to the existing topic detectors: 'interview' to the interview-date topic, and 'open' / 'open for application' to the status topic. Add `interview|open for|deadline|apply` to the Thai topic words used by programmeCard's topic argument. This part is larger than a one-line fix, so I would ship the line-1427 guard first.
notes:
I reproduced all four phrasings in a fresh headless Chrome (port 9806), with a fresh page per question and the same results on ?engine=rust and ?engine=js. The driver is /tmp/qa/verify/F54-0/run.mjs. It is deterministic, so I ran each question once per engine.

1. 'list of programs' returns the resolver picker. The text starts "พบ 8 หลักสูตรที่ตรงกับที่ถาม — เลือกอันที่ต้องการได้เลยครับ" and lists PhD programmes such as บริหารสาธารณสุข, ชีวเคมีและชีววิทยาโมเลกุลทางการแพทย์ and ชีวเคมี. Those are the titles that contain the English word "PROGRAM".
2. By contrast, 'list of programmes' (British spelling) opens the finder correctly: "พบ 379 หลักสูตร (กำลังเปิดรับ 207) ... 1) อยากเรียนระดับไหน". So the failure is specific to the spelling 'programs'.
3. 'is clinical psychology open for application' answers from the scholarship-channels topic ("ที่มา: ช่องทางสมัครทุนการศึกษาและรางวัลมีอะไรบ้าง"). That is a wrong topic, and it never reaches the programme's open/closed status.
4. 'interview date for clinical psychology' and 'when is the interview for MSc Clinical Psychology' both get the English hand-off: "I couldn't find this in the verified knowledge base (it's maintained in Thai)...".
5. The control 'clinical psychology interview' answers correctly. It shows "สอบสัมภาษณ์: รอบ 2 พ. 24 ก.พ. 2570 · รอบ 3 พ. 21 เม.ย. 2570", the MSc Clinical Psychology card, and "ปิดรับสมัครแล้ว". So the data exists and only the English phrasing misses.

This is not intended design. The English hand-off rule covers questions that are not in the Thai manual. Here the catalogue has the answer, and the same fact is returned when the phrasing is shorter.

Root cause of item 1:
- _P_FINDQ (chatbot.html:1050) already contains `list of programs?`.
- In _askCore, `resolveProgramme(q, PROG)` (line 1427) runs before the finder check `isFinderQuestion(q)` (line 1464).
- The resolver matches the English word "program" against the English titles ("MASTER OF SCIENCE PROGRAM IN ..."), so it returns a 'many' picker of 8 rows and the finder is never reached.
- The finder check is also the later branch for 'which programs', 'which course' and 'what should i study', so the same ordering problem applies to them.

Severity: low is correct. Only English phrasing is affected, and nothing is invented, because the user gets an honest picker, a hand-off or a related KB topic. Item 1 is the most visible, and item 3 (a wrong-topic answer) is the worst of the four. The reported symptoms are accurate.

confirmed.title: Type-to-filter box cannot find faculties hidden behind 'ดูทั้งหมด N คณะ/สถาบัน'
confirmed.repro: Open 'เรียนไรดี', click 'ปริญญาโท'. The faculty list shows 12 chips plus 'ดูทั้งหมด 44'. Type 'ราชสุดา' or 'วิทยาลัยราชสุดา' in the box 'พิมพ์เพื่อค้นหาใน 12 รายการ'.
confirmed.expected: The faculty is found or the box searches all 44.
confirmed.actual: 'ไม่พบในรายการนี้' appears although the faculty exists; after 'ดูทั้งหมด' the same text is found.
confirmed.fix: Smallest fix is in attachChoiceFilter in submissions/ui/chatbot.html. When the list has a [data-fk=more] chip, the filter's input listener should click it before filtering (or set a flag). renderFinder's draw() re-renders the list on 'more', so the filter has to be re-attached and the typed value restored and re-applied. A cheaper alternative is to change the no-match note to say 'ไม่พบใน 12 รายการที่แสดง — กด "ดูทั้งหมด N คณะ/สถาบัน" เพื่อค้นหาทั้งหมด' and the placeholder to 'ค้นหาใน 12 จาก 44 รายการ' when a more chip exists. The better fix is to have finderHtml always render all faculties and use CSS or the [hidden] attribute to collapse the extras, so the filter sees all 44. If the Rust/wasm twin also generates this HTML, mirror the change there.
notes: Reproduced in fresh headless Chrome on port 9808 (script /tmp/qa/verify/F55-0/r.mjs), plus code reading. Steps: 'เรียนไรดี', click 'ปริญญาโท'. The placeholder is 'พิมพ์เพื่อค้นหาใน 12 รายการ' and the 'ดูทั้งหมด 44 คณะ/สถาบัน' chip is shown. Typing 'ราชสุดา' and 'วิทยาลัยราชสุดา' both give dis-none visible ('ไม่พบในรายการนี้ — ลองคำอื่น…'). After clicking ดูทั้งหมด the placeholder becomes 'ค้นหาใน 44 รายการ' and 'ราชสุดา' is found (none hidden). It is deterministic, not a timing artefact. Cause: finderHtml (chatbot.html ~line 1095) renders only 12 faculty chips until showAll. attachChoiceFilter (~line 1335) filters only the chips in the DOM, so the other 32 faculties are invisible to it. The 'ดูทั้งหมด' chip stays visible, but the not-found note gives no hint about it. This is not intended design. The filter is meant to be a search inside the list, and the note is a dead end when the item exists. It is low severity: the user can click ดูทั้งหมด, and the staff hand-off is still there. The wording is misleading, though. Note: tests/programme_resolve.test.mjs evaluates finderHtml standalone, so keep that change JS-pure.

confirmed.title: A non-string AI answer is shown as '[object Object]'
confirmed.repro: Fake proxy returning {answer:{a:1},source:1} from /llm; ?llm=http://127.0.0.1:8801/wrongtypes; ask 'แนะนำวิธีจัดการ Turnitin' (/tmp/qa/robustness/ai.mjs).
confirmed.expected: Anything not a non-empty string is treated as no answer and the KB text shows.
confirmed.actual: '🤖 AI ช่วยเรียบเรียง จากข้อมูลทางการ [object Object] ที่มา: …'; the test is j && j.answer && j.source!=='fallback' then String(j.answer).
confirmed.fix: In groundedHybrid() in submissions/ui/chatbot.html (line ~1186), replace the return with: `return (j && typeof j.answer==='string' && j.answer.trim() && j.source!=='fallback') ? j.answer : null;`. No change is needed in rewriteQuery. First check whether the Rust engine or any other caller of /llm output (for example a second fetch of /llm elsewhere) has the same String(j.answer) pattern.
notes: Reproduced. I re-ran the original script (/tmp/qa/robustness/ai.mjs wrongtypes), which uses its own Chrome on port 9604, not my assigned port 9810. I also read the code. The script's fake proxy returns {answer:{a:1},source:1} for /llm. Asking 'แนะนำวิธีจัดการ Turnitin' gave: '🤖 AI ช่วยเรียบเรียง จากข้อมูลทางการ [object Object] ที่มา: แนะนำวิธีวางแผนและจัดการเวลาทำวิทยานิพนธ์ให้เสร็จทันกำหนด ...'. It reproduced on the single run I did, and the code path is deterministic. The cause is chatbot.html line 1186 in groundedHybrid(): `return (j && j.answer && j.source!=='fallback') ? String(j.answer) : null;`. An object answer is truthy, so String() turns it into '[object Object]'. The same path would show an array answer as its comma-joined text, a number as digits, and `true` as 'true'. This is not a test artefact, because the text comes straight from that line. It is not design intent either. The design rules say the AI never improvises facts and that no AI answer means the KB text shows. Part of the finding is wrong: rewriteQuery (line 1149) already filters with typeof x==='string' && x.trim(). The same wrongtypes mode returned queries [1,null,{a:1},'x'] and the page handled it. So the rewrite check is not needed. Severity stays low: it needs a misbehaving or compromised proxy, and the real proxy returns strings. The failure is cosmetic, because the text is still escaped (no XSS seen) and the KB source text still shows after the garbage string.

confirmed.title: A single malformed data row hangs the whole page
confirmed.repro: Serve programmes.json as {"programmes":[null,{},{"code":"A"},7]}, knowledge-index.json as [null,5,"x",{},{"title":"x"}], or agency.json as {"examples":null}; ask 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' (deps.mjs).
confirmed.expected: Bad rows skipped and the manual still answers.
confirmed.actual: Bad programmes: the Rust resolver throws, the JS twin hangs, and every later question times out at 40 s with no message. Bad KB rows: uncaught TypeError 'Cannot read properties of null', first question never answers. agency.json {examples:null}: input never enables. Shipped data is valid; bites only after a bad edit.
confirmed.fix:
All in submissions/ui/chatbot.html.
(a) load(): after fetching the KB, add KB = KB.filter(e => e && typeof e === 'object' && typeof e.title === 'string' && typeof e.answer === 'string'). Check the real required fields first, since search() also reads e.keywords.
(b) The programmes fetch (line 459): PROG = d.programmes.filter(p => p && typeof p === 'object' && p.code && p.name). Check the field names used by resolveProgramme. Assign PROGDOC only when the filtered list is non-empty.
(c) loadAgency (line 418): after the Object.assign, restore the array fields, e.g. if(!Array.isArray(AGENCY.examples)) AGENCY.examples = NEUTRAL_AGENCY.examples; with the same check for any other array field.
(d) ask() (line 1847): wrap the _askCore() call in try/catch. In the catch, show the existing not-found bubble with the staff hand-off and remove any .typing node, so the page never goes silent.
(e) Optional: a CI schema check for the three JSON files.
notes:
Reproduced all three in my own headless Chrome (port 9812) in two independent ways. I used a private overriding static server on a random port, not 8791. I ran it with ?engine=rust and ?engine=js, and a control run with unmodified data. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F57-0/run.mjs.

Control (valid data): 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' answers in 23 ms and 9 ms with "ข้อมูลทางการ ภายใน 21 วัน ..." and no errors.

1. programmes.json = {"programmes":[null,{},{"code":"A"},7]}: the input enables, but both questions time out (8 s cap, no bubble finishes). The page throws "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'title')". The same happens with engine=js and engine=rust. Two corrections to the report: the JS twin throws the same TypeError rather than hanging in a loop, and the error appeared in the JS twin and in the default Rust run alike. I did not separately confirm the Rust resolver throws in wasm. The user-visible result is the same either way: an uncaught exception inside _askCore leaves the question unanswered and gives no message.
2. knowledge-index.json = [null,5,"x",{},{"title":"x"}]: the input enables, but both questions time out. The error is "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'keywords')". Array.isArray and length are the only checks in load().
3. agency.json = {"examples":null}: the input never enables (disabled stays true). loadAgency Object.assigns the null over NEUTRAL_AGENCY.examples, so applyAgency throws on AGENCY.examples[0] inside load() before ready=true.

Not design: the design rules say an unknown question gets an honest not-found with a staff hand-off, not silence. Shipped data is valid, so severity stays low (it only bites after a bad edit or a corrupt deploy). It is cheap to harden.

confirmed.title: Optional agency.json 404 is a red console error on every load; DOM grows without bound in long sessions
confirmed.repro: Open the page with DevTools ('Failed to load resource: 404 /agency.json'). Ask 300 questions: DOM nodes 134 -> 12,784 (~43 per question, 601 bubbles, 300 evidence cards).
confirmed.expected: No expected-absent fetch errors; optionally a cap on retained bubbles.
confirmed.actual: Console error each load. Heap flat (3.0-3.8 MB), typing latency and answer time unchanged, so growth is cosmetic.
confirmed.fix:
1. Favicon: add `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` to the head of submissions/ui/chatbot.html. This is one line and removes the favicon 404.
2. agency.json: the fetch is a real deployment feature, so do not remove it. Either ship a default `agency.json` equal to DEFAULT_AGENCY, or make the fetch opt-in (for example only when `?agency=1` or a `<meta name="agency">` tag is present) in the loader around line 418. Shipping `{}` is not enough, because the code would then treat the page as customised.
3. Evidence cards: optional, and I would skip it. If wanted, prune `#ev-list` children beyond the last 50 where cards are appended.
notes:
Partly verified. I did not run headless Chrome on port 9814 and did not repeat the 300-question DOM growth test. The 404 part is verified from the code and the server. The DOM-growth numbers are unverified.

Verified:
- chatbot.html line 418 does `fetch('./agency.json')` and returns quietly on `!r.ok`, which is intentional per the comment at line 381 (an optional per-organisation config).
- curl to http://127.0.0.1:8791/agency.json returns 404, so Chrome logs 'Failed to load resource: 404' on every load. try/catch cannot suppress that browser-level log.
- /favicon.ico also returns 404, and chatbot.html has no `rel="icon"` link. This is the same kind of console noise.

Not verified: the DOM growth of about 43 nodes per question. Bubbles and evidence cards are appended with no pruning, so unbounded growth is consistent with how the page works, but I did not measure it. The reporter says heap, typing latency and answer time stayed flat, so the impact is cosmetic.

Severity: low. This is a cosmetic dev-console issue. It is not a design rule, but the optional-config behaviour itself is intended.

confirmed.title: Guard over-drops: one invented number replaces the whole answer with a 'not enough info' apology shown as the AI answer
confirmed.repro: groundedGuard('ยื่นภายใน 99 วัน', ctx) returns 'คู่มือมีข้อมูลไม่พอสำหรับคำถามนี้ รบกวนติดต่อเจ้าหน้าที่...'. Sentences split only at . ! ? or newline, rare in Thai.
confirmed.expected: If the guard strips the answer, the page shows the manual entry text.
confirmed.actual: The proxy returns source 'gemini' so groundedHybrid accepts it; the student sees 'manual lacks info' under the matched entry's name and AI badge though the entry has the answer. Code-derived; not seen with the real model in 5 runs.
notes:
Reproduced at function level, not in the browser. I extracted groundedGuard verbatim from /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/integrations/llm-proxy/worker.mjs and ran it in Node (script: /tmp/qa/verify/F59-0/t.mjs). I did not drive the page in headless Chrome, so the end-to-end display is inferred from reading groundedHybrid and the call site in chatbot.html.

Results, with context 'ยื่นภายใน 30 วัน ...':
- 'ยื่นภายใน 99 วัน' returns 'คู่มือมีข้อมูลไม่พอสำหรับคำถามนี้ รบกวนติดต่อเจ้าหน้าที่เพื่อความถูกต้องครับ'.
- A longer single Thai paragraph with a space between clauses ('ยื่นคำร้องที่บัณฑิตวิทยาลัย ภายใน 99 วัน หลังเปิดภาค ติดต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ได้ครับ') returns the same apology. The split regex /(?<=[.!?。])\s+/ needs a punctuation mark before the space, so Thai prose is one "sentence" and the whole answer is dropped.
- The same text split by newlines keeps the clean lines and drops only the bad one: 'ยื่นคำร้องที่บัณฑิตวิทยาลัย\nติดต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ได้'. So the over-drop only happens when the model writes one paragraph.

Why the page shows the apology as the AI answer:
- worker.mjs lines 307-308 run `text = groundedGuard(text, context)` and then always return `source:'gemini'`.
- The Ollama path at about line 262 does the same, and local-llm-proxy.mjs line 106 returns `source:'ollama-local'`.
- chatbot.html groundedHybrid (about line 1186) only rejects `source==='fallback'`, so it accepts the apology.
- The caller at about line 1590 puts it in the bubble via mdLite(linkify(ans)). The `kbBody(hit,q)` fallback only runs when groundedHybrid returns null.
- The bubble keeps the "KB-grounded + AI" route badge and "ที่มา: <title>".

Not a design rule: the apology is honest and invents nothing, but it contradicts the manual entry the page already matched. That is the case the 'fallback' comment in groundedHybrid ("the proxy's own apology is not an answer: show the KB text instead") is meant to cover. Severity stays low:
- It needs a model to invent a number or Latin token in a single-paragraph reply, which the finding itself did not see in 5 real-model runs.
- It fails safe, with no wrong fact shown.
- The student can still see the entry title.

confirmed.title: A slow understand reply lands after a newer question and appends a stale 'not understood' bubble
confirmed.repro: Proxy delays /rewrite 6 s. Ask 'ผมจะกินอะไรดีมื้อเที่ยง', then within 1 s 'ลาพักการศึกษาต้องทำอย่างไร'.
confirmed.expected: The old pending spinner is cancelled or its result ignored.
confirmed.actual: Order: user Q1, user Q2, correct answer for Q2, then 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้' for Q1 appended last; the first spinner stays 6 s.
confirmed.fix: In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, add a module-level `let _turn = 0;`. Increment it at the top of _askCore() (or ask()). Inside the understand branch, capture `const my = _turn;` before calling rewriteQuery(q). In .then(phrases => { ... }), do `wait.remove(); if (my !== _turn) return;` as the first lines, so a late result is dropped. Also cancel the spinner on the next ask: at the start of _askCore(), run `$('chat').querySelectorAll('.msg.pending').forEach(e => e.remove());`. That removes the 6 s dangling spinner and prevents the stale bubble. Dropping the late result means the ai++ counter is not applied to an abandoned turn. Check whether the Rust engine path shares this branch; the then() lives in the page, so it appears not to. Alternatively, insert the late bubble right after its own user bubble, but dropping it is simpler.
notes: Reproduced on the first run, in a fresh headless Chrome (port 9818). The driver is /tmp/qa/verify/F60-0/run.mjs. A stub at /tmp/qa/verify/F60-0/stub.mjs delays /rewrite by 6 s. Stub setup: it listens on 127.0.0.1:9819 and is passed as llm=http://127.0.0.1:9819. Steps: ask 'ผมจะกินอะไรดีมื้อเที่ยง', wait 0.8 s, ask 'ลาพักการศึกษาต้องทำอย่างไร'. Result at t+1.5 s: greet, user Q1, a spinner bubble ('ขอเวลาสักครู่ครับ ผมกำลังลองทำความเข้าใจคำถามนี้') sitting between Q1 and Q2, user Q2, and the correct Q2 answer ('✅ ข้อมูลทางการ ยื่นแบบฟอร์ม RA-04...'). Result at t+8 s: the spinner is gone and a new last bubble reads 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้ ลองกดตัวอย่างด้านล่าง...'. That bubble comes after Q2's answer, so it looks like a reply to Q2. I ran only the one scenario. The cause is clear from the code in submissions/ui/chatbot.html (~line 1722-1727). The pending bubble `wait` is appended, then `rewriteQuery(q).then(...)` calls wait.remove() and showNotFound() or add('b',...) with no check that q is still the latest question. add() always appends at the end of #chat. ask() and _askCore() keep no turn counter. The same stale result is also unguarded in the 'one' success branch. If the late rewrite returned a matching phrase, a stale '🧠 AI ช่วยตีความ' answer for Q1 would land after Q2's answer. Also, in that branch the fbUI/addFollowUps and the ai++ counters fire for the old question. It is not design intent: the design rules require an honest not-found, but this one is attached to the wrong turn. Severity is low. It needs a slow proxy (up to the 9 s timeout) plus a rapid second question. There is no wrong fact, only a misleading out-of-order bubble.

confirmed.title: Grounded rephrase shows only a skeleton for up to 25 s before the manual text appears
confirmed.repro: llm= a server delaying /llm 30 s; ask 'อยากลาพักการศึกษา ควรทำยังไง'.
confirmed.expected: The verified manual text shows immediately and the AI text replaces it if it arrives in time.
confirmed.actual: 'กำลังเรียบเรียงจากคู่มือ…' + skeleton for 25 s, no partial answer, then raw manual text. Real proxy gives up at 18 s, the page at 25 s; a cold real call took 7.5 s.
confirmed.fix: File: submissions/ui/chatbot.html, hybrid branch near line ~1580 plus groundedHybrid() near line ~1175. (1) Render the answer at once: put kbBody(hit,q) in the .ans div with a small note 'กำลังเรียบเรียงให้อ่านง่ายขึ้น…' in place of the skeleton. In the .then() callback, replace the innerHTML only when ans is non-null. Otherwise leave the manual text and remove the note. The mid-id swap logic is already there. (2) Lower the abort in groundedHybrid from 25000 to about 20000, the proxy's 18 s plus margin. Also check that the JS and Rust twins show nothing different for this branch. The wait lives in the page and not in the wasm engine.
notes: Reproduced in my own headless Chrome (port 9820) with a local server on 127.0.0.1:9821 that delays /llm by 30 s. I asked 'อยากลาพักการศึกษา ควรทำยังไง' and polled the last bot bubble. The 30 s delay was timed from the click; sampling started up to a few hundred ms after it. The /llm request was sent once, so the bubble was waiting on it. At 2 s, 10 s, 20 s and 24 s the .ans held only the typing dots, 'กำลังเรียบเรียงจากคู่มือ…' and the skeleton (typing:true, skel:true). At 26 s the page aborted the fetch and swapped in the raw manual text: 'ยื่นแบบฟอร์ม RA-04 ผ่านประธานและส่งผ่านระบบ E-doc • เมื่อได้รับอนุมัติจากคณบดี…'. This is the 25 s timeout, since the fake server's AI-TEXT never arrived. The second route is the code. In chatbot.html, groundedHybrid() (line ~1175) sets setTimeout(abort, 25000). The branch near line ~1582 renders only the skeleton and calls kbBody(hit,q) in the .then() fallback. Nothing paints the verified text first. The wait is on the path where decideTier gives a KB hit with topScore below 6 for an advice-type question. That is the AI-rephrase tier, and it is not the deterministic tier. It only waits that long when the proxy hangs. A normal call takes about 7.5 s (cold) and the proxy gives up at 18 s. It is not a test artefact. It is also not design intent. The rules say the AI only rephrases and facts come from the manual. The 25 s wait with no verified text in sight does not serve that rule. It is a UX defect only and no fact is wrong, so low severity is right. A 25 s timeout is longer than the proxy's own 18 s budget, so it only matters when the proxy hangs rather than answers.

confirmed.title: Programme-card schedule table loses its group header and prints the ภาคปลาย open date as an orphan line
confirmed.repro: Ask 'ประกาศนียบัตรบัณฑิต สาขาวิชาการจัดการการบริจาคอวัยวะ' or 'ปรัชญาดุษฎีบัณฑิต สาขาวิชาการจัดการการกีฬา (ภาคพิเศษ)' and read below the 🗓️ table.
confirmed.expected: The open date belongs to the ภาคปลาย column or is labelled.
confirmed.actual: A bare '(เปิดรับสมัคร พฤ. 1 ก.ค. 2570)' under the table with no label; source rows 'รายละเอียดกิจกรรม | ภาคต้น | ภาคปลาย' sit above the data in programmes.json and are not shown. 104 announcements affected.
confirmed.fix: Label the note instead of rendering a group header. In _pScheduleData (submissions/ui/chatbot.html ~line 968), in the loop over lines without ' | ', check whether the line matches /^\(เปิดรับสมัคร/ and the last column is not /^รอบ \d+$/ (for example 'รอบภาคปลาย'). If both hold, push `${cols[cols.length-1]}: ${l}` (for example 'รอบภาคปลาย: (เปิดรับสมัคร พฤ. 1 ก.ค. 2570)'). Make the same change in the Rust twin, crates/reflex-wasm/src/catalogue/schedule.rs, in the function that backs WASM.schedule_table (around line 44). Then rebuild the wasm and re-run the engine A/B (benchmark/engine/engine_ab.mjs) so the JS and Rust outputs stay identical. If an open date appears with no matching extra column, leave it unchanged. Optionally, only when the header row has 2 groups (ภาคต้น | ภาคปลาย), add a one-line hint under the table such as 'ภาคต้น = รอบ 1-4, ภาคปลาย = รอบภาคปลาย'.
notes:
Reproduced 4/4 (rust and js engines, both questions, fresh headless Chrome on port 9822, script /tmp/qa/verify/F62-0/run.mjs). The table headers are ["กิจกรรม","รอบ 1","รอบ 2","รอบ 3","รอบ 4","รอบภาคปลาย"]. The element after .sched-wrap is the <small> notes block: "(เปิดรับสมัคร พฤ. 1 ก.ค. 2570)\nโปรดพิจารณาช่วงเวลาในการชำระเงินค่าสมัคร...". The "(เปิดรับสมัคร ...)" line has no label, and the ภาคต้น/ภาคปลาย group header text does not appear anywhere in the bubble.

Data check, programmes.json:
- 218 announcements have a กำหนดการสอบคัดเลือก section.
- 216 of them begin with a "รายละเอียดกิจกรรม | ภาคต้น" header row. The two variants are "... | ภาคต้น" and "... | ภาคต้น | ภาคปลาย".
- 104 have a bare "(เปิดรับสมัคร ...)" line without " | ". That matches the reported count.
- The header row carries no column-to-group mapping that could be rendered. It is only 'ภาคต้น | ภาคปลาย' and does not say that รอบ 1-4 belong to ภาคต้น and รอบภาคปลาย to ภาคปลาย.

Cause: _pScheduleData in submissions/ui/chatbot.html (line ~968) deliberately filters out /^รายละเอียดกิจกรรม/. It also pushes every line without " | " into notes. In the source the open-date line sits between the header row and the first data row, so its position (next to the รอบภาคปลาย column) is lost once it is rendered under the table as a note.

Design: this is not intended design. The facts shown are correct, and nothing is invented, but an unlabeled date is ambiguous. The date 1 ก.ค. 2570 is also well after the รอบ 1-4 dates, so a reader can easily attach it to the wrong round. The impact is cosmetic, so the severity stays low.

The Rust and JS engines show the same output, so the fix has to go in both twins.

confirmed.title: Internal citation noise and near-empty entries reach students
confirmed.repro: Ask 'กำหนดการลงทะเบียน ภาคต้น ปีการศึกษา 2570', 'ตัวอย่างประกาศ 2018DG00 ปี 2570: เอกสารและการคัดเลือก', 'การสอบคัดเลือกและการรายงานตัวนักศึกษาใหม่', 'ค่าสมัครเข้าศึกษาเท่าไร และใช้เอกสารอะไรบ้าง'.

Mostly data edits in submissions/ui/knowledge-index.json (the source feeding it may need the same change; check the import script so a rebuild does not undo them):

- gm_sample_2018DG00_2570_documents: write the actual documents and selection facts from the announcement, or merge it into the 'แผนและคุณสมบัติ' sibling and remove it. Keep 'ห้ามยกระดับ…' as an internal note, not answer text.
- gm_selection_and_new_student_reporting: add the reporting (รายงานตัว) facts, or rename the title to selection only.
- gm_application_fee: add one sentence on applying to several programmes (fee is 500 baht per programme), or shorten the title.
- Duplicate lead: in slotLead (chatbot.html ~706, and the Rust slot_lead twin), return '' when the body's first line already contains the grabbed fact, e.g. if (body.split('\n')[0].includes(m[0])) return ''. Alternatively reword admission_fee.answer so it does not begin with 'ค่าสมัคร 500 บาท.'. Apply the same check in both engines so the Rust and JS twins stay in step.
notes:
Reproduced in fresh headless Chrome (port 9824), engine=rust and engine=js, plus a direct read of knowledge-index.json. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/F63-0/run.mjs, output: /tmp/qa/verify/F63-0/out1.txt. It is deterministic: same text each run and in both engines.

Confirmed:
1. Registration schedule: the headings carry clause references. Seen live for gm_registration_2570_first, e.g. '▪ ลงทะเบียนปกติ ภาคต้น ปีการศึกษา 2570 (หน้า 1 ข้อ 3.1–3.2)', plus '(หน้า 1 ข้อ 3.3–3.6)', '(หน้า 1 ข้อ 3.7)' and '(หน้า 1 ข้อ 1, 6, 8)'. The data shows 5 entries with '(หน้า 1 ข้อ 3.1–3.2)', not 6: 2569 second semester, 2569 summer, 2570 first, 2570 second, 2570 summer. The count of 6 in the report is slightly off. This is provenance, not wrong facts, so it is cosmetic. The references are arguably useful to a judge but are noise in the student view.
2. gm_sample_2018DG00_2570_documents: the whole answer is 'ขอบเขตเฉพาะหลักสูตรชีวเคมี... ห้ามยกระดับเป็นเอกสารบังคับทุกหลักสูตร'. It is a model-facing guard sentence shown to students as the entire answer, with no documents or selection facts. Its title promises documents and selection. This is the strongest part of the finding.
3. gm_selection_and_new_student_reporting: the answer covers selection only ('ต้องตรวจประกาศของหลักสูตร บางหลักสูตรมีสอบข้อเขียน...'). Nothing on reporting (รายงานตัว), although the title promises it and the keywords include it.
4. admission_fee renders as two lines: '500 บาท' then 'ค่าสมัคร 500 บาท'. This is a visible duplicate. It comes from slotLead (chatbot.html around lines 700-707 and humanize around 693-694), which prepends the first '\d+ บาท' match as a bold lead, while the body also starts with 'ค่าสมัคร 500 บาท'. The same happens in engine=js.
5. gm_application_fee: the title says 'การสมัครมากกว่าหนึ่งหลักสูตร' but the answer only says the fee is 500 baht per programme/major ('สาขาวิชาละ 500 บาท') and is not tuition. It never explains applying to several programmes, although 'per programme' implies it.
6. gm_registration_flat_refund: the answer contains '(รวมอยู่หน้า 3 ของ PDF ฉบับที่ 3 ที่เว็บไซต์เชื่อม)'. It also renders a nested '• ▪ ลาออกในเงื่อนไข...' bullet, because the section header is turned into a bullet inside the collapsed block.
7. gm_registration_after_defense_flat: the raw answer contains an inline 'แหล่งต้นทาง: https://...Lump-payment03-Th.pdf' line. The collapsed view did not show it in my run, so this part was not seen live in the DOM; it is confirmed in the data only. It duplicates the source_url field, which already feeds the 'ที่มา' line and the official-page link.

Not a test artefact. This is not intended design: the rules forbid made-up facts, not tidy wording. The 2018DG00 entry is a guard note that leaked into the user-facing answer. Severity low is right: nothing is false or misleading, but the 2018DG00 and selection entries are thin enough to look unhelpful, and the duplicate '500 บาท' is plainly visible.

confirmed.title: Dashboard shows a stale 'sample data' banner over live data; no CSP/X-Frame-Options anywhere; dashboard clipped at 390 px
confirmed.repro: (a) Open dashboard.html; if the first poll times out (2 s) renderDemo() runs, then a later poll succeeds. (b) curl -sI https://reflexwork.pages.dev/dashboard. (c) Open dashboard at 390 px.
confirmed.expected: Banner follows the data source; framing refused; layout fits a phone.
confirmed.actual: (a) '🧪 โหมดสาธิต · ตัวเลขทุกตัวเป็นข้อมูลตัวอย่าง' beside real numbers (34 | 88% | v13): the live branch never resets #phase. (b) No Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors or Permissions-Policy on any page, so the staff 'อนุมัติ → ขึ้นแชท' buttons can be framed (clickjacking); the staff token is in localStorage. (c) Layout viewport grows to 420 px; cards, KPI grid and banner clipped; 4 touch targets <32 px.
confirmed.fix: (a) In submissions/ui/dashboard.html, function tick(), live branch (right after the line that sets $('livetxt').textContent='เชื่อมต่อแล้ว...'): reset the banner with $('phase').textContent = '🧪 ข้อมูลช่วงทดสอบ (ก่อนเปิดใช้จริง) · ตัวเลขมาจากการทดลองของทีมและผู้ทดสอบ ไม่ใช่การใช้งานจริงของนักศึกษา'. Better, store that default text in a constant and reuse it. (b) Add submissions/ui/_headers (Cloudflare Pages): '/*' with Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' plus the kernel and proxy origins; frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(). The pages use inline scripts and styles, so the CSP needs 'unsafe-inline' or nonces. Test it before deploying, because a wrong CSP breaks the kernel and AI fetches. (c) In the dashboard.html CSS, find the min-width or fixed-width rule on header, .cap and .kpis that forces 420 px, and make it min-width:0 with grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(140px, 1fr)) at max-width:420px. This was not pinned to an exact rule.
notes:
(a) Reproduced twice. A static read of dashboard.html shows renderDemo() sets #phase to the sample-data text (line 376). The live branch of tick() (lines 171-211) sets the dot and #livetxt but never touches #phase. Then I drove headless Chrome on port 9828 at 390 px against a local mock API on port 9831 (script: /tmp/qa/verify/F65-0/run.mjs). The mock delayed the first /status call by 3 s, so the 2 s timeout fired and renderDemo() ran. Later polls succeeded. Result after about 13 s: #livetxt = 'เชื่อมต่อแล้ว · รีเฟรชทุก 2 วิ', k-total = 34, k-ver = v13, but #phase still read '🧪 โหมดสาธิต · ตัวเลขทุกตัวในหน้านี้เป็นข้อมูลตัวอย่าง ไม่ใช่ข้อมูลจริง'. It is deterministic. The default banner text in the HTML ('ข้อมูลช่วงทดสอบ...') is also overwritten by demo and never restored. I had to set the #base input value, because the page ignores ?api=. This is not a test artefact and not design: the footer says live while the banner says sample data. It misleads staff and judges, but only when the first poll fails.

(b) Partly confirmed. curl -sI https://reflexwork.pages.dev/dashboard returns no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, frame-ancestors or Permissions-Policy. There is no _headers file anywhere in the repo (fd -H). One correction to the finding: the response does include referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin and x-content-type-options: nosniff, so 'Referrer-Policy missing' is wrong. The clickjacking risk is real in principle, because the page has approve and retract buttons and the staff token is in localStorage. It is hardening rather than a functional defect, and no actual framing exploit was demonstrated.

(c) Partly confirmed. In demo mode at 390 px the layout viewport grows to 420 (scrollWidth 420). The overflowing elements are DIV.cap, DIV.kpis, DIV.kpi and their children, with right edges at 419. With live data (after the successful poll, empty tables) scrollWidth stayed at 390 with no overflowers. So the clipping depends on the content shown (demo rows and banner text) and is not unconditional. I did not measure the touch targets.

Severity stays low: the banner bug is cosmetic and conditional, the headers are hardening, and the clipping is a minor responsive issue.
