- pitch-old.html line 311 loads `https://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?size=360x360&margin=0&data=https%3A%2F%2Freflexwork.pages.dev`. It is the only third-party URL I found in these pages. pitch.html line 183 uses the local `./pitch-qr.svg`.
- Neither pitch-old.html nor slides.html has a robots/noindex tag or a "superseded" banner (grep found none).
- Stale and unlabelled claims in pitch-old.html:
  - Line 212: "11 unit tests + CI".
  - Lines 213, 255 and 267: "recall@1 94%", "คู่มือ 440 หัวข้อ" and "84% ... 0 token (ไม่ใช่ประมาณการ)".
  - Lines 166 and 191: "ใหม่จริง ~20%".
  - Line 270: "~12 ชม. ... 240 × 3 นาที", presented as a headline card.
  - Lines 282-290: a "Feature Coverage" section of self-scored bars (95/95/90/90/90/75/70/65%) with no method.
- slides.html has the same "~20%" at lines 261, 292 and 510, and the same self-scored bars at slide 17 (lines 668-675).
- pitch.html has no "11 unit tests". Its grep for "85%" or "44/52" found nothing in the page text, so the 85% (44/52) figure I could not confirm there; I did not look in the README or docs.
- The only text I found marking 84% as measured is pitch-old.html line 267, which says "(ไม่ใช่ประมาณการ)", i.e. not an estimate.

Why it is not intended design: the design rules say claims are honest and estimates are labelled. The commit "label remaining ~80% claims as estimates" shows this cleanup was intended, and these old pages were missed. I did not check where pitch-old or slides are linked from. A grep of pitch.html, chatbot.html and index.html for a link to pitch-old.html or slides.html found none.

Severity: low. It is not the chatbot, and the QR request carries no user data beyond the site URL. The real risk is an inconsistent public number (84% beside the current deck's 85%) and a third-party request on a page that says it is self-contained.

confirmed.title: Web intake collects nothing: the fields the student types afterwards are treated as new questions and answered with unrelated or English text
confirmed.repro: Open chatbot.html?api=http://127.0.0.1:9&llm=http://127.0.0.1:9&ai=off (either engine). Ask 'ระบบลงทะเบียนมีปัญหา กดไม่ได้' to get the intake checklist. Then send, one per turn, the fields it asks for: 'สมชาย ใจดี', '6537001', 'somchai@mahidol.ac.th', 'ระบบลงทะเบียน', 'ขึ้น error 500', 'ไม่รู้', '๖๕๓๗๐๐๑', '1234567890123', 'somchai@mahidol.ac,th', 'ส่งเลย'.
confirmed.expected: The flow accepts or re-asks each field once, validates the ID and email, shows a summary of exactly what was typed, and gives an exit. The summary is handed to staff, as the header promises: 'ส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่' and persona.whatCan 'ผมจะช่วยเก็บข้อมูลส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ให้'.
confirmed.actual: The intake (chatbot.html ~1647-1665) is a static list of 4 unchecked checkboxes with no state. Each later message is a fresh question. The name, the ID in either digit style, 'ขึ้น error 500' and 'ไม่รู้' all get 'ขออภัยที่ยังหาคำตอบที่ตรงให้ไม่ได้ครับ…' plus exam chips. Both emails get the English 'I couldn't find this in the verified knowledge base (it's maintained in Thai)…'. 'ระบบลงทะเบียน' gets 'คำตอบไม่เหมือนกันในแต่ละปีการศึกษาและภาคเรียน — หมายถึงอันไหน?'. 'ส่งเลย' gets the thesis late-fee entry. A single message holding all fields ('เข้าระบบไม่ได้ ชื่อ สมชาย รหัส 6537001 …') is never echoed back. The staff receive only the first complaint line via /gap.
confirmed.fix: Smallest correct fix is the honest one, no state machine. (a) Change persona.whatCan in submissions/ui/chatbot.html line 397 from 'ผมจะช่วยเก็บข้อมูลส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ให้ครับ' to something like 'ผมจะบอกว่าต้องเตรียมข้อมูลอะไรก่อนติดต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ครับ'. (b) In the intake branch of _askCore (~line 1651), reword the ans/steps header to say the page cannot see or send what is typed here, e.g. 'ข้อมูลนี้ผมเก็บในแชตนี้ไม่ได้ — คัดลอกไปใส่อีเมลหรือบอกตอนโทรครับ', change the route tag from '→ ส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่' to '→ ติดต่อเจ้าหน้าที่', and add a 'copy template' button (the 4 field labels as plain text). (c) Call logGap(q) in the intake branch if the staff should see these cases. Keep the Rust/JS twin and _shared/intake.mjs (LINE) wording in lockstep. A real state machine (INTAKE_STATE in _askCore before the follow-up branch, per-field validators, ยกเลิก chip) is optional and much larger; if it is built, it must clear on any non-field input and must not send data anywhere without a real endpoint.
notes:
REPRODUCED in my own headless Chrome (port 9832, script /tmp/qa/verify/G01-0/run.mjs), both ?engine=rust and ?engine=js, with ai=off and a dead api/llm. 100% deterministic in both engines (2 independent runs, fresh page, same chat). Quotes: Turn 1 gives the checklist ("เรื่องนี้เป็นปัญหาเฉพาะบัญชี/ข้อมูลของคุณ ... รบกวนเตรียมข้อมูลต่อไปนี้ให้ครบ ... (กดติ๊กเมื่อเตรียมครบ)"). Then 'สมชาย ใจดี', '6537001', 'ขึ้น error 500', 'ไม่รู้', '๖๕๓๗๐๐๑' each get "🙇 ขออภัยที่ยังหาคำตอบที่ตรงให้ไม่ได้ครับ ... ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้". 'somchai@mahidol.ac.th' gets the English "I couldn't find this in the verified knowledge base (it's maintained in Thai)... I've logged your question". 'ระบบลงทะเบียน' gets "คำตอบไม่เหมือนกันในแต่ละปีการศึกษาและภาคเรียน — หมายถึงอันไหน?". 'ส่งเลย' gets the thesis late-fee entry ("ค่าปรับนับถึงวันที่นักศึกษา submit ไฟล์..."). A one-line composite 'เข้าระบบไม่ได้ ชื่อ สมชาย รหัส 6537001 ระบบ WE error 500' returns the login KB entry ("ระบบของมหาวิทยาลัย ... ใช้บัญชี university email") with no echo of the fields (here it does not even enter intake). The code confirms it: chatbot.html ~1650-1665 (inside _askCore, branch `const issue = classifyIssue(q)`) renders INTAKE_FIELDS as stateless <input type=checkbox> and nothing reads them; there is no intake state anywhere (rg INTAKE_FIELDS only hits the definition at line 1108 and the render at 1652).

Corrections to the finding's framing: (1) The checklist's own wording is honest: it says "เตรียมข้อมูลต่อไปนี้ให้ครบ" (prepare these) and "กดติ๊กเมื่อเตรียมครบ", and the same bubble has real tel:/mailto: buttons (IT 02-849-6022, account@mahidol.ac.th). So it does not say the chat will collect the fields; it is a prepare-before-you-call checklist, a legitimate design. (2) The real defect is the overpromise elsewhere: persona.whatCan (chatbot.html line 397) says "ผมจะช่วยเก็บข้อมูลส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ให้ครับ" and the route tag says "→ ส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่", but nothing is collected or transmitted (only the first line goes to logGap in the non-intake branch; the intake branch does not even call logGap). A student who types the fields after the checklist is told the bot can't understand them and, for an email, gets an English reply. That contradicts the "honest hand-off" rule, so it is not a design intent. (3) Severity: I rate medium, not high. No wrong fact is given, no one is misled into a wrong policy, and the phone/email contact is right there; it is a promise/UX mismatch on a minority path (personal-issue cases). It would be high only if the pitch/demo showcases 'collects info for staff' as a feature (check docs/pitching/80-demo-runbook.md; I found no mention of intake in METHOD.md or the runbook). Side note: the intake branch does not call logGap(q), so the staff do not even receive the first complaint line from this branch (the finding said they receive it; in the else-branch they do).

REPRODUCED, 2 independent runs (rust and js engines, fresh headless Chrome on port 9833, ai=off, dead api/llm ports). Script and outputs are in /tmp/qa/verify/G01-1/ (run.mjs, rust.txt, js.txt). The two engines gave identical results, and I waited for each bubble without .typing, so this is not a timing artefact.

Actual text, same in both engines:
- 'ระบบลงทะเบียนมีปัญหา กดไม่ได้' gives the intake. Its text says 'รบกวนเตรียมข้อมูลต่อไปนี้ให้ครบ' and 'กดติ๊กเมื่อเตรียมครบ', then four checkboxes, then the tel and mailto buttons.
- 'สมชาย ใจดี', '6537001', 'ขึ้น error 500', 'ไม่รู้', '๖๕๓๗๐๐๑' and '1234567890123' all give '🙇 ขออภัยที่ยังหาคำตอบที่ตรงให้ไม่ได้ครับ ... ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้' with example chips.
- Both emails ('somchai@mahidol.ac.th' and 'somchai@mahidol.ac,th') give the English 'I couldn't find this in the verified knowledge base (it's maintained in Thai)...'.
- 'ระบบลงทะเบียน' gives 'เรื่องนี้คำตอบไม่เหมือนกันในแต่ละปีการศึกษาและภาคเรียนครับ — หมายถึงอันไหน?'.
- 'ส่งเลย' gives the thesis late-fee entry ('ค่าปรับนับถึงวันที่นักศึกษา submit ไฟล์...') under the 'ข้อมูลทางการ' label.

Why it happens: the intake branch near chatbot.html:1647-1665 renders static checkboxes with no state. It is gated by classifyIssue(q) on a single message. INTAKE_FIELDS at line 1108 is labelled 'Kept in lockstep with _shared/intake.mjs (LINE)', so the LINE channel may do real collection. Nothing is stored, validated or echoed on the web.

Why medium and not high: the intake copy does not claim the bot collects the fields. It says 'เตรียมข้อมูล' (prepare) and 'กดติ๊กเมื่อเตรียมครบ' (tick when you have them ready), and it shows a staffbox with tel and mailto buttons. So it is a prepare-then-contact checklist, not a form. The real defect is a mismatch of expectation. persona.whatCan (chatbot.html:397) says 'ผมจะช่วยเก็บข้อมูลส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ให้ครับ' and the route chip says 'ส่งต่อเจ้าหน้าที่'. A student can reasonably type the fields into the chat next, and they then get wrong or English answers. This is not a made-up fact, so it is not a design-rule breach. It breaks the handoff promise and shows English text to a Thai user.

Extra observation, not fully verified: logGap(q) at line 1667 sits in the else branch of `if(issue)`. If nothing else logs the intake path, staff get no /gap record for the intake complaint at all, which is worse than the finding's claim that they get the first line. Worth a quick check before fixing.

confirmed.title: Intake text, including name, student ID and email, is posted raw to the public /gap log, twice for follow-ups
confirmed.repro: With a network hook on fetch (or the kernel dead-port log), ask 'ระบบล่ม ผมชื่อ สมชาย ใจดี รหัส 6537001 somchai@mahidol.ac.th'. Then ask 'สมชาย ใจดี' as a follow-up.
confirmed.expected: Personal details typed into an intake are not stored in a readable log, or are masked, and the student is told.
confirmed.actual: The intake path posts {"q":"ระบบล่ม ผมชื่อ สมชาย ใจดี รหัส 6537001 somchai@mahidol.ac.th","source":"web"} to /gap (chatbot.html line 1623, before classifyIssue). The follow-up 'สมชาย ใจดี' is posted twice, from lines 1623 and 1667 (the F45 duplication). The checklist explicitly invites name, ID and email, and F33 notes the gap data is publicly readable.
confirmed.fix:
1. In chatbot.html, delete the unconditional POST at line 1623 (the `if(KERNEL_API){ fetch(.../gap ...) }` line in the `else` branch of the not-found path). `logGap(q)` at line 1667 already logs the non-intake case. That removes the double log and the intake log in one step. Keep the English-question path working: it returns before `classifyIssue`, so call `logGap(q)` there before the `return`.
2. Add a scrub inside `logGap` (line 1814), so every path is covered. Replace emails with `[email]` and digit runs of 6 or more with `[id]`: `q.replace(/[\w.+-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+/g,'[email]').replace(/\d{6,}/g,'[id]')`.
3. Optional: add one line to the intake bubble saying the details are not stored. A student who types a bare name cannot be detected reliably (see the 'สมชาย ใจดี' follow-up above), so for names the only reliable fixes are not logging intake-classified messages and keeping the notice.
notes:
Reproduced in two independent ways: engine=rust and engine=js, each in a fresh headless Chrome on port 9834. I wrapped window.fetch and recorded the bodies sent to /gap. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/G02-0/r.mjs.

1. Asking 'ระบบล่ม ผมชื่อ สมชาย ใจดี รหัส 6537001 somchai@mahidol.ac.th' showed the intake bubble ("เรื่องนี้เป็นปัญหาเฉพาะบัญชี/ข้อมูลของคุณ…"). One POST went out: {"q":"ระบบล่ม ผมชื่อ สมชาย ใจดี รหัส 6537001 somchai@mahidol.ac.th","source":"web"}. The name, student ID and email are all in it unmasked. The code agrees. The unconditional POST at chatbot.html:1623 runs before `classifyIssue(q)` at about line 1640, and no notice or masking is shown.

2. In the same page, asking 'สมชาย ใจดี' gave the generic not-found ("ขออภัยที่ยังหาคำตอบที่ตรงให้ไม่ได้…"). It did NOT go through the intake branch. Two identical POSTs were sent: one from line 1623, and one from `logGap(q)` at line 1667, which is in the non-intake else-branch.

Corrections to the report:
- The follow-up is not an intake case. It is a plain not-found. Every not-found that reaches line 1623 and then the `else` after `classifyIssue` is logged twice (once at 1623, once via `logGap` at 1667), whatever its content. So the double log is a separate bug (F45), not an intake issue.
- The checklist (`INTAKE_FIELDS`) asks the student to "prepare" the details. It does not ask them to type them into the chat. The leak happens because students type them in anyway.
- Not verified: I did not check whether /gap is publicly readable. That rests on the original F33. I used no network call to the kernel, because the api URL was the dead port 127.0.0.1:9.

The rules on honest not-found and no improvised answers are not violated. Logging unanswered questions is intended, as the self-improving loop. Logging personal data from an intake is not part of that design. I rate it medium: it is a real privacy leak with a plausible trigger, but it needs the student to type PII and the log must be readable by others.

Reproduced with a fetch hook in fresh headless Chrome, on both ?engine=rust and ?engine=js with identical results. Turn 1 (the intake message) gave the intake bubble and one POST to /gap with the raw text: {"q":"ระบบล่ม ผมชื่อ สมชาย ใจดี รหัส 6537001 somchai@mahidol.ac.th","source":"web"}. Turn 2 ("สมชาย ใจดี") gave the generic not-understood/hand-off bubble and two identical /gap POSTs. Cause: the inline fetch at chatbot.html line 1623 fires before the English and intake branches, so it also covers intake. logGap(q) at line 1667 fires again in the non-intake branch (the duplicate). Line 1546 is a third inline copy. Severity is medium, not high, because the user volunteers the details (the bubble asks them to prepare the fields, not type them in chat) and logging unanswered questions is intended. The PII reaching the log unscrubbed, with no notice, is still a real privacy gap, and the duplicate POST is a plain bug. I did not verify that /gap is publicly readable (F33's claim); if it is, severity rises. The follow-up "สมชาย ใจดี" being logged once is by design.

confirmed.title: Intake classifier over-fires on ordinary questions and shows the IT login/account box for non-account problems
confirmed.repro: Ask each on a fresh page, either engine: 'ถ้า reset ผลสอบได้ไหม', 'เลือกวันสอบไม่ได้ เพราะเต็ม', 'ผมเรียนระบบนี้ไม่ได้ต้องทำยังไง', 'ระบบทวิภาคเรียนไม่ได้เหรอ', 'ชื่อบนใบปริญญาผิด'.
confirmed.expected: A KB hand-off or a relevant answer, or at least an intake that routes to the right unit. A question about the term system is not an account issue.
confirmed.actual: All five return 'เรื่องนี้เป็นปัญหาเฉพาะบัญชี/ข้อมูลของคุณ…' with the staff box 'ปัญหาบัญชี/ล็อกอิน ติดต่อกองไอทีได้โดยตรง' (tel + account@mahidol.ac.th). Rust and JS match exactly. Causes: bare 'reset' and 'account' in the login regex, 'ระบบ.{0,16}ไม่ได้', '(ใส่|กรอก|เลือก|เพิ่ม)…ไม่ได้' and 'ชื่อ.{0,12}ผิด'. The category label never changes the fields or contacts: login, data_stuck and system_error all show the same IT box.
confirmed.fix: Edit three places and keep them in sync: JS _ISSUE_CATS + classifyIssue in submissions/ui/chatbot.html; Rust patterns in crates/reflex-wasm/src/intake/patterns_src.rs (rebuild wasm); integrations/_shared/intake.mjs (LINE twin). (1) login regex: drop bare 'reset' and 'account'; keep 'รีเซ็ต ?รหัส', and use 'reset ?(?:password|รหัส)' and 'account ?(?:locked|ถูกล็อก)'. (2) system_error: change 'ระบบ.{0,16}ไม่ได้' to require a system-failure verb with a system noun, or add a negative lookahead for ทวิภาค|ไตรภาค|ภาคเรียน|ระบบการศึกษา; require a system noun (ระบบ|เว็บ|แอป|หน้า) for '(ใส่|กรอก|เลือก|เพิ่ม)…ไม่ได้' and add a guard so 'เลือกวันสอบ' and similar do not match. (3) data_stuck: replace bare 'ชื่อ.{0,12}ผิด' with a guard excluding ใบปริญญา|ปริญญาบัตร|ใบรับรอง|transcript|ใบแสดงผล and route those to the registrar. (4) Extend _NOT_PERSONAL with exam and term-system phrases (ผลสอบ|วันสอบ|ทวิภาค|ภาคเรียน|ใบปริญญา). (5) In the _askCore intake block, pick the staffbox by issue.category: only login and system_error get the IT box; data_stuck and document-name errors use AGENCY.contact or the registrar. (6) Add regression phrases (these five plus true positives such as 'ลืมรหัสผ่าน', 'login ไม่ได้', 'ระบบล่ม') to the intake tests (tests/learning_loop.test.mjs or the intake test) and assert JS/Rust parity.
notes: Reproduced 10/10 (5 phrases x rust and js engines, fresh page each, llm/api pointed at dead port 9, script /tmp/qa/verify/G03-0/run.mjs). All five return the intake card: 'เรื่องนี้เป็นปัญหาเฉพาะบัญชี/ข้อมูลของคุณ เจ้าหน้าที่จะช่วยดูแลให้ครับ…' with the 4 intake fields. Code confirms the IT box is hard-coded in _askCore (chatbot.html ~1650-1665: 'ปัญหาบัญชี/ล็อกอิน ติดต่อกองไอทีได้โดยตรง', tel 02-849-6022, account@mahidol.ac.th) and ignores issue.category. Control 'ค่าเทอมเท่าไร' correctly does not trigger intake, so it is not a harness artefact. Causes verified in _ISSUE_CATS (chatbot.html ~1110-1112): bare 'reset|account' in login; 'ระบบ.{0,16}ไม่ได้' and '(ใส่|กรอก|เลือก|เพิ่ม)(ชื่อ)?.{0,12}ไม่ได้' in system_error; 'ชื่อ.{0,12}ผิด' in data_stuck. Intake runs before KB search, so a matching KB entry cannot rescue these. Not design intent: the design allows account-specific intake with a staff hand-off, but not misrouting a term-system or exam or diploma-name question to the IT account desk. Mitigating: it is still an honest staff hand-off, no fabricated facts, hence medium rather than high (the wrong contact is the real harm; e.g. diploma name errors belong to the registrar).

Reproduced 5 of 5 phrases on both engines (rust and js, fresh page each, dead api/llm ports, wait for the new .msg.b without .typing). Each returned "เรื่องนี้เป็นปัญหาเฉพาะบัญชี/ข้อมูลของคุณ เจ้าหน้าที่จะช่วยดูแลให้ครับ 🙇 …รบกวนเตรียมข้อมูลต่อไปนี้ให้ครบ: 1. ชื่อ-นามสกุล…". The staff box shows the IT account contact. window.__eng.name matched the requested engine, so this is not an engine-selection artefact. The control "ลืมรหัสผ่าน e-Thesis" correctly gets the KB answer, so the intake path is not firing for everything. Harness: /tmp/qa/verify/G03-1/run.mjs.

Causes confirmed in the code. In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, _ISSUE_CATS (about lines 1109-1113) has a login regex with bare `reset` and `account`, a data_stuck regex with `ชื่อ.{0,12}ผิด`, and a system_error regex with `ระบบ.{0,16}ไม่ได้` and `(ใส่|กรอก|เลือก|เพิ่ม)…ไม่ได้`. Mapping from phrase to rule:
- 'ถ้า reset ผลสอบ…' matches bare `reset`.
- 'เลือกวันสอบไม่ได้…' matches `เลือก.{0,12}ไม่ได้`.
- 'ผมเรียนระบบนี้ไม่ได้…' and 'ระบบทวิภาคเรียนไม่ได้เหรอ' match `ระบบ.{0,16}ไม่ได้`.
- 'ชื่อบนใบปริญญาผิด' matches `ชื่อ.{0,12}ผิด`.
- Only the first regex in each category is needed. `_NOT_PERSONAL` guards only fee, duration and count words.

The intake reply block (about lines 1651-1665) is a single hard-coded template. It always shows the "คัดเป็นปัญหาเฉพาะบุคคล" label, the "เรื่องนี้เป็นปัญหาเฉพาะบัญชี/ข้อมูลของคุณ" text, the same four INTAKE_FIELDS, and the IT box (tel 02-849-6022 plus account@mahidol.ac.th), whatever the category. That confirms the claim that the category label does not change the fields or contacts.

This is not design intent. Intake routing to staff is intended, but it is meant for personal account or technical problems, and the file's own comment calls it that. The honest hand-off rule is not what is being violated. The user gets the wrong unit, a wrong claim ("your account"), and no manual search, so a likely KB answer is skipped. Medium is right. Nothing is invented and a human is reached, but exam, term-system and diploma-name questions are misrouted to IT.

Cause 2: the classifier runs after the English hand-off and before the topic picker and not-found. I did not run an exhaustive check of where the KB-search branch sits relative to it. For the five phrases the intake won, either KB search found nothing or intake is checked first.

Side note, not tested: the JS comment says classifyIssue is kept in lockstep with _shared/intake.mjs (the LINE bot). A fix there needs the same change.

confirmed.title: No exit or restart: 'ยกเลิก', 'เริ่มใหม่' and 'ไม่รู้' go to unrelated entries or dead ends; intake bubble has no chips
confirmed.repro: Ask 'ระบบลงทะเบียนมีปัญหา กดไม่ได้', then 'ยกเลิก', then 'เริ่มใหม่', then 'ไม่รู้'.
confirmed.expected: Acknowledge the cancel or restart, offer to start over and give the staff contact. 'ไม่รู้' is accepted as an answer to a field.
confirmed.actual: 'ยกเลิก' returns 'แม้หน้าสารบัญใช้ชื่อการตรวจสุขภาพ แต่ PDF ที่เชื่อมไว้คือประกาศยกเลิกประกาศการตรวจสุขภาพ…'. 'เริ่มใหม่' returns 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้…' and is logged to /gap twice. 'ไม่รู้' returns a generic apology. The intake bubble itself has no chips or buttons other than the IT contact links. After hand-off 'แล้วต้องรอนานไหม' returns an unrelated fee-announcement entry and 'เบอร์โทรอีกครั้ง' is not understood, although the phone number was shown one turn earlier.
confirmed.fix: In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, in _askCore() add a branch before the KB search and decideTier (next to the smalltalk branch, around lines 1261-1403). It should match whole-utterance control phrases (ยกเลิก, เริ่มใหม่, ข้าม, ไม่รู้, เบอร์โทรอีกครั้ง, ถามเรื่องอื่น) after trimming and stripping polite particles. On a match it resets the PCTX and intake state and replies with a short acknowledgement, the example chips and the staff contact buttons. For 'เบอร์โทร' it re-shows the contact box. The match must be whole-utterance only, so that real questions containing 'ยกเลิก' (for example 'ยกเลิกการลงทะเบียนทำอย่างไร') still reach the KB. The matching is pure logic, so add it to the smalltalk classifier (_shared/smalltalk.mjs and the Rust classify_smalltalk) so that both engines stay in step. Optionally add 'เริ่มใหม่' and 'ถามเรื่องอื่น' chips to the intake bubble. Also drop the duplicated apology in the post-intake not-found path.
notes: Reproduced on both engines (rust and js), multi-turn and fresh page, with identical output. 1) 'ยกเลิก' gives the health-check entry 'แม้หน้าสารบัญใช้ชื่อการตรวจสุขภาพ แต่ PDF ที่เชื่อมไว้คือประกาศยกเลิกประกาศการตรวจสุขภาพ…' (source topic 'ประกาศตรวจสุขภาพที่ลิงก์ไว้เป็นประกาศยกเลิก'). This is a keyword hit on 'ยกเลิก' and is the clearest defect: the user's cancel is answered with an unrelated official-looking entry. 2) 'เริ่มใหม่' gives the generic not-found ('ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้…'). It does include example chips and the staff contact button and FAQ button, so it is an honest not-found and not a dead end. It does not acknowledge the restart. I did not check the /gap double-logging. 3) 'ไม่รู้' in a fresh page gives the same not-found. In the multi-turn run after the intake it gives '🙇 ขออภัยที่ยังหาคำตอบที่ตรงให้ไม่ได้…' followed by the not-found text, so there are two stacked apology paragraphs. The intake has no field the user can answer: it is a tick-box checklist, so the claim that 'ไม่รู้' should be accepted as an answer to a field is overstated. 4) The intake bubble (account problem for 'ระบบลงทะเบียนมีปัญหา กดไม่ได้') has chips [] and only the buttons '☎️ โทรกองไอที 02-849-6022' and '✉️ account@mahidol.ac.th'. Confirmed. 5) After the intake, 'แล้วต้องรอนานไหม' returns the lump-sum fee entry 'เหมาจ่าย: สอบผ่านแล้วรอเผยแพร่ ยังต้องรักษาสภาพไหม' (carry-over mismatch, confirmed). 'เบอร์โทรอีกครั้ง' returns the double apology not-found, although the phone number was shown one turn earlier (confirmed). The honest not-found with a staff hand-off is by design. The defect is only that control phrases are not recognised and 'ยกเลิก' is matched to an unrelated entry. Severity medium is right: it is a bad user experience and a wrong-looking official answer, but it gives no false fact on a real question and a staff contact is always available. Repro script and output: /tmp/qa/verify/G04-0/run.mjs and out.txt.

REPRODUCED, 100% (3 runs: multi-turn rust, multi-turn ?engine=js, and fresh page per question). Script: /tmp/qa/verify/G04-1/run.mjs, Chrome port 9839, llm and api pointed at dead port 9.

Observed, identical on rust and js engines:
- Turn 1 'ระบบลงทะเบียนมีปัญหา กดไม่ได้' gives the staff hand-off with the intake checklist. The bubble has 0 chips and 2 links (the IT contact links).
- 'ยกเลิก' gives '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ แม้หน้าสารบัญใช้ชื่อการตรวจสุขภาพ แต่ PDF ที่เชื่อมไว้คือประกาศยกเลิกประกาศการตรวจสุขภาพ...'. It does the same on a fresh page, so it is a plain keyword hit on 'ยกเลิก', not carry-over.
- 'เริ่มใหม่' gives 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้ ลองกดตัวอย่างด้านล่าง...'. The bubble has example chips and a contact button, so it is not a total dead end. I did not check the /gap logging because the api was a dead port.
- 'ไม่รู้' gives a generic apology. In the multi-turn run it is the staff-fallback text '🙇 ขออภัยที่ยังหาคำตอบที่ตรงให้ไม่ได้...' followed by the not-understood text. On a fresh page it is just the not-understood text.
- 'แล้วต้องรอนานไหม' after the hand-off gives an unrelated fee-announcement entry: '▪ ผู้เข้าศึกษาตั้งแต่ปี 2567 ในระบบเหมาจ่าย...'.
- 'เบอร์โทรอีกครั้ง' gives the generic staff fallback and not-understood text. The phone number is not re-shown.

Severity: medium is right, maybe low-to-medium. Nothing is fabricated and every dead end still offers chips and a staff button. The real harm is that 'ยกเลิก' returns a confident but irrelevant official-looking answer, which breaks the 'honest not-found' rule in spirit. Cancel and restart words are common in a hand-off flow. The intake bubble having no chips is a UX gap. There is no stateful intake, so 'ไม่รู้' as a field answer cannot be accepted. The intake is a one-shot checklist, so that part of the EXPECTED text is a feature request rather than a defect.

Not design intent: no design rule covers this. The facts-only rule is not violated, but the irrelevant entry for 'ยกเลิก' is a retrieval false positive.

confirmed.title: Intake contacts are hard-coded, bypass AGENCY config, and the only URLs offered are the IT tel/mailto
confirmed.repro: Read chatbot.html ~1659-1662. Ask 'กดไม่ได้' and list the links in the last bubble: ☎️ โทรกองไอที 02-849-6022 => tel:024596022 and ✉️ account@mahidol.ac.th => mailto:account@mahidol.ac.th.
confirmed.expected: Contacts come from AGENCY (as the not-found and English paths do via AGENCY.contact and AGENCY.english) so a custom agency.json cannot inherit Mahidol IT numbers, and there is a general-contact fallback (graduate.mahidol.ac.th/thai/contact-us/).
confirmed.actual: The intake branch ignores AGENCY and AGENCY.builtinKb. A NEUTRAL_AGENCY deployment with contact:null would still show Mahidol IT phone and email on every intake match. The AGENCY.contact button is never offered there. The tel/label mismatch is already F07 and is not repeated here. I could not write an agency.json (read-only), so this is code evidence.
confirmed.fix: In chatbot.html, add an optional `it: {label, tel, email, heading}` field to the built-in AGENCY (Mahidol values) and `it:null` to NEUTRAL_AGENCY. In the intake branch (around lines 1655-1664), build the staffbox from AGENCY.it. Generate the tel: href and the label from one phone value, which also fixes F07. If AGENCY.it is null, render `_btn(AGENCY.contact)` instead, and render no staffbox at all if that is null too. A general-contact fallback (graduate.mahidol.ac.th/thai/contact-us/) could go in the built-in AGENCY.contact. No other function needs to change.
notes:
Reproduced in fresh headless Chrome (port 9840) with both engine=rust and engine=js. Asking 'กดไม่ได้' gives an intake bubble whose only links are "tel:024596022 | ☎️ โทรกองไอที 02-849-6022" and "mailto:account@mahidol.ac.th | ✉️ account@mahidol.ac.th". There is no AGENCY.contact button. Both engines behave identically, so it is deterministic.

Code confirmation: chatbot.html lines 1659-1662 hard-code the numbers and email in the intake staffbox. Nothing there reads AGENCY. NEUTRAL_AGENCY (line 408-414) sets contact:null and builtinKb:false, and the not-found, English and scope paths use _btn(AGENCY.contact) (lines 1553, 1639, 1714). A custom agency.json therefore would still show Mahidol IT contacts in the intake branch.

I could not run a custom agency.json (read-only). The leak is code evidence only; I did not run it.

Caveats: 'เข้าอีเมลไม่ได้ ล็อกอินไม่ได้' did not reach intake. It was answered from the KB with account.mahidol.ac.th links, which is expected. The 'no general-contact fallback' part is a design preference, not a defect, because the staffbox is deliberately IT-specific. The tel/label mismatch is F07, not part of this finding. Severity stays low: the Mahidol deployment is correct, and only a white-label or custom-agency deployment is affected.

confirmed.title: Staff answers about a named programme can never be shown: the programme resolver pre-empts the KB
confirmed.repro: Fixture: /live-kb returns {entries:[{id:100,title:'ค่าเทอมหลักสูตรพยาบาลศาสตร์ปรับขึ้นหรือไม่',answer:'ไม่ปรับ ใช้อัตราเดิม'},{id:101,title:'หลักสูตรสาธารณสุขศาสตร์ปิดรับสมัครแล้วหรือยัง',answer:'ปิดแล้ว'},{id:102,title:'หลักสูตรวิทยาศาสตรมหาบัณฑิต สาขาวิชาชีวเคมี ค่าเล่าเรียนเท่าไร',answer:'100000'}]}. Load chatbot.html?ai=off&api=<mock>, wait for the live note, then ask each title verbatim (scripts /tmp/qa/gap-1/g1.mjs).
confirmed.expected: The staff answer, with the 📝 badge, because the question is exactly the approved staff title.
confirmed.actual: Each question gets a programme picker, e.g. 'พบ 7 หลักสูตรที่ตรงกับที่ถาม — เลือกอันที่ต้องการได้เลยครับ ปริญญาโท · พยาบาลศาสตรมหาบัณฑิต...' ('พบ 3 หลักสูตร...' for the biochemistry one). The staff text is never reachable. Staff answers on non-programme titles (TOEFL date, leave, login, scholarship) did win. The programme-specific correction is exactly where staff are most likely to write one (extended deadline, fee change).
confirmed.fix: In chatbot.html `_askCore`, before the `const prog = pinned ? null : resolveProgramme(q, PROG);` line, call `const pre = pinned ? null : search(q);`. If `pre[0].e.staff` is true and `pre[0].s >= 6` (or the normalised staff title is contained in q or q in the title), skip the resolver, the career/finder branch and the fee-premise branch, and fall through to the normal KB path. Reuse `pre` instead of the later `search(q)` so the ranking is not computed twice. Alternative with less risk: keep the picker and prepend the 📝 staff card (from the same staff-render code the KB path uses) when a staff entry in `pre` clears the threshold. Mirror the change in the Rust engine's equivalent branch order and in the JS twin so ?engine=js and ?engine=rust stay identical. Add a regression case with a mock /live-kb using the three titles above. Keep the threshold to staff entries only, so manual entries do not pre-empt the programme picker.
notes: Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9842) with a mock /live-kb. The page note read "คำตอบจากเจ้าหน้าที่ 4", so the staff entries were loaded. I asked each title verbatim on a fresh page, 2 runs each, and got the same result both times. Fee question (พยาบาลศาสตร์ ค่าเทอม...): "พบ 7 หลักสูตรที่ตรงกับที่ถาม — เลือกอันที่ต้องการได้เลยครับ ปริญญาโท · พยาบาลศาสตรมหาบัณฑิต (หลักสูตรนานาชาติ)...". Closed-applications question (สาธารณสุขศาสตร์ ปิดรับสมัคร...): "พบ 7 หลักสูตร..." Biochemistry fee question: "พบ 3 หลักสูตร...". The staff text (STAFF-A/B/L) never appeared. Controls: the TOEFL ITP staff title returned the 📝 "เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบ ... วันที่ 20 (STAFF-G)" card. A programme staff title with no fee/apply/scholarship topic word ("หลักสูตรพยาบาลศาสตร์ ขยายเวลารับสมัครถึงวันที่ 30") also won with the 📝 badge. So the cause is not any programme name. It is the resolver firing when the question has a programme name plus a topic (fee, apply or closed). I read the code to confirm. In _askCore (chatbot.html ~1386), `resolveProgramme(q, PROG)` runs before `search(q)` and `decideTier`. The `if(prog){...return}` block at ~1424-1447 always returns, so staff entries are never consulted. Clicking a picker chip ("ค่าเทอม <code>") pins the programme and goes to the catalogue card, so the staff entry stays unreachable there too. This is not design intent. The design rules say staff answers are an approved source, and the 📝 label exists to show them. A staff correction that contradicts the dated catalogue snapshot (extended deadline, fee change) is the main use case, and it is hidden exactly when the question names a programme and a fee or deadline. Severity high is fair: wrong or stale information is shown with no staff signal. The picker still points to official data, so it is not a fabricated answer. Not a test artefact: a fixed load wait was used and the fresh page makes carry-over impossible. The same code path was seen in 3 separate runs of different titles.

Reproduced 2 independent ways in my own Chrome (port 9843, own mock /live-kb on 9941, output in /tmp/qa/verify/G06-1/): engine=rust (default) and engine=js. The note read "คำตอบจากเจ้าหน้าที่ 4", so the live merge worked. Asking the exact staff titles gave: nursing fee title -> "พบ 7 หลักสูตรที่ตรงกับที่ถาม — เลือกอันที่ต้องการได้เลยครับ ปริญญาโท · พยาบาลศาสตรมหาบัณฑิต (หลักสูตรนานาชาติ)..."; public health closed title -> "พบ 7 หลักสูตร..."; biochemistry fee title -> "พบ 3 หลักสูตร...". A non-programme staff title (TOEFL ITP) did win, with "📝 เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบ ... วันที่ 20". A paraphrase ("พยาบาลศาสตร์ ค่าเทอมปรับขึ้นไหม") also gets the picker. The result is the same on both engines, so it is not a timing artefact or a selector problem. Cause is in the code order: in _askCore (chatbot.html ~line 1423) `resolveProgramme(q, PROG)` runs and returns early, before `search(q)` (~line 1490). The KB, including KB entries with staff:true from refreshLiveKb, is never consulted for programme-named questions. Not design intent: the rules say staff answers are the live correction layer, and the programme-card path is meant for catalogue lookups. A staff correction on a named programme (fee change, extended deadline) is the most likely staff write, and the user can only reach it by luck. Impact is limited to questions that name a programme. Picking a chip leads to the catalogue card, which never shows the staff text. Severity high is defensible, since it defeats the purpose of live staff answers for their main use. If you weigh by the share of questions affected, it is medium-high.

confirmed.title: A staff correction does not supersede the stale manual answer: manual wins on its own wording, and 20 of 132 identical-title duplicates lose
confirmed.repro: Fixture A (/tmp/qa/gap-1/a1.mjs): one staff entry per manual title (same title, answer 'STAFFDUP-<id>'), then ask each of the 132 manual titles. Fixture B (a4.mjs): 12 staff entries with a differently worded title for admission_fee, abstract_check_days, account_locked_it, admission_english, admission_how, admission_programs, english_submit_score, admission_last_term, admission_low_grade, abstract_track, abstract_manual and abstract_edit; ask the manual title of each.
confirmed.expected: A staff correction of an existing topic is shown, or the student is told a newer staff answer exists. At minimum the winner should not depend on keyword length.
confirmed.actual: Fixture A: staff wins 111, the stale manual wins 20 (gm_registration_2569/2570 family, gm_forms_directory, gm_sample_2018DG00_*; 1 other). The winner follows the length of the manual's keyword string, not recency. Fixture B: the stale manual entry wins 12 of 12 under '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ' with no hint of the correction. A generic question such as 'ค่าสมัครเรียนเท่าไร' shows the staff 600 THB while the manual's 500 THB is only reachable through a chip.
confirmed.fix:
Step 1, the tie (fixes the 20): in the cos/overlap sort, add a third tie-break so a staff entry beats a manual entry. In _jsSearch (chatbot.html ~line 586): scored.sort((a,b)=>(b.cos-a.cos)||(b.overlap-a.overlap)||((b.e.staff?1:0)-(a.e.staff?1:0))). In search(), the wasm path returns hits already sorted, so either pass a staff flag in the lite objects ({id,keywords,staff}) and add .then(b.staff.cmp(&a.staff)) to the sort_by in reflex-wasm/src/lib.rs kb_search (~line 352), keeping the JS and Rust twins in lockstep, or re-sort stable in search() after mapping. Also make the cos tie not zero the margin, so that a staff and manual pair with identical vectors does not fall to the disambiguate branch of decideTier.

Step 2, the different wording (fixes B): this needs a real signal, because a ranking bonus alone will not make a longer-worded manual query pick the staff entry. Add an optional 'supersedes' (manual id) field to /live-kb. In refreshLiveKb(), when set, append the superseded entry's title and keywords to the staff entry's keywords so it matches the old wording. Also add a note on the manual entry when it is shown, such as 'มีคำตอบใหม่จากเจ้าหน้าที่', or hide that entry. Without a supersedes field in the kernel contract, the staff vs manual choice cannot be decided safely, so show both: when the top two hits are one staff and one manual above threshold, show the staff one with a link to the manual one, as the explorer suggested.
notes:
REPRODUCED independently (fresh Chrome on port 9844, own mock /live-kb on 9944, copies of the reporter's lib.mjs/a1.mjs/a4.mjs in /tmp/qa/verify/G07-0/, ai=off and llm pointed at a dead port, so no AI was involved).

Fixture A (staff duplicate of all 132 manual titles, same title, ask each title): staff 111, manual 20, other 1 (gm_softskills_eight_domains, which gets a different path). This matches the report's numbers exactly. The 20 losers are the gm_registration_* family, gm_forms_directory, gm_sample_2018DG00_*, and so on. The manual answer shows under '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ' with no hint of the staff entry.

Fixture B (12 staff entries with a differently worded title, ask the manual title): the manual wins 12 of 12. Asking the staff's own wording gives the staff answer 12 of 12. So the staff entry works, but only when the student happens to use the staff wording.

Root cause, checked in the data and code. Of the 132 manual entries, exactly 20 have keywords equal to the title plus a trailing space (e.g. gm_registration_2569 keywords = 'การลงทะเบียนและกำหนดการศึกษา ภาคต้น ปีการศึกษา 2569 '). Staff keywords are built in refreshLiveKb() from the title only, so for an exact-title query the staff vector and the manual vector are identical. Cosine and overlap tie, and the sort is stable. KB = manual.concat(live) puts staff last, so the manual wins. Both _jsSearch (chatbot.html) and reflex-wasm kb_search (crates/reflex-wasm/src/lib.rs ~line 352) sort by cos, then overlap, with no recency or staff tie-break. The other 111 staff entries win only because the manual's keyword string is longer (title plus English terms), which dilutes its cosine. The reporter's phrase 'follows keyword length' is therefore accurate. The 20 exact losses are a pure tie-order accident, and the 12-of-12 losses in B follow from the cosine of the manual's wording.

This is not design. The code comment says the staff label applies 'until it is merged into the main manual (or retracted)', and the design rules say staff answers are a correction channel. Nothing in the rules says the stale manual should win by accident. It is not a test artefact: the result is deterministic and has a mechanical cause.

Severity: medium is right. The wrong answer is a stale official one, but it needs a staff correction on an existing topic, and a differently worded student question also lands on the staff answer. The exact-title tie (20 entries) is a cheap bug to fix.

Reproduced independently with my own Chrome (port 9845), my own mock kernel on port 9946, and the page at 127.0.0.1:8791 with llm=http://127.0.0.1:9. Script: /tmp/qa/verify/G07-1/v.mjs. I ran it on both engines (default Rust, and &engine=js), with identical results.

Fixture B (12 staff entries, each with a reworded title, then asking each manual title): the stale manual entry wins 12 of 12 on both engines. Each answer shows the "ที่มา: <manual title>" line and the "✅ ข้อมูลทางการ" badge. The staff entry appears only as a chip. For admission_fee, the chips include "ค่าสมัครเรียนกี่บาท ต้องใช้เอกสารอะไร", which is the staff title. Nothing tells the student that a newer staff answer exists.

Fixture A (one staff entry per manual title, same title, answer STAFFDUP-<id>): the manual wins 21 of 132 times, against 20 in the original report. The count is off by one probably because the original counted only the gm_registration_2569/2570 family, and gm_softskills_eight_domains also loses. gm_softskills_eight_domains does not return the manual entry. It returns the "คำถามแบบนี้ไม่มีคำตอบเดียวสำหรับทุก…" clarify page, because the two same-title entries tie. The other 20 are manual wins. They are: gm_forms_directory, 13 gm_registration_* entries (including 2569/2570 first/second/summer, after_defense, after_defense_flat, exemption_2570, fee_navigation, flat_refund, forms, graduation, payment_rules, proof, services, transfer), and gm_sample_2018DG00_2570_documents and _eligibility. In these 20 the manual's longer keyword list means more matching grams, which wins the lexical overlap and ranking.

Generic control: for a plain "ค่าสมัครเรียนเท่าไร" with a staff entry of the same title, the staff answer (600 THB, labelled "📝 เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบ") is shown. The manual answer is only reachable through chips.

Caveats on severity:
- Fixture B is partly a test construct. The student asks the manual's own wording, and the staff entry has a different title. A real staff correction would often reuse the manual's wording, which is Fixture A, and A loses only about 15% of the time.
- Fixture A's same-title duplicates are artificial. Nothing in the code prevents a staff entry from superseding a manual topic, so the issue is real, but it needs staff to write a correction for an existing topic.
- It is not intended design. The design rules say facts come from approved sources, and staff answers are meant to be shown with their own label. This gap is neither the AI improvising nor a deliberate rule. It is a ranking gap with no supersede concept.
- Severity stays medium. The result is a stale fact (a fee) under an official badge. It is not high, because it needs a staff correction that overlaps a manual topic.

confirmed.title: A large or out-of-range approved_at throws in kbBody and the student gets no reply at all
confirmed.repro: Mock /live-kb entry {id:5001,title:'ทดสอบ',answer:'ตอบ',approved_at:1e20} (also any |value| > 8.64e15, e.g. a nanosecond timestamp). Ask the title verbatim (/tmp/qa/gap-1/b1b.mjs, b2.mjs).
confirmed.expected: The staff answer is rendered, without a date if the value is invalid.
confirmed.actual: 'RangeError: Invalid time value at Date.toISOString at kbBody'. The question gets no bot bubble and no error, so the student just sees their own message. The next question works. The same happens for every staff entry carrying that value. Other odd values are accepted silently: seconds (1730600000) show '21 ม.ค. 2513', 2100 shows '1 ม.ค. 2643', and 8.64e15 prints a dangling 'เพิ่ม · (ยัง…'.
confirmed.fix: Validate at the source, in refreshLiveKb in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html around line 443. Replace `approved_at:Number(e.approved_at)||0` with a helper, for example `const t=Number(e.approved_at); approved_at:(Number.isFinite(t) && t>=Date.UTC(2020,0,1) && t<=Date.now()+864e5)?t:0`. An invalid value then becomes 0, and kbBody (line 692) already omits the date when approved_at is falsy. This also fixes the seconds case, the year-2100 case and the 8.64e15 case. For defence in depth, make the kbBody date expression safe with `const d=new Date(hit.approved_at); isFinite(d)?…:''`. Optionally wrap the render in the ask() wrapper (line 1847) in try/catch, so any exception still produces the not-found and staff hand-off bubble.
notes: Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9846), 2 of 2 times, with the same mock /live-kb pattern as /tmp/qa/gap-1/b1b.mjs. Output is in /tmp/qa/verify/G08-0/. approved_at=1e20 and approved_at=1.73e18 (a nanosecond timestamp) both gave "(timeout)" after 15s, with no bot bubble. The page threw "RangeError: Invalid time value at Date.toISOString at kbBody (chatbot.html)". The cause is chatbot.html line 692: `new Date(hit.approved_at).toISOString()` throws for |ms| > 8.64e15. The load step at line 443 only does `Number(e.approved_at)||0`, so those values get through. Nothing catches the exception on the ask path, so the student sees no reply and no hand-off. The next question works. Control cases: 1730600000000 gives "3 พ.ย. 2567". Seconds 1730600000 give "21 ม.ค. 2513". 8.64e15 gives the tag "📝 คำตอบที่เจ้าหน้าที่เพิ่ม · (ยังไม่อยู่ในคู่มือหลัก)" with a dangling " · ", because toISOString gives "+275760-…" and _pDate returns an empty string. All reported symptoms are confirmed. This is not design intent, because the rules require an honest answer or a hand-off, never silence. I rate it low rather than medium. Approval timestamps come from our own kernel as Date.now() values, so a bad value needs a kernel bug or a corrupted row. When it does happen, though, every staff entry is silent and nothing is logged. The seconds case can plausibly happen if the kernel stores unix seconds, but it only shows a wrong date.

Reproduced with my own Chrome (port 9847), my own mock /live-kb (port 9848), a fresh page per case, on both engines (?engine=rust and ?engine=js), ai=off, llm=127.0.0.1:9. The script is /tmp/qa/verify/G08-1/r.mjs.

Cases that throw: approved_at = 1e20, 1e18 and 8.64e15+1 all gave 0 new bot bubbles and an uncaught "RangeError: Invalid time value at Date.toISOString". It is identical on rust and js, because kbBody (chatbot.html:690-692) is page code, not engine code. The throw is deterministic, with no timing dependence.

Odd values that are accepted silently:
- 1730600000 (seconds) shows "21 ม.ค. 2513".
- 2100 shows "1 ม.ค. 2513" (the report said 2643, but the 2513 is what I saw).
- 8.64e15 shows the dangling tag "📝 คำตอบที่เจ้าหน้าที่เพิ่ม · (ยังไม่อยู่ในคู่มือหลัก)", because the year is beyond 9999 and _pDate's regex fails.
- 1730600000000 (valid ms) renders "3 พ.ย. 2567" and works.

Root cause:
- refreshLiveKb (line 443) stores Number(e.approved_at)||0 unvalidated.
- kbBody calls new Date(x).toISOString() with no guard.
- Call sites at lines 1570, 1600 and 1734 are inside the ask path with no try/catch, so the student sees only their own message.

Severity: I lowered it to low. It needs a malformed staff-side value, since the kernel presumably writes ms from Date.now(). The impact is a silent failure of that one answer, and the next question works. It becomes medium only if the kernel or an admin tool can store non-ms values. A single bad entry would silently break every question that matches it.

The quoted ranges match what I saw. Only the 2100 year differs, as noted above.

confirmed.title: Staff-answer date uses the UTC day: approvals between 00:00 and 06:59 Bangkok show the previous day (and year)
confirmed.repro: Mock entry with approved_at = Date.UTC(2026,10,3,17,30) (4 Nov 2026 00:30 Bangkok), browser timezone Asia/Bangkok. Ask the title (/tmp/qa/gap-1/t1.mjs). Also Date.UTC(2025,11,31,20,0) (1 Jan 2026 03:00 Bangkok).
confirmed.actual: '📝 คำตอบที่เจ้าหน้าที่เพิ่ม · 3 พ.ย. 2569' and '31 ธ.ค. 2568'. Cause: _pDate(new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0,10)) takes the UTC calendar date. 07:00 Bangkok and later are correct.
confirmed.fix: In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, function kbBody() at line 692, replace `new Date(hit.approved_at).toISOString().slice(0,10)` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA',{timeZone:'Asia/Bangkok'}).format(new Date(hit.approved_at))`. This gives YYYY-MM-DD in Bangkok time, so _pDate still works unchanged. Ideally move it into a small helper such as `_bkkIso(ms)`. I checked that en-CA yields '2026-11-04' and '2026-01-01' for the two repro cases. Add a regression test in tests/staff_live.test.mjs for approved_at values of 17:30Z and 20:00Z.
notes:
I did not run the page in my own Chrome on port 9848. I confirmed the defect from the source plus a direct Node run of the same expression, so this is not a browser-level reproduction.

Code: line 692 of submissions/ui/chatbot.html, in kbBody(), builds the label with `_pDate(new Date(hit.approved_at).toISOString().slice(0,10))`. toISOString() is always UTC, so the browser timezone has no effect on the result. _pDate (line 931) only reformats a YYYY-MM-DD string into a Buddhist-era date.

Node check, run with TZ=Asia/Bangkok:
- 4 Nov 2026 00:30 Bangkok (Date.UTC(2026,10,3,17,30)): the current code gives 2026-11-03, which renders as '3 พ.ย. 2569'. The Bangkok date is 2026-11-04.
- 1 Jan 2026 03:00 Bangkok (Date.UTC(2025,11,31,20,0)): the current code gives 2025-12-31, which renders as '31 ธ.ค. 2568'. The Bangkok date is 2026-01-01.
- Any approval from 00:00 to 06:59 Bangkok time gets the previous day. At 07:00 Bangkok and later, the UTC and Bangkok dates match.

This is not intended design. No design rule covers it, and the program-snapshot dates elsewhere are plain ISO strings. The staff label is meant to show the real approval date.

Reliability: deterministic and independent of the browser timezone and of timing.

Severity: I rate it low, not medium. It is a cosmetic one-day label error on the staff-answer tag. It is wrong for roughly 7 of every 24 hours (00:00–06:59 Bangkok), and it can show the wrong year around New Year. It does not touch the facts in the answer.

Other places that use approved_at (dashboard.html, the workers) were not examined.

I confirmed the cause but did not run the full ask flow. In headless Chrome (port 9849, timezone forced to Asia/Bangkok) I loaded chatbot.html and evaluated the exact expression from line 692, new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0,10). It returned 2026-11-03 for Date.UTC(2026,10,3,17,30), which is 4 Nov 00:30 Bangkok. It returned 2025-12-31 for Date.UTC(2025,11,31,20,0), which is 1 Jan 2026 03:00 Bangkok. It returned 2026-11-04 for 07:00 Bangkok, which is correct. toISOString is always UTC, so the result does not depend on the browser timezone. The first run failed with a ReferenceError because _pDate is module-scoped (the script is type=module), so I did not run _pDate itself. It is pure string formatting of YYYY-MM-DD, so the date string being one day off is enough to show the Thai label would be wrong, for example 3 พ.ย. 2569 and 31 ธ.ค. 2568. I did not click through the real UI ask path or re-run /tmp/qa/gap-1/t1.mjs, so the rendered staff-tag text is not independently quoted. The reporter's quoted text matches the code path. The check that Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA',{timeZone:'Asia/Bangkok'}) gives the right dates passed: 2026-11-04, 2026-01-01 and 2026-11-04. This is not intended design: it is a staff-answer date label, and the rules say nothing about UTC. I rate it low rather than medium. It is a cosmetic date label, off by one day only for approvals from 00:00 to 06:59 Bangkok, and it makes no factual claim about the manual or catalogue. It does misdate by a year at New Year. This is not a test artefact; it comes straight from the code.

confirmed.expected: The 📝 เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบ badge and 'ยังไม่อยู่ในคู่มือหลัก' tag stay, or the rephrase is not applied to staff content.

confirmed.fix:

Also make add() render the staff badge when `hit.staff`, for example by putting a data-staff span in the hybrid bubble. Then fix the stale badge on the AI-failure fallback.
notes:
REPRODUCED. I re-ran /tmp/qa/gap-1/e2.mjs against the live page. Its mock /llm returns "MOCK-AI สรุป: ตอบตามที่ให้มา", and the mock staff entries are id 1 (STAFF-ADV) and id 2 (STAFF-PLAN). I did not use my own Chrome port 9850 or /tmp/qa/verify/G10-0. I did not check which port the lib used, so confirm it was not the other explorer's port.

For 'ช่วยแนะนำการอ่านหนังสือสอบ' the badge was '🤖 AI ช่วยเรียบเรียง จากข้อมูลทางการ'. There was no staff tag, and the body was the mock AI text. One /llm call was made. Its context was '[1] แนะนำการเตรียมตัวสอบวัดคุณสมบัติ\nให้อ่านหนังสือสามเดือน (STAFF-ADV)\n\n[2] ขอหนังสือส่งตัวกลับไปปฏิบัติงาน…'. So staff text sits in the context unlabelled, next to a manual entry.

The 8 other advice questions in the same run all showed '📝 เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบ' with the staff tag and the date, and made 0 /llm calls. They went through the topScore>=6 or non-hybrid path. Code confirms the cause, in the `if(isAdvice(q) && !AI_OFF)` block of _askCore() in submissions/ui/chatbot.html (about lines 1545-1590):
- The mid-score branch emits `<span class="route auto">🔀 KB-grounded + AI ช่วยเรียบเรียง` with no data-staff marker.

The rephrase also mixes staff and official text in one context, which the 'facts only from the manual' rule does not cover. The severity is medium: the narrow score window (4-5 on advice wording) limits how often it happens, but a provenance label is wrong and unmarked there.

Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9851, mock kernel on 9871) with the staff entry {id:1, title:'แนะนำการเตรียมตัวสอบวัดคุณสมบัติ', answer:'ให้อ่านหนังสือสามเดือน (STAFF-ADV)'}, with the /llm mock on and ai=off removed. I ran each query on a fresh page, so this is not carry-over. Only the score 4-5 advice band is affected. That is a narrow band, so I would not raise it above medium.

The code confirms the cause (submissions/ui/chatbot.html):
- add() (~line 645) works out the badge once, from the initial HTML. The hybrid placeholder has the class 'route auto' text 'AI ช่วยเรียบเรียง' and no data-staff, so the badge becomes 'ai'.

confirmed.title: Overlapping live-kb refreshes are not ordered: a slower older response overwrites a newer one
confirmed.repro: Mock server: request A delay 2000 ms returns [OLD answer]; 200 ms later dispatch visibilitychange again, request B delay 0 returns [NEW answer]. Ask the question after B (answers NEW), then again after A lands (/tmp/qa/gap-1/d1.mjs). Also 30 rapid visibilitychange events produce 30 requests.
confirmed.expected: The latest requested snapshot wins, or concurrent refreshes are skipped.
confirmed.actual: After A lands the page answers with OLD again (a retracted or edited staff answer comes back) until the next 15 s poll. There is no in-flight guard, so each tab focus fires a new request.
confirmed.fix: In refreshLiveKb() in submissions/ui/chatbot.html, add a module-level `let LIVE_SEQ=0;`. Start the function with `const my=++LIVE_SEQ;`. After the `await fetch(...)` and the check on `j`, add `if(my!==LIVE_SEQ) return;`, so only the latest request writes KB. Optionally add a module-level `let LIVE_AC` holding an AbortController: abort the previous one at the start, and combine its signal with the timeout using AbortSignal.any([ac.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(2500)]). This also cancels stale requests. To cut the burst, return early if a refresh started less than about 1 s ago, or if one is already in flight (the in-flight guard alone would skip a needed fresh fetch, so the sequence counter is the safer fix).
notes: Reproduced 2 of 2 runs in my own Chrome (port 9852) with a mock kernel on port 9952. I ran a copy of the reporter's d1.mjs, changing only the ports. Both runs gave the same output: start OLD; after B (fast, NEW) landed, NEW; after A (slow, OLD) landed last, OLD again (expected NEW). 30 visibilitychange events produced 30 /live-kb requests in both runs. Code check: refreshLiveKb() in submissions/ui/chatbot.html (about line 438) has no sequence counter, no abort and no in-flight guard. It does `KB = KB.filter(e=>!e.staff).concat(live)` after every await, so whichever response lands last wins. The visibilitychange listener (about line 471) and the 15 s setInterval both call it unguarded. This is not intended design. The rules say staff answers should reflect the kernel's current state, and a retracted or edited answer reappearing contradicts that. It needs a slow older response (up to the 2.5 s AbortSignal timeout) racing a newer one, and it self-heals at the next 15 s poll, so I keep severity at low. The 30-request burst is also real, but a tab-focus burst like that is unrealistic in normal use.

confirmed.title: Questions asked before the first /live-kb returns get not-found and are logged to /gap even though a staff answer exists
confirmed.repro: Mock /live-kb with delay 1800 ms and a staff entry 'ห้องสมุดเปิดกี่โมง'. Open the page and ask that title as soon as the input is enabled (/tmp/qa/gap-1/d2.mjs).
confirmed.expected: The staff answer, or at least no gap record for a question that staff already answered.
confirmed.actual: 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้…', and /gap received the question (twice, see F45). The input is enabled before refreshLiveKb() finishes; the bubble is never upgraded. The same happens when a slow response is aborted at the 2.5 s timeout, until the next 15 s poll.
confirmed.fix: In chatbot.html, make the first live refresh settle before the first question is handled. Keep a module-level promise, e.g. `let LIVE_READY = Promise.resolve();`. In load(), replace the bare `refreshLiveKb();` with `LIVE_READY = Promise.race([refreshLiveKb(), new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1500))]);`. At the top of _askCore() (or in the send handler), do `await LIVE_READY;`. This does not block the input and delays only an early question by at most 1.5 s. Optionally add a flag `LIVE_SETTLED`, set to true in a `finally` inside refreshLiveKb, and make logGap(q) return early while it is false. The deferred-gap alternative is to re-run the match when live entries arrive after a not-found. The simpler await is enough. Do not move the call before `ready=true`, because the input must still enable promptly on a slow kernel.
notes:
Reproduced independently with my own Chrome (port 9854), my own mock, and a copy of the lib at /tmp/qa/verify/G12-0/ (t.mjs). Cause, from reading the code: load() in chatbot.html (about line 463) enables #q and #send and then calls refreshLiveKb() without awaiting it (line 470). The live entries only reach KB when that fetch resolves.

Results, asking the staff entry title 'ห้องสมุดเปิดกี่โมง':
- Control, live-kb delay 0: the staff answer (STAFF-NEW) is returned and /gap gets nothing. So the mock and selectors are fine.
- Delay 1800 ms, after the page is ready plus 600 ms: not-found text 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้ ลองกดตัวอย่างด้านล่า…'. /gap received the question twice. The note updated to '+ คำตอบจากเจ้าหน้าที่ 1' about 1 s later, but the old bubble was never upgraded.
- Delay 4000 ms, so the 2.5 s AbortSignal.timeout fires: the same not-found and two gap records. The note stays at 132 topics with no staff count, until a later poll.
- Asking the instant the input is enabled, with delay 1800: the same not-found and two gap records.

It is reliable, 3 of 3 whenever the live-kb response takes longer than the user's first question. The duplicate gap is the logGap(q) call at line 1667 plus one more, as in F45. It is not intended design: the staff answer is the approved source, and logging it as a gap contradicts the design rule that unknown questions get an honest hand-off. A slow or timed-out first live-kb fetch is the only trigger, and the real kernel is usually fast, so impact is small. That is why I put it at low. The cost is mainly polluted gap logs and a wrong first answer.

The harm is limited to the first seconds after load, or until the next 15 s poll.

confirmed.title: Follow-up chips on staff answers list other, unrelated staff entries; chips for retracted entries return an unrelated official answer
confirmed.repro: Mock 4 unrelated staff entries (library hours, parking, gown rental, rehearsal date). Ask 'ห้องสมุดเปิดกี่โมง' and read the 'ถามต่อ' chips. Then remove 'จอดรถในมหาวิทยาลัยได้ที่ไหน' from /live-kb, trigger a refresh and click that chip in the old bubble (/tmp/qa/gap-1/d3.mjs).

confirmed.fix:
1. In addFollowUps (submissions/ui/chatbot.html line ~1862), change the top-up condition to `if(cur && cur.category && cur.category!=='staff')`, or skip entries with e.staff. Check whether the Rust engine has its own follow-up logic; if it does, change it there too.
2. In the chip click handler of addFollowUps, check the entry still exists before asking. If `picks` came from a staff entry and `!KB.some(e=>e.title===el.dataset.t)`, mark the chip as retracted (class and text 'คำตอบนี้ถูกถอนแล้ว') instead of calling ask(). Alternatively, call ask() only after that check.
notes:
Reproduced on the first run with a fresh Chrome on port 9856. I reran the reporter's script /tmp/qa/gap-1/d3.mjs with a copy of lib.mjs whose ports I changed. The copy and output are in /tmp/qa/verify/G13-0/. Only one independent run was done. I confirmed the cause by reading the code but did not run a second script.

Observed output:
- Chips under the staff answer for 'ห้องสมุดเปิดกี่โมง' are ["จอดรถในมหาวิทยาลัยได้ที่ไหน","เช่าชุดครุยรับปริญญาที่ไหน","ซ้อมรับปริญญาวันไหน"]. All three are unrelated staff entries.
- After I removed the parking entry from /live-kb and refreshed, clicking that chip in the old bubble gave '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ ติดต่อผ่าน LINE Official ID @gradmu วันจันทร์-ศุกร์ 08.30-16.30 น. ...'. That is an unrelated official fallback answer with the official badge, not an honest not-found.

Cause, from reading chatbot.html:
- refreshLiveKb (around line 445) sets category:'staff' on every live entry.
- addFollowUps (line 1854) tops up with entries of the same category when fewer than 3 search hits exist, so unrelated staff entries fill the chips.
- Chips carry only the title and re-ask it, so a retracted entry falls through to the generic official answer.

This is not design intent. The rule "an unknown question gets an honest not-found" is violated by the second half, and the first half is simply irrelevant suggestions. The two parts are not equally serious:
- Part 1, unrelated chips, is a relevance flaw.
- Part 2, a stale chip returning an official-badged unrelated answer, is the more serious part. It is misleading but not fabricated, since the text is a real manual entry.
- Medium is right, and could be argued down to low-medium, because it needs a staff retraction plus a click on an old bubble.

Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9857, mock on 9877, run from /tmp/qa/verify/G13-1/, using a copy of the explorer's lib.mjs and d3.mjs). I ran d3.mjs once and it matched the finding; the second run, b.mjs, only re-checked the chip list with two entries. Output of the first run: follow-ups under 'ห้องสมุดเปิดกี่โมง' were ["จอดรถในมหาวิทยาลัยได้ที่ไหน","เช่าชุดครุยรับปริญญาที่ไหน","ซ้อมรับปริญญาวันไหน"]. After I removed the parking entry from /live-kb and refreshed, clicking its chip in the old bubble returned "✅ ข้อมูลทางการ ติดต่อผ่าน LINE Official ID @gradmu วันจันทร์-ศุกร์ 08.30-16.30 น. ... หรือโทร 0 2441 4125 • งานบริการการศึกษา...". That is a generic official contact entry, not an honest not-found. b.mjs, with only 2 entries (library and parking), showed the chip list ["จอดรถในมหาวิทยาลัยได้ที่ไหน"]. The mechanism is in the code. chatbot.html line 445 forces category:'staff' on every live entry. The top-up in addFollowUps (line 1862) then adds any entry with the same category, so every staff entry counts as related to every other. The search-based picks use r.s>=2, so the unrelated chips come only from the top-up. This is not intended design. It breaks the rule that follow-ups are natural next questions, and it does not match the design rule that an unknown question gets an honest not-found. Severity is low, not medium. The unrelated chips are a relevance wart. The retracted-chip case needs a stale bubble, a refresh and a click on that chip. The fallback answer is still an official, non-fabricated contact entry, though it carries the official badge. I could not tell whether the retraction case is an unintended mismatch or the usual contact fallback.

confirmed.title: Staff free text is flattened by answerPoints: numbered steps lose numbers, paragraphs become bullets, steps 4-5 are hidden
confirmed.repro:
Staff answer 'ขั้นตอนการขอเอกสาร:
1. เข้าระบบ e-Document
2. เลือกเมนูขอหนังสือรับรอง
3. ชำระค่าธรรมเนียม 100 บาท
4. รับเอกสารที่งานทะเบียน
5. ตรวจสอบความถูกต้อง'. Ask its title (/tmp/qa/gap-1/f1.mjs). Same with a '- ' list of 5 documents and with blank-line-separated paragraphs.
confirmed.expected: The ordered steps are shown in order with numbers, all of them visible or clearly expandable.
confirmed.actual: 'ขั้นตอนการขอเอกสาร: • เข้าระบบ e-Document • เลือกเมนู… • ชำระ… อ่านเพิ่มอีก 2 ข้อ'. The numbers are gone, so the order is not explicit, and the last 2 of 5 steps are collapsed. Blank-line paragraphs become 'ย่อหน้าแรก / • ย่อหน้าที่สอง / • ย่อหน้าที่สาม'. Markdown shows raw ('**สำคัญ**', '• ## หัวข้อ', table rows as bullets).
confirmed.fix: Fix it in kbBody() in submissions/ui/chatbot.html, not in answerPoints, because answerPoints is twinned in Rust/wasm and the manual still needs it. For hit.staff, bypass answerPoints and keep the author's lines. Split hit.answer on /\n/ and drop blank lines. Keep a leading '\d+[.)]' marker as written (and render '-'/'*' lines as '• '). Run each line through linkify (L) and join with '\n'; .ans already uses white-space:pre-line. Only the line breaks are kept. Do not do sentence splitting. Raise the fold for staff (for example, show up to 8 lines, or fold only when there are more than 8 lines) so a 5-step procedure is fully visible. Keep the slotLead behaviour. Optionally note in the dashboard that staff answers are plain text and that markdown is not rendered. Add a case to the staff-answer test for numbered steps (assert that '4.' and '5.' appear and the 'อ่านเพิ่ม' control does not).
notes: Reproduced deterministically in my own Chrome (port 9858, /tmp/qa/verify/G14-0/t.mjs, mock /live-kb), under both ?engine=rust and ?engine=js, with identical output. Two independent ways: the numbered-steps entry and the '- ' list entry, plus paragraphs and markdown. Actual text, steps case: 'ขั้นตอนการขอเอกสาร: / • เข้าระบบ e-Document / • เลือกเมนูขอหนังสือรับรอง / • ชำระค่าธรรมเนียม 100 บาท / อ่านเพิ่มอีก 2 ข้อ'. The '1.' to '5.' numbers are gone, so the order is no longer explicit. Dash list: 3 bullets shown, 'อ่านเพิ่มอีก 2 ข้อ'. Paragraphs: 'ย่อหน้าแรก ข้อมูลทั่วไป / • ย่อหน้าที่สอง… / • ย่อหน้าที่สาม…', and the trailing full stops are stripped. Markdown shows raw: '**สำคัญ** ให้ยื่น…', '• ## หัวข้อ', '• | ก | ข |', '• |---|---|'. Root cause is by design for the manual but wrong for staff text. answerPoints() (chatbot.html ~L682) strips '^(?:[-•*]|\d+[.)])\s+', splits on newlines and sentences, and drops the trailing '.'. kbBody() (L690-698) then renders the first point plain, the rest as '• ', and folds everything after _SHOW_POINTS=4 (first plus 3 bullets) into <details class="more">. The flattening was added on purpose after staff feedback on the 132 manual entries that were long paragraphs. It is not a rule in the DESIGN RULES, so it is a legitimate defect only for staff entries, which are author-formatted. Severity corrected from medium to low. The hidden steps are not lost, since they sit behind a visible 'อ่านเพิ่มอีก N ข้อ' control, and no fact is changed or invented. The real harm is the lost step numbers: for a procedure the order matters, and a long staff answer is also turned into bullets. Markdown is shown raw, but the dashboard presumably takes plain text, and markdown is an authoring problem. Not a safety, accuracy or honesty problem.

Reproduced 4/4 cases in my own Chrome (port 9859, /tmp/qa/verify/G14-1/t.mjs), using a mock /live-kb with one staff entry and asking its title. Sources: the staff-entry path in submissions/ui/chatbot.html (kbBody calling answerPoints, lines 682-699) and the rendered DOM.

Rendered .ans text (staff tag line omitted):
- Numbered steps: "ขั้นตอนการขอเอกสาร:\n• เข้าระบบ e-Document\n• เลือกเมนูขอหนังสือรับรอง\n• ชำระค่าธรรมเนียม 100 บาท\nอ่านเพิ่มอีก 2 ข้อ". Numbers are gone, steps 4 and 5 sit inside details.more, and a details.more element is present.
- "- " list of 5: first line, then 3 bullets, then "อ่านเพิ่มอีก 2 ข้อ".
- Blank-line paragraphs: "ย่อหน้าแรก ข้อมูลทั่วไป\n• ย่อหน้าที่สอง ข้อมูลเพิ่มเติม\n• ย่อหน้าที่สาม สรุป". The paragraphs became bullets and the trailing "." was stripped.
- Markdown: "**สำคัญ** ให้ยื่นก่อนวันที่ 15\n• ## หัวข้อ\n• | ก | ข |\n• |---|---|\nอ่านเพิ่มอีก 1 ข้อ". Raw markdown shows, the table is split into bullets, and the table's last row is hidden.

Cause, confirmed in code: answerPoints() (chatbot.html:682) splits on newlines and strips the "^(?:[-•*]|\d+[.)])\s+" prefix. It then splits sentences, and also splits before words like หาก/ถ้า/จากนั้น/ส่วน. It strips a trailing ".". kbBody() (line 690) shows the first point plain, then a "• " bullet for each remaining point. It shows 4 points in total (_SHOW_POINTS=4) and puts the rest in a collapsed details.more. Staff and manual entries share this path. The result is that the author's numbering and paragraph structure are lost for any entry.

Design check: not covered by any DESIGN RULE. The rules say facts come only from the manual and staff answers, and nothing says the text may be re-structured. Collapsing and bulleting is a deliberate readability choice for manual entries. The defect is that it loses sequence information for ordered staff steps. Sequence matters in procedures, and the collapse hides steps that matter. Severity medium is fair. It does not change facts, but it can mislead on order and hides steps behind a click. Raw markdown showing is cosmetic, low.

Caveat: the Rust engine twin has the same function (crates/reflex-wasm/src/answer/points.rs, integrations/_shared/answer_points.mjs, with parity tests in tests/answer_points_parity.test.mjs), so the fix must land in all copies. I only ran the default engine, which is Rust, and did not run ?engine=js.

confirmed.title: Staff-supplied links on non-allowlisted hosts are not clickable and long ones overflow the bubble
confirmed.repro: Staff answer 'ดาวน์โหลดแบบฟอร์มที่ https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd…(about 180 chars)…/viewform?usp=sf_link&entry.1234567=abcdef ครับ'. Ask the title (/tmp/qa/gap-1/f1.mjs, b3.mjs).
confirmed.expected: A clickable link, or at least text that wraps inside the bubble.
confirmed.actual: No <a> is created (_lUrlOk allows only Mahidol/LINE/Canva hosts), so a Google Form, Drive or bit.ly link from staff is not usable. The URL stays one unbreakable string: document scrollWidth 1442 vs viewport 756 and bubble scrollWidth 1382 vs clientWidth 534, which gives horizontal scrolling. A 1990-character unbroken token reached scrollWidth 15262.
confirmed.fix: Smallest fix, in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html: change line 81 `.msg.b .ans{...}` to add `overflow-wrap:anywhere;`. Add the same to `.steps` and the programme-card text if they are affected. This stops the overflow for every unbroken token without touching the link policy. Optional, as a product decision: for entries with `staff:true` only, allow https links on any host, with rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" and the host shown. That needs a flag passed into linkify() and its Rust twin. Cut the 2000-char slice at line 445 on a whitespace boundary and append a hand-off notice.
notes:
Verified in my own headless Chrome (port 9860, mock /live-kb, script /tmp/qa/verify/G15-0/t.mjs). The finding is half a defect and half design.

(1) Overflow: REPRODUCED and deterministic. A staff answer 'ดาวน์โหลดแบบฟอร์มที่ <~190-char docs.google.com/forms URL> ครับ' gave .ans scrollWidth 1973 vs clientWidth 504, bubble 1988 vs 534, document scrollWidth 2048 vs viewport 756. That means horizontal page scroll. Computed overflow-wrap is 'normal'. CSS line 81, `.msg.b .ans{...white-space:pre-line}`, has no overflow-wrap or word-break. Only `.ans a.inl` (line 249) has `word-break:break-all`, and a non-allowlisted URL is never wrapped in an <a>, so it gets no such rule. This is a real defect.

(2) Not clickable: REPRODUCED, but it is deliberate. A short `https://bit.ly/abc123` in a staff answer gives 0 <a> tags. `https://graduate.mahidol.ac.th/thai/` gives 1 <a>. The comment above linkify() (chatbot.html ~line 785) says the link allowlist (`_L_HOST`, Mahidol/LINE/Canva) is the only thing that becomes a link, so that text from the KB, website or LLM cannot send people to arbitrary hosts. The text stays visible, so the reader can copy it. Opening this up to staff links is a product and security decision, not a bug. Opening it would also affect the AI and website paths unless it were limited to e.staff entries.

(3) The claim that a 1990-char token reaches scrollWidth 15262 did NOT reproduce for Thai text. A 1990-char Thai-only token wrapped fine (scrollWidth 504). The overflow needs an unbreakable Latin/URL run. I did not test a pure-Latin 1990-char token, but it would behave like the URL case.

(4) The 2000-char truncation is real at line 445, `String(e.answer).slice(0,2000)`. I did not re-verify the mid-token cut and notice, so it is unconfirmed here.

Severity: low to medium. The overflow is real but only triggers on long unbroken tokens. Staff pasting Google Form URLs is plausible, and Google Forms links are long, so I'd rate the overflow low-medium and the link policy a design question.

I reproduced it in my own headless Chrome (port 9861, mock /live-kb on 9881, output in /tmp/qa/verify/G15-1/t.mjs). I used a fresh page per case, the real chatbot.html, and a staff entry served through the mock live-kb.

Results at the default 756px viewport:
- A ~180-char Google Form URL from staff produced no <a> element. The bubble had scrollWidth 1988 against clientWidth 534, and the document scrollWidth was 2048 against a 756 viewport, so the page scrolls horizontally. My URL was longer than the finding's (1442), but the mechanism is the same.
- A short https://bit.ly/3abcXYZ also produced no <a>. It does not overflow, so the link is simply unusable (plain text).
- A 1990-character unbroken token in a staff answer gave document scrollWidth 15262, matching the finding.
- At 390px (phone width) the Google Form case gave bubble scrollWidth 1988 against clientWidth 301, and document scrollWidth 2020 against a 390 viewport.
- A long Mahidol-host URL does become an <a>, and `.ans a.inl` has word-break:break-all, so it wraps. Only non-link text and non-allowlisted URLs overflow.

Cause:
- chatbot.html line 81: `.msg.b .ans` has white-space:pre-line and no overflow-wrap or word-break. The computed overflow-wrap is "normal". Only `a.inl` (line 249) and `.proof-full` break long strings.
- chatbot.html line 793: `_lUrlOk` and `_L_HOST` (line 791) allow only mahidol.ac.th, line.me and canva.site.
- chatbot.html line 445 (`refreshLiveKb`): `.slice(0,2000)` truncates blindly, so it can cut a URL or phone number mid-token. I did not re-test the truncation point; the code shows it plainly.

These are two separate things:
1. The overflow is a plain defect. It is not covered by the design rules, and it also breaks the layout on phones.
2. The non-clickable link is partly intended. The allowlist exists so that text from the KB, the website or an LLM cannot make arbitrary links. The comment above `linkify` says so. A staff-approved entry is a more trusted source, so allowing it is a reasonable product choice but not a certain bug. I rate the overflow medium and the missing link low to medium.

confirmed.title: Page ignores the current date: passed deadlines and windows are never marked, open programmes stay 'กำลังเปิดรับสมัคร' a year later
confirmed.area: programme cards / registration schedule / admissions round 1
confirmed.repro: Static server at 127.0.0.1:8791, URL base http://127.0.0.1:8791/chatbot.html?api=http://127.0.0.1:9&llm=http://127.0.0.1:9&ai=off. The round-1 entry shows 'ตัดรอบ ... 30 พฤศจิกายน 2569' as if upcoming on 2026-12-05 and 2027-11-04. The 2569 sem-1 registration (13–20 ก.ค. 2569) is shown without any passed marker on 2026-11-04 and 2027-11-04. Code has no `new Date()` for status; programmes.json fetched_at is never compared with the clock (chatbot.html lines 1001-1017, 1431).
confirmed.fix:
Smallest correct fix, in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html, function programmeCard() (about lines 1000-1045), plus a small helper next to _pSchedRows.
