2. Add _pDays(asOf, today). In programmeCard(), when fetched_at is more than about 30 days older than today, replace the quiet asOfLine with a visible warning: '⚠️ ข้อมูลนี้เก็บเมื่อ <date> (เก่ากว่า N วัน) — ตรวจสถานะล่าสุดที่ปุ่มด้านล่างก่อนตัดสินใจ'.

3. Parse the Thai-date cut-off rows in SC.rows (rows like 'จ. 30 พ.ย. 2569', via the existing _pDate or schedule parser). Append ' (ผ่านมาแล้ว)' to dates before today.
   - If every parsed round date is before today, drop the 🟢 and use '⚪ ตามประกาศ ณ <date> — รอบที่ระบุสิ้นสุดแล้ว'.
   - The same condition should also stop showing the apply_url button at the end of the return statement.

4. For the KB entries (registration, round 1), add a header line computed from the date ranges in the entry. That would be a render step in the KB answer path, not in the data. Cover the Rust twin too if it renders any of these strings.

Add a test in tests/ (like tests/answer_first.test.mjs) with an injected date.
notes:
Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9862, /tmp/qa/verify/G16-0/r.mjs). I used the same Date override through CDP Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument and a fresh page per question. The page's own clock matched the override (today = 2026-06-01, 2026-12-05 and 2027-11-04). Answers were byte-identical across all three dates for all three questions:
- '2018D04G เปิดรับสมัครไหม ปิดรับวันไหน ยังทันไหม' still starts with 'ตัดรอบพิจารณาคัดเลือก...: รอบ 1 จ. 30 พ.ย. 2569 · รอบ 2 อา. 31 ม.ค. 2570 · รอบ 3 พ. 31 มี.ค. 2570 · รอบ 4 จ. 31 พ.ค. 2570' and then '🟢 สถานะบนเว็บบัณฑิตว...'. On 2027-11-04 every round has passed, and nothing is marked.
- 'ตัดรอบสมัครรอบ 1 เมื่อไหร่' still says 'ตัดรอบ... 30 พฤศจิกายน 2569 ต้องชำระก่อนเวลา 22.00 น' with no passed marker on 2026-12-05 or 2027-11-04.
- 'ลงทะเบียนภาคต้น 2569 ได้ถึงเมื่อไหร่' still shows 'ช่วงลงทะเบียนเรียนปกติ: 13–20 กรกฎาคม 2569' on 2027-11-04.

I confirmed the cause in the code. chatbot.html has no clock use for status. The only `new Date` is at line 692, for the staff-answer tag. programmeCard() (lines 1000-1045) builds the 🟢 or 🔴 light only from `a.status`. The only staleness text is the fixed asOfLine, 'ข้อมูลจากเว็บบัณฑิตวิทยาลัย ณ <fetched_at> — สถานะอาจเปลี่ยน'. That line is a warning, but it never gets stronger as the data ages.

This is not a test artefact or intended design. 'Dated snapshot' is a design rule, and the page does print the snapshot date. But the rules say it must not make wrong claims, and a green 'กำลังเปิดรับสมัคร' with a list of passed deadlines, no marker and no 'ยังทันไหม' answer is a stale-state defect.

I rate it medium, not high. Today (2026-11-04) the snapshot is 2 days old and the data is correct. The harm only appears if programmes.json and the KB are not refreshed. It will be real for the first batch of passed round-1 dates after 30 Nov 2026. The data pipeline (submissions/build_programme_catalogue.py) is meant to be re-run.

I did not test the Rust engine separately. programmeCard is JS inside chatbot.html, and the fix there covers the default path unless the Rust engine renders the cards too. That needs a check before fixing.

Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9863), with Date overridden through CDP Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument (the page saw today = 2026-06-01, 2026-12-05 and 2027-11-04). I asked the three finding questions on a fresh page per question. Each question gave exactly one distinct answer text across the three dates (the script's distinct-answer check printed [1,1,1]), so the answers are byte-identical regardless of date. Harness: /tmp/qa/verify/G16-1/h.mjs. I did not run the 2026-07-15 and 2027-05-12 dates, or the sample of 10 open programmes.

Quoted text at 2027-11-04:
- 2018D04G card: '🗓️ ตัดรอบพิจารณาคัดเลือก ...: รอบ 1 จ. 30 พ.ย. 2569 · รอบ 2 อา. 31 ม.ค. 2570 · รอบ 3 พ. 31 มี.ค. 2570 · รอบ 4 จ. 31 พ.ค. 2570 ... 🟢 สถานะบนเว็บบัณฑิตว...'. I truncated the card at 420 characters, so I did not re-read the full green line or the footer; the other explorer's report quotes the 'กำลังเปิดรับสมัคร' status.
- Round 1: 'ตัดรอบ... 30 พฤศจิกายน 2569 ... ที่เก็บวันที่ 26 ตุลาคม 2569' with no passed marker.
- Registration: 'ช่วงลงทะเบียนเรียนปกติ: 13–20 กรกฎาคม 2569' with no passed marker.

Code check: chatbot.html has no clock use for status. programmeCard (line 1000) builds statusLine and asOfLine (lines 1039-1044) from the data only. _pSchedRows (line 995) prints the dates raw. PROGDOC.fetched_at is only formatted, never compared with the clock (lines 1431, 1470).

Mitigations and limits:
- The answers do carry source dates: the round-1 KB answer says 'ที่เก็บวันที่ 26 ตุลาคม 2569', and the programme cards say 'ณ 2 พ.ย. 2569'.
- The current date, 2026-11-04, is two days after the snapshot, so nothing is wrong today. The defect only appears once the data goes stale.
- The page is a static page whose data refreshes only on redeploy, so the risk is a forgotten refresh. That is why I rate it medium, not high.
- It is not a design-rule exception. 'Programme data is a dated snapshot' justifies the 'ณ' line. It does not justify an unqualified green 'กำลังเปิดรับสมัคร' after every listed round has passed. Tagging dates against the clock adds no new facts, so it does not break 'no improvised facts'.

confirmed.fix:
Smallest fix, in chatbot.html (mirror it in the Rust/wasm twin because Rust is the default engine). Add a deterministic temporal-intent step in _askCore, after smalltalk and before resolveProgramme:
1. Detect pure time words with no programme name: /ตอนนี้|วันนี้|เทอมนี้|ภาคนี้|ปีนี้|ยังทัน|หมดเขต|ปิดรับหรือยัง|ผ่านไปแล้วหรือยัง/.
2. On a match, skip resolveProgramme and the finder (isFinderQuestion), so time words never open the 379-programme list.
3. Rewrite the query to a registration-schedule query. Pick the term from the date, or show the existing 'กำหนดการลงทะเบียน' picker with the current term first and an honest line such as 'ผมดูวันที่แน่นอนให้ไม่ได้ ดูตารางด้านล่าง'. For a bare 'ยังทันไหม', ask 'ทันเรื่องอะไร (ลงทะเบียน / สมัคร / ส่งเล่ม)' with 3 chips.
Separate fix for the 'ทัน' substring match: in resolveProgramme (line 868) and the faculty/area regex near line 1060 (`ทันต`), require a word boundary or a following 'ต' (ทันต) so bare 'ทัน' no longer matches ทันตแพทย์. Also stop 'ตอนนี้' alone from pulling in unrelated KB entries, e.g. add it to the stop-words in search().
notes:
Reproduced in fresh headless Chrome (port 9864) on two fake clocks (2026-11-04 and 2027-11-04) with an injected Date override. Output is identical on both dates, because chatbot.html has no code that reads the current date (rg for `new Date(`/`Date.now` finds only a format call at line 692). So "now/this term" is never resolved, and the clock is irrelevant to every symptom. Script and evidence: /tmp/qa/verify/G17-0/run.mjs. Verbatim results:
- 'ลงทะเบียนได้ถึงเมื่อไหร่', 'หมดเขตลงทะเบียนเมื่อไหร่', 'เทอมนี้ลงทะเบียนวันไหน' all give the picker "คุณอาจหมายถึง (คิดซ้ำแล้วมีหลายข้อใกล้กัน)" with chips ภาคต้น 2570 / ภาคปลาย 2570 / ภาคปลาย 2569.
- 'ปีนี้ลงทะเบียนภาคปลายวันไหน' gives the scope-guard question "คำตอบไม่เหมือนกันในแต่ละปีการศึกษา — หมายถึงอันไหน?" with 2570 and 2569, even on 2027-11-04.
- 'ตอนนี้อยู่ในช่วงลงทะเบียนไหม' gives the entry "สอบวิทยานิพนธ์/สารนิพนธ์ผ่านแล้วแต่รอเผยแพร่", which is off-topic.
- 'วันนี้ปิดรับหรือยัง' and 'ลงทะเบียนล่าช้าตอนนี้ทันไหม' both give "ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้".
- 'ยังทันไหม' gives "ผมยังไม่แน่ใจว่าหมายถึงหลักสูตรไหน", then a list of dentistry programmes (ทันตแพทยศาสตร์ / ทันตกรรมจัดฟัน).
- 'ตอนนี้ลงทะเบียนเรียนได้ไหม' gives the wrong entry "กำลังศึกษาเทอมสุดท้ายสมัครเรียนได้ไหม" (a pre-admission topic), with schedule follow-up chips.
- 'ตัดรอบสมัครรอบ 1 พ.ย. 2569 ผ่านไปแล้วหรือยัง' and 'ตอนนี้ภาคเรียนอะไร' both open the 379-programme finder ("พบ 379 หลักสูตร ... อยากเรียนระดับไหน").

Correction to the report: the claim that the "2569 sem 1 and summer" options are missing is partly a data fact. The manual (knowledge-index.json) has only these schedule entries: ปลาย 2569, ฤดูร้อน 2569, ต้น 2570, ปลาย 2570, ฤดูร้อน 2570. There is no ภาคต้น 2569 entry, so that part is a content gap, not a logic bug. The summer 2569 entry exists but was not offered in the picker.

Not a violation of the design rules: nothing is invented, and the bot does hand off or ask. The defect is quality: no sensible answer for common time-relative questions, and some wrong-topic hits. The wrong-topic and finder hits are the worst part, because they look confident, e.g. a thesis-publication entry answering "am I in registration period". Severity stays medium: no wrong fact is stated, but the common question is not answered, and the dentistry hit looks silly in a demo.

I reproduced the symptoms on both ?engine=rust and ?engine=js. I used a fresh headless Chrome on port 9865 with a fresh page per question and the same wait pattern as scripts/coverage_probe.mjs. The behaviour was identical on both engines, so it is not a rust/wasm artefact. The probe is /tmp/qa/verify/G17-1/p.mjs.

Clock: the "fake clock 2026-11-04" part of the repro is irrelevant. chatbot.html never reads the current date; the only `new Date(` is for staff approved_at formatting. The result is deterministic and the same on any date, which fits the reporter's note that other dates gave the same output.

What reproduced, all 10 questions, quoted from the page:
- 'ลงทะเบียนได้ถึงเมื่อไหร่', 'หมดเขตลงทะเบียนเมื่อไหร่', 'เทอมนี้ลงทะเบียนวันไหน': "คุณอาจหมายถึง (คิดซ้ำแล้วมีหลายข้อใกล้กัน)" with chips ภาคต้น 2570, ภาคปลาย 2570, ภาคปลาย 2569.
- 'ปีนี้ลงทะเบียนภาคปลายวันไหน': "เรื่องนี้คำตอบไม่เหมือนกันในแต่ละปีการศึกษาครับ — หมายถึงอันไหน?" with chips ภาคปลาย 2570 and ภาคปลาย 2569.
- 'ตอนนี้อยู่ในช่วงลงทะเบียนไหม': wrong topic, the 'สอบวิทยานิพนธ์/สารนิพนธ์ผ่านแล้วแต่รอเผยแพร่' entry, presented as ✅ ข้อมูลทางการ.
- 'วันนี้ปิดรับหรือยัง' and 'ลงทะเบียนล่าช้าตอนนี้ทันไหม': "ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้" with generic chips (a dead end apart from the staff contact).
- 'ยังทันไหม': "ผมยังไม่แน่ใจว่าหมายถึงหลักสูตรไหน" with a picker of ทันตแพทยศาสตร์ programmes.
- 'ตอนนี้ลงทะเบียนเรียนได้ไหม': answers with the 'กำลังศึกษาเทอมสุดท้ายสมัครเรียนได้ไหม' entry ("สมัครได้ โดยใช้ใบเกรด..."). That is a wrong topic, though the follow-up chips offer the 3 registration schedules.
- 'ตัดรอบสมัครรอบ 1 พ.ย. 2569 ผ่านไปแล้วหรือยัง': the 379-programme finder ("พบ 379 หลักสูตร ... ข้อมูล ณ 2 พ.ย. 2569").

Corrections to the finding:
- The picker for the first four questions is honest behaviour, not a bug. It lists approved manual entries, makes up no date, and the page cannot know today's date. The only gap is that the manual has no entry for ภาคต้น 2569. knowledge-index.json only has ภาคต้น 2570, ภาคปลาย 2569, ภาคปลาย 2570, ฤดูร้อน 2569 and ฤดูร้อน 2570. So "2569 sem 1 missing from the picker" is a content gap, not a code bug. The summer 2569 entry does exist but is not offered by these queries.
- The picker is also arguably the intended "ask which one" design. I do not count the first four questions as defects; the remaining items are mild.
- Real, smaller defects:
  1. 'ยังทันไหม' opens a dentistry programme picker. The programme resolver matches a fragment such as 'ทัน' to 'ทันตแพทย์'. I did not trace the exact mechanism, but the symptom is clearly wrong.
  2. 'วันนี้ปิดรับหรือยัง' and 'ลงทะเบียนล่าช้าตอนนี้ทันไหม' are not understood at all.
  3. 'ตอนนี้อยู่ในช่วงลงทะเบียนไหม' and 'ตอนนี้ลงทะเบียนเรียนได้ไหม' land on unrelated entries (thesis-exam entry; last-term-applicant entry). This is a confident wrong answer shown as ✅ ข้อมูลทางการ, which is the more serious part.
  4. 'ผ่านไปแล้วหรือยัง' on a round deadline opens the generic 379-programme finder.

Severity: low overall. Nothing is made up and every case offers staff contact or chips. The wrong-topic ✅ answers (3) are the only medium-ish parts.

confirmed.title: CE year in a term question is read as an academic-year number, so 'summer 2026' silently returns the May 2027 schedule
confirmed.repro: Clock 2026-11-04, ask 'ลงทะเบียนภาคฤดูร้อน 2026 ได้เมื่อไหร่' and 'ภาคปลาย 2026 ลงทะเบียน'.
confirmed.expected: A CE year is a calendar year; 'ฤดูร้อน 2026' (May-Jul 2026) belongs to academic year 2568, which the manual does not cover, so the guard should say that (or ask), as it does for 2571.
confirmed.actual: scopeOf maps 2026 -> 2569 and returns 'ภาคฤดูร้อน ปีการศึกษา 2569' with 'ช่วงลงทะเบียนปกติ: 10–17 พฤษภาคม 2570' (which is CE 2027). The only hint is the entry's own 'แม้บางกิจกรรมอยู่ในปีปฏิทิน 2570' line. For 'ภาคปลาย 2026' the 2569 sem-2 entry (14–21 ธ.ค. 2569 = CE 2026) happens to fit, so the same rule is right for one term and wrong for another.
confirmed.fix:
Smallest fix is in scopeOf() in submissions/ui/chatbot.html. Have it return a ce flag, and a calendar year when the year was CE. In the 2024-2045 branch, do this:
- If the term is ฤดูร้อน, set year = String(n+542), because a CE-year summer belongs to the academic year that began the previous July. Then 2026 summer becomes 2568, which hits the existing scopeClarify 'no_year' message ('มีเฉพาะปี 2569, 2570').
- Otherwise keep n+543.
Update tests/kb_scope.test.mjs to match. As a second step, show the user an echo such as 'ตีความ 2026 เป็นปีการศึกษา 2569' with an undo chip, the same way the programme resolver echoes its interpretation. Keep the echo inside the scopeClarify 'pick' result.
notes:
Reproduced 2/2 independent ways: a fresh page per question, once with ?engine=rust and once with ?engine=js. The output is identical in both. The script is /tmp/qa/verify/G18-0/p.mjs on Chrome port 9866.

Actual answers:
- 'ลงทะเบียนภาคฤดูร้อน 2026 ได้เมื่อไหร่' returns the 'ภาคฤดูร้อน ปีการศึกษา 2569' entry. It says 'ช่วงลงทะเบียนปกติ: 10–17 พฤษภาคม 2570' and 'แม้บางกิจกรรมอยู่ในปีปฏิทิน 2570'. May 2570 is CE 2027, not 2026. There is no echo of how '2026' was read.
- 'ภาคปลาย 2026 ลงทะเบียน' returns the 2569 sem-2 entry, '14–21 ธันวาคม 2569', which is CE 2026 and happens to fit.
- 'ภาคฤดูร้อน 2569' gives the same answer as the 2026 question, so a CE year and a BE year are indistinguishable.
- 'ภาคฤดูร้อน 2571' gets the no-year guard: 'ยังไม่มีข้อมูล...ปีการศึกษา 2571 (มีเฉพาะปี 2569, 2570)'.

Cause: scopeOf() in submissions/ui/chatbot.html (about line 737) maps any 2024-2045 to n+543 as the academic year. That is right for ภาคต้น and ภาคปลาย, whose dates fall in the same CE year as the academic year starts. It is wrong for summer, whose dates fall in the next CE year. scopeOf exists only in the JS file (and tests/kb_scope.test.mjs), so the rust engine does not change it.

Not intended design: facts stay inside the manual, but the page silently picks one reading of an ambiguous year and shows dates a calendar-year reader would not expect. Severity low: the entry text carries the 'ปีปฏิทิน 2570' hint, and a CE year in a term question is uncommon. There is no made-up fact.

Not design intent: the design rules say facts come from the source and the AI must not improvise, which argues against silently rewriting dates, but the finding does not ask for that. The card faithfully copies a self-contradictory source, so I do not call it a code bug. Severity: I rate it low rather than medium. It is a faithful copy of the school's own typo, and the card already tells the user to check the source. The harm is that an applicant may trust a wrong weekday or date. Evidence on which part is wrong: for 15 ก.ย. 2570 a Friday would be 15 ต.ค. 2570, which is a Friday and would fit the order, so the cut-off 30 ก.ย. or the announcement date may be the typo. confirmed.title: 30 public KB entries are marked status: draft and 3 'unit_faq_pending_owner_review', yet are served as approved
confirmed.repro: Parse the frontmatter of /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/knowledge-public/*.md. 30 files have status: "draft" (gm_schedule_2570_round1, gm_application_fee, gm_scholarship_directory, gm_softskills_eight_domains, gm_mental_wellbeing_navigation, gm_travel_navigation and others). 3 have verification_status: unit_faq_pending_owner_review (gm_thesis_submission_05_committee_names, _07_title_change, _13_review_time). 12 have owner_unit '(รอตรวจสอบขอบเขตโดยเจ้าของงาน)'. All 132 have approval_status: approved, and the build script and https://reflexwork.pages.dev/knowledge-index.json publish them. Plan 001 records that all files were flipped to approved on a verbal OK.
confirmed.expected: One state field decides publication. If 'draft' or 'pending_owner_review' means not ready, the entry is not in the public index; if it does not, the field is removed or renamed.
confirmed.actual: Students are answered from 33 entries that their own frontmatter calls draft or pending owner review, with the official-information badge. The 'approved' flag is the only gate (F43 covers the two gated .md files on production, not this).
confirmed.fix: Smallest fix, after the owner decides. (1) For each of the 33 ids, either set `status: "current"` or `verification_status: "checked_against_saved_public_source"` in the frontmatter once the owner confirms, or set `approval_status: "pending_owner_approval"` to withhold the entry. (2) In submissions/build_knowledge_index.py, in the entry loop at about line 135, add a guard. Skip the entry when `fm.get("status") == "draft"` or `"pending" in fm.get("verification_status", "")`, unless a `--publish-all` or `--allow-draft` flag is passed, and list the skipped ids in the existing `skipped` summary. (3) Record the owner confirmation in .plans/001. Do not do (2) before (1), or about 33 entries will vanish from the public index and the chatbot will answer not-found for those topics.
notes: I checked the data and the build script directly. I did not run Chrome, because this is a static data and process finding. Counts from knowledge-public/*.md: 132 files; 30 have `status: "draft"` (e.g. gm_application_fee.md line 4); 3 have `verification_status: "unit_faq_pending_owner_review"` (e.g. gm_thesis_submission_07_title_change.md, which has status "current"); 12 contain the owner_unit text 'รอตรวจสอบขอบเขต'; all 132 have `approval_status: "approved"`. knowledge-index.json has 132 entries. build_knowledge_index.py lines 135-137 gate only on `approval_status != "approved"`, and it never reads `status` or `verification_status`. A grep of chatbot.html for 'draft' and 'pending_owner' finds nothing that gates on them, apart from an unrelated comment. So the factual claim holds. Plan 001 line 119 already records that Kiro flipped all 62 gm_ files to approved on a verbal OK. Plan 001 line 88 records the user's decision on 2026-10-31 to keep the files as imported and flag the approved flag for the user. The inconsistent fields therefore come from an acknowledged choice, not a hidden gap, and the 30 draft files are not all in the gm_ import. I rate it low, not medium. It is a metadata or process inconsistency. It is not a chatbot behaviour defect, because the design rules say answers come from the approved manual. The risk is real but small: draft-labelled content such as fees or schedules is shown with the official badge. I did not check whether any individual draft entry has wrong content. The finding's own suggestion says this is an owner decision, not a code bug.

I verified this by reading the files, not by driving Chrome. The finding is about data and build-script state, not page behaviour, so a browser run would add nothing.

Every count in the finding reproduces, using rg on /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/knowledge-public:
- 132 files in total, and all 132 have approval_status: approved.
- 30 files have status: "draft".
- 3 files contain unit_faq_pending_owner_review.
- 12 files have owner_unit text containing "รอตรวจสอบ".

The build gate is as described. /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/build_knowledge_index.py filters only on approval_status (lines 135-137). Nothing in the script reads `status` or `verification_status`, so those fields are never checked. The built knowledge-index.json has no "status" key either. The draft entries I sampled (welfare, application fee) are tagged source_type: official_public_website_snapshot with public snapshot dates of 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-28. That is why I read `status` as a content-lifecycle label and not a publication gate.

Plan 001 line 119 already records that Kiro flipped all 62 gm_ files to approved on Nott's verbal OK. It also records that 17 of those bodies still say "ข้อมูลทดสอบ / รอรับรองจากเจ้าของงาน", with the action "confirm with user that Nott's OK covers this". So the owner knows about the general issue. I found no record of a decision that covers these specific 33 ids.

This is not a design-rule exemption. The rules say facts come only from the approved manual, but the data contradicts itself about what "approved" means. I would not call it a functional defect, though. The page behaves as built, and the real issue is a missing owner decision and ambiguous field semantics. I rate it low, below the proposed medium, for these reasons:
- It is a governance and documentation gap, not a bug.
- The content comes from an official public-site snapshot.
- The risk is mainly reputational: the official-information badge may overstate review status.
- If the 3 pending_owner_review entries (committee names, title change, review time) carry operational claims, I would treat those 3 as medium. That needs an owner check.

confirmed.title: No IME composition guard: Enter that confirms a candidate sends the question; arrow keys during composition are hijacked by the typeahead
confirmed.repro: Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/chatbot.html?ai=off . Focus #q, type 'ค่าเทอม' with an IME that uses composition (desktop Thai/Japanese/Chinese IME, Gboard predictive Thai), press Enter to pick the candidate. Reproduced at event level with /tmp/qa/gap-4/t1.mjs, t3.mjs, t14.mjs: dispatch compositionstart then keydown {key:'Enter', keyCode:229, isComposing:true} on #q.
confirmed.expected: An Enter (or ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Escape) that belongs to an IME session must be ignored by the page: no send, no preventDefault. This also covers Safari's order (compositionend, then keydown Enter with keyCode 229 and isComposing=false).
confirmed.actual: The keydown handler (chatbot.html ~line 1883) only tests e.key. Composing Enter -> 1 user bubble sent with half-composed text and the input is cleared. Safari-order Enter with keyCode 229 -> sent. ArrowDown with isComposing:true and the typeahead open -> preventDefault'ed and the typeahead item is highlighted instead of the IME candidate. The same handler runs in Firefox. Caveat: proven with synthetic events; CDP cannot drive a real OS IME.
confirmed.fix: In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, add a shared guard and use it in both keydown handlers: the main $('q') handler at about line 1883 and the dis-filter inp handler at about line 1348. Declare `let _imeOn=false;` and add listeners on $('q'): `compositionstart` sets _imeOn=true; `compositionend` runs `setTimeout(()=>{_imeOn=false},0)`. The timeout covers Safari, which fires compositionend before the confirming keydown. Define `const _ime=e=>e.isComposing||e.keyCode===229||_imeOn;`. Put `if(_ime(e)) return;` as the first line of the $('q') keydown handler, before the ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Escape/Enter logic. Do the same in the dis-filter handler (give it its own flag, or attach the same composition listeners to inp). Optionally also guard the typeahead `input` handler so it does not refresh the suggestion list mid-composition. The guard does not disable the Send button, so clicking it still works.
notes: I reproduced this at event level in my own headless Chrome (port 9878) with /tmp/qa/verify/G24-0/t.mjs, on a fresh page each time with ai=off. I did not test a real OS IME, because CDP cannot drive one. I read the handler at submissions/ui/chatbot.html:1883 and it matches the finding: it only tests e.key. Results: (1) After compositionstart, keydown Enter with keyCode 229 and isComposing true sent the question: 1 user bubble, the input cleared to '', defaultPrevented false. (2) Safari order, Enter with keyCode 229 and isComposing false, gave the same result: the question was sent and the input was cleared. (3) With the typeahead open after typing 'ค่า', ArrowDown with isComposing true was preventDefault'ed and one .sg-i item got the 'on' class. The typeahead hijacked the key from the IME candidate list. The behaviour is deterministic because it is plain code logic. Nothing in the design rules permits this, so it is a real defect. Severity medium: it hits every Thai, Japanese or Chinese IME user on desktop and on predictive keyboards that fire composition Enter. The cost is a half-composed question sent and the input lost. It does not corrupt answers. The dis-filter handler at line 1348 has the same flaw: it preventDefaults Enter and clicks the only visible chip while composing. That one is less harmful.

Reproduced in my own headless Chrome (port 9879, script /tmp/qa/verify/G24-1/t.mjs). I loaded chatbot.html?ai=off on a fresh page for each case.

Results, all with synthetic events:
- compositionstart, then keydown Enter with keyCode 229 and isComposing true: 1 user bubble sent. The input was cleared (val ''). defaultPrevented was false, so the ask() branch ran.
- Safari order, compositionend, then keydown Enter with keyCode 229 and isComposing false: 1 bubble sent, input cleared.
- Typeahead open for 'ค่า', then composing ArrowDown: the typeahead was open, defaultPrevented was true, and 1 .sg-i item got the 'on' class. The IME candidate navigation is hijacked.

Code check: the keydown handler at chatbot.html line 1883 ($('q').addEventListener('keydown')) tests only e.key. There is no isComposing, keyCode or composition* anywhere in the file (rg found none). The dis-filter handler at line 1348 also only checks e.key==='Enter'. That one does preventDefault and clicks only when exactly one chip is visible, so its impact is smaller.

Not a design rule. Nothing in the design rules covers it; it is a plain input-handling defect.

Caveat: this is synthetic. CDP cannot drive a real OS IME, but the event shapes match the real browser behaviour. The Chrome and Firefox order is keydown with isComposing true and keyCode 229. The Safari order is compositionend first, then keydown with keyCode 229.

Severity: medium is right. The page is Thai-first, and Thai users on mobile (Gboard predictive) or desktop IMEs hit it, but only with composition-based input. The effect is a premature send of half-typed text, not wrong facts. It is lower than medium for plain Thai keyboards, which do not compose.

confirmed.title: Printing an answer (schedule) is unusable: no @media print, collapsed dates are lost, sticky nav printed over the text, pale ink
confirmed.repro: Ask 'กำหนดการลงทะเบียน ภาคต้น ปีการศึกษา 2569' then 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน', emulate media=print and Page.printToPDF (/tmp/qa/gap-4/t8.mjs; output /tmp/qa/gap-4/shots/print.pdf and print_p1.png). Or use the browser's print preview.
confirmed.expected: A student printing the registration schedule gets every date, in dark readable text, without UI chrome.
confirmed.actual: chatbot.html and theme.css have no @media print rule. The PDF shows only 4 lines of the schedule followed by 'อ่านเพิ่มอีก 30 ข้อ': the 30 folded items (the remaining dates) are not printed. Computed text colour stays rgb(233,237,255) on a white page (pale grey), the user bubble is clipped at the right edge, the sticky nav is printed in the middle of the text over 'ปีการศึกษา 2569', and the input box, example chips and vote buttons are printed.
confirmed.fix: Add a single `@media print` block at the end of the `<style>` in submissions/ui/chatbot.html. It needs these rules: (1) `.rw-nav, .ask, .chips, .followups, .vote, #ev-list, .evidence, .howto {display:none !important}` (confirm the real class names for the input row, vote buttons and evidence panel). (2) `body, .msg, .msg.b, .msg.u {background:#fff !important; color:#000 !important; box-shadow:none}`. (3) `.rw-nav {position:static}` (only needed if the nav is not hidden). (4) `.msg {max-width:100%; break-inside:avoid}`. Chrome cannot print a closed `<details>`. For print, add a `beforeprint` listener in chatbot.html that sets `open=true` on all `#chat details` and an `afterprint` listener that restores them. Do not rely on CSS for this.
notes: Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9880, /tmp/qa/verify/G25-0/t.mjs, output print.pdf). I did not repeat the second question or rebuild the PNG. Code check: `rg "@media print"` finds it only in dashboard.html, slides.html and pitch*.html. chatbot.html and theme.css have none. After the schedule question, the page has one `details.more` with summary "อ่านเพิ่มอีก 30 ข้อ". With media=print, the computed colour is rgb(233,237,255), nav position is sticky and #q is display:block. The PDF is 2 pages. pdftotext shows the schedule cut off after two date lines (regular registration period and the last payment day) followed by "อ่านเพิ่มอีก", so the 30 folded dates are missing. The input box, example chips and the other UI text are printed (verified from the text only, not the layout). Not intended design: no design rule covers print. I did not visually confirm the clipped user bubble or the nav overlapping the text. I confirmed the cause in code: `.msg{max-width:84%}` and `--ink:#e9edff` with `--bg:#0b1020`. Browsers drop backgrounds when printing by default, so the pale ink lands on white paper. I rate it low rather than medium: it is a real defect but only affects an optional print path. The core Q&A is not affected.

I reproduced this in my own headless Chrome (port 9881) with a fresh profile. The script is /tmp/qa/verify/G25-1/t.mjs and the PDF is /tmp/qa/verify/G25-1/print.pdf. I asked the two questions on one page, emulated media=print, ran Page.printToPDF, and read the PDF with pdftotext.

What I saw:
- **No print rules:** no stylesheet has an @media print rule (printRules=0). `rg "@media print"` finds none in chatbot.html or theme.css. Other pages (slides, pitch, dashboard) do have print rules, so this is an omission rather than design.
- **Folded dates lost:** the schedule answer prints as 4 lines and then "อ่านเพิ่มอีก 30 ข้อ". The `<details class="more">` is closed (open=false, height about 22px), so the other 30 items, which hold the remaining dates, are not in the PDF. This reproduced every time.
- **Pale ink:** the computed colour of body and `.ans` is rgb(233,237,255) in print media. That is near-white text, which is unreadable on paper unless the user turns on "background graphics". I ran with printBackground:false, so the white page is exactly the case where it fails.
- **Chrome left in:** the PDF text includes the example chips ("ลองถามเรื่องเหล่านี้ได้เลย"), the "👆 กดตัวอย่าง…" hint, the "คำตอบนี้ช่วยได้ไหม? 👍 ใช่ 👎 ไม่" vote row, the "ถามต่อ:" follow-up chips, and the "🔬 ดูหลักฐานเบื้องหลัง" button.
- **Sticky nav in the middle of the text:** `.rw-nav` computes to display:flex and position:sticky in print. The line "🦀 ReflexWork ถามคำถาม ยื่นคำร้อง เบื้องหลังระบบ" appears mid-body, right after the second question's "✅ ข้อมูลทางการ" label. The finding's claim that it overprints "ปีการศึกษา 2569" is not something I checked. The nav does repeat inside the content.
- **Cut-off bubble:** I did not check the clipped user bubble. documentElement.scrollWidth is 756, wider than a portrait page, which supports the overflow.
- **Evidence panel:** `.evidence` is display:none, so that part of the finding does not hold. The evidence panel is not printed.

Severity: I rate this low, not medium. It only affects people who print or save to PDF, and nothing wrong is stated. The one real information loss is the dropped dates, and the user can open the details first. The unreadable pale ink is the most visible symptom. Medium is defensible only if printing the schedule is a core use case for students.

confirmed.title: Sticky nav plus sticky input leave almost no room on small/short screens, and the input is not sticky on landscape phones and tablets
confirmed.repro: Chrome mobile emulation with touch: (a) 320x568, ask 7 questions, then shrink the viewport to 284-341 px high (keyboard open) - /tmp/qa/gap-4/t5.mjs; (b) 427x267 css px (=300% zoom of a 1280 window); (c) 844x390 landscape phone and 768x1024: ask 3 questions and measure #q (/tmp/qa/gap-4/t6.mjs).
confirmed.expected: The input stays reachable and a usable strip of the conversation stays visible with the keyboard open, at high zoom and in landscape.
confirmed.actual: (a) at <=560 px wide the sticky nav (94 px) + sticky input block (118 px) = 212 px; with the keyboard, only 72-129 px remain for bubbles on 320x568. (b) At 300% zoom the two bars exceed the viewport (free space -52 px): no answer is visible. (c) The sticky .ask rule is in @media(max-width:560px) only, so at 844x390 the input is below the fold after each answer (top 432-437 px vs viewport 390; 4142 px down after 7 questions) and the page auto-scrolls to the bubble start, so the user must scroll to find the input; the 768 tablet is fine only while the viewport is tall.
confirmed.fix: In submissions/ui/chatbot.html (CSS block near line 210) move `.ask{position:sticky;bottom:0;z-index:15;background:var(--bg);margin-top:0}` out of the @media(max-width:560px) block and key it to `@media (max-width:560px), (max-height:500px), (pointer:coarse)`. Note the base rule `.ask{position:relative}` at line 151 comes earlier, so the new media rule must stay after it. In the same query, or in theme.css (shared by 4 pages, so scope it with a chatbot-only selector or put it in chatbot.html), add `@media (max-height:500px){.rw-nav{position:static}}` so the 56-94px nav does not stack with the input. Optionally keep the nav on one line in short viewports. The suggestion to refocus #q after send is not needed to fix the layout and should be treated as separate (it would pop the keyboard on touch devices).
notes: Reproduced in my own Chrome (port 9882), mobile emulation, real page, 3 questions per size, measured via getBoundingClientRect/getComputedStyle (script /tmp/qa/verify/G26-0/t.mjs). Results: 320x568: nav sticky 0-94, .ask sticky 118px tall (450-568), so 212px of chrome and about 356px of the viewport remains. 320x300 (keyboard-like height): nav 0-94 plus ask 182-300 leaves 88px for the chat (the finder said 72-129). 427x267 (=300% zoom): nav 94 plus ask 118 leaves 55px, which is cramped but not negative, so the finder's -52px figure did not reproduce here (maybe a different width or wrap). 844x390 landscape: .ask computes position:relative (the sticky rule is only inside @media max-width:560px, line 210 of chatbot.html). After question 1, #q is at top 433-479 with viewport 390, so it is off-screen. After question 2 it is at 340, after question 3 at 266, so it is below the fold only on the first answer(s) and the page scrolls to the bubble start (scrollY 546/1035/1336). The finder's "4142px down after 7 questions" was not re-run but is consistent with the unsticky layout. 768x1024 is fine (q at 900-946, in view) and 1280x720 desktop is fine. This is a real layout defect, not a timing artefact (positions are stable after 3.5s waits) and not a design rule. It is not a correctness or fact issue, so medium is fair, perhaps low-medium because only landscape phones, very high zoom and keyboard-open cases are affected; portrait phones at normal height work. Caveat: headless emulation does not shrink the visual viewport like a real soft keyboard (iOS keeps the layout viewport and uses the visual viewport), so the keyboard case is simulated by a short viewport only.

I reproduced it in my own Chrome (port 9883, scripts in /tmp/qa/verify/G26-1/t.mjs and t2.mjs). I used mobile emulation and the harness from /tmp/qa/gap-4/lib/cdp.mjs.

(c) Landscape 844x390, 7 questions asked on one page. The reproduction was 7 out of 7 runs:
- .ask computes position:relative; only .rw-nav is sticky (56 px high).
- #q top after each answer was 432, 437, 339, 433, 438, 339, 432 px against a 390 px viewport. It is below the fold in 5 of 7 runs and in view only on every third question. The in-view cases are the short answers.
- Each answer scrolls the page so the new bubble sits at top -14. scrollY reached 3339 and the page was 3895 px tall, so the user has to scroll down to reach the input.
- document.activeElement is BODY after each answer, so focus is not returned to #q. The send helper clicks #send, so a real tap could differ slightly.

(a) 320x568, then resized to 320x300 as a keyboard stand-in: .rw-nav is 94 px sticky and .ask is 118 px sticky, so 212 px are fixed. Only 88 px remain for bubbles at 300 px high. The input stays reachable, so this part is a squeeze, not a lockout.

(b) 427x267 (300% zoom): the bars take 212 of 267 px, leaving 55 px. The finding's -52 px figure is not what I measured. #q was still in view, but almost no conversation is visible. This is a severe squeeze, not a total lockout.

768x1024: the input is in view and fine while the viewport is tall, as the finding said. .ask is not sticky there either, because the rule only applies at max-width:560px.

Cause (verified in the code):
- chatbot.html:210 puts `.ask{position:sticky;bottom:0...}` inside `@media (max-width:560px)`.
- theme.css:13-14 sets `.rw-nav{position:sticky;top:0}` at every size.
- Nothing is keyed to viewport height.

This is not intended design. No design rule covers layout, and the code comment at line 210 says the aim is that the phone input stays on screen.

Severity stays medium. The page works on a normal portrait phone (320x568 and larger). The failures are specific to landscape, high zoom and keyboard-up on small screens. They are real usability problems, but the input is still reachable by scrolling.

The suggested `focus #q after send` is probably counterproductive on mobile because it reopens the keyboard. I would skip it.

confirmed.title: normChat does not canonicalise Thai variants and invisible characters, so short or pasted queries diverge
confirmed.repro: With /tmp/qa/gap-4/t2.mjs, t4.mjs, t7.mjs: ask 'ล่มทำอย่างไร' then the same with sara am typed as U+0E4D U+0E32 ('ล่มทํา อย่างไร' without the space: 'ล่มทําอย่างไร'); ask 'ต้องมีกี่บท' with the tone mark typed before the vowel (e.g. 'กี่' as U+0E01 U+0E48 U+0E35); paste a question containing U+2060 or U+00AD after every letter.
confirmed.expected: Same answer as the canonical spelling (brief: tone-mark order variants and sara am as nikhahit + sara aa retrieve the same answer).
confirmed.actual: normChat (chatbot.html ~line 779) only does NFC, strips U+200B-200D/FEFF, collapses 3+ repeats and whitespace. Sara am decomposed: 5 of 57 short queries change (e.g. 'ล่มทำอย่างไร' -> GRID-down entry, decomposed -> 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้'). Tone before vowel: 9 of 73 change ('ต้องมีกี่บท' -> not understood; 'ต้องส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' -> same entry but the bold lead 'ภายใน 21 วัน' is lost). 22 of 31 invisible code points are kept (U+00AD, U+034F, U+200E/F, U+202A-E, U+2060-2064, U+2066-2069, U+FE0E/F, U+3164); a soft hyphen or word joiner after every letter breaks 117 of 132 KB titles. Long full-sentence titles survive sara-am variants (48/48) and a single stray invisible char, so impact is mainly on short queries.
confirmed.fix: In normChat (submissions/ui/chatbot.html, line 779), after .normalize('NFC') add: .replace(/ํา/g,'ำ') to fold nikhahit + sara aa into sara am; .replace(/([่-๋])([ัิ-ื็ํ])/g,'$2$1') to put the vowel before the tone mark; and widen the strip to /[\p{Cf}︀-️͏ㅤ]/gu, which covers U+00AD, U+200E/F, U+202A-E, U+2060-2069 and the variation selectors. Do the Thai reordering before stripping so that the characters sit adjacent. If a Rust normaliser exists in the wasm source, mirror the same three rules there and add the variants to scripts/coverage_probe.mjs or tests/chat_robust.test.mjs.
notes:
Reproduced in my own headless Chrome (port 9884). Script: /tmp/qa/verify/G27-0/t.mjs. Output: out.txt (default engine) and out_js.txt (?engine=js). I used a fresh page per question and waited for programmes.json to load, so this is not a timing artefact. The two engines behave the same.

Results, canonical spelling first:
- 'ล่มทำอย่างไร' returns the official-info (✅ ข้อมูลทางการ) answer 'แจ้งข้อมูลการจองผ่าน LINE @693lascg…'. The same query with sara am typed as U+0E4D U+0E32 returns 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้…'.
- 'ต้องมีกี่บท' returns '✅ ข้อมูลทางการ จำนวนบทขึ้นกับประเภทและรูปแบบของเล่ม: …6 บท'. With the tone mark typed before the vowel (ก ่ ี) it returns the not-understood message.
- 'ต้องส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' with the tone mark before the vowel still finds the entry, but the answer opens 'กำหนดทั่วไปตามประกาศ…' instead of the bold lead 'ไม่เกิน 21 วัน…'. This is a second, quieter divergence.
- 'ต้องส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' with sara am decomposed is unaffected: the query contains no sara am, so my transform changes nothing.
- All three queries with U+2060 or U+00AD after every letter return not-understood. The same happens when the questions are pasted that way.

The cause is confirmed in normChat (chatbot.html line 779-781). It does NFC, strips only U+200B-200D and U+FEFF, collapses repeated characters and collapses whitespace. NFC does not fold U+0E4D U+0E32 into U+0E33, and it does not reorder Thai tone marks.

Real-world likelihood is low. Normal Thai keyboards produce U+0E33 and the canonical mark order. The variants show up mainly with pasted text from PDFs, Word or some mobile IMEs. Impact is limited to short queries and falls back to an honest not-understood with options, so it is not a wrong answer.

I did not check the 5-of-57, 9-of-73 and 22-of-31 counts or the 117-of-132 title figure. I only confirmed the direction and the three example queries.

The Rust twin: I found no norm_chat in any .rs file. Only the JS normChat and tests/chat_robust.test.mjs reference the name. The wasm twin may normalise elsewhere, and I did not locate it. Whoever applies the fix should check that both engines still agree. Both engines gave identical results here, so the normalisation is probably shared or applied before the wasm call.

confirmed.title: Reload or in-tab navigation silently discards the whole conversation and follow-up context
confirmed.repro: Open the page, ask 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' and 'แล้วถ้าส่งช้าล่ะ', then either reload or click the nav link 'ยื่นคำร้อง' and press Back (/tmp/qa/gap-4/t9.mjs).
confirmed.expected: At least a clear note that the conversation is not kept, or the last answers restored (the product says no login, but nothing prevents session-only storage).
confirmed.actual: After Back/Reload: 0 user bubbles, only the greeting; 'แล้วถ้าส่งช้าล่ะ' then returns 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้' because the programme/topic context is gone. Only rw_ev (judge view) is persisted; sessionStorage is unused and there is no pushState. Answer links use target=_blank so the common path is not affected; the nav links open in the same tab. A real browser's bfcache may restore the DOM (not testable headless).
confirmed.fix: In /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html, make the smallest fix first. Add target="_blank" rel="noopener" to the student-desk.html nav link at line ~291. Optionally, persist the last N (about 10) Q/A pairs plus the follow-up context object (programme/topic) in sessionStorage. Write it at the end of _askCore, or wherever the bubbles are appended. On load, restore the bubbles and the context before enabling #q. Wrap every storage call in try/catch, as the rw_ev code at lines 1895-1897 does. If you do not want persistence, show a one-line note in the greeting such as 'การสนทนาไม่ถูกเก็บไว้เมื่อรีโหลด'. Investigate the in-session follow-up failure for 'แล้วถ้าส่งช้าล่ะ' separately in the follow-up branch of _askCore.
notes:
I reproduced the state loss in my own Chrome (port 9886, /tmp/qa/verify/G28-0/t.mjs, out.txt), using two methods. The "context is gone" claim is confounded, and the finding's evidence for it is wrong.

1. Nav click and Back. I asked Q1 and Q2, which gave 2 user bubbles and 3 bot bubbles. I clicked the 'ยื่นคำร้อง' nav link, which opened /student-desk.html in the same tab, then navigated back through history. The result was 0 user bubbles and only the greeting. sessionStorage was empty and localStorage held only rw_ev.
2. Reload. I asked Q1, then reloaded. The result was again 0 user bubbles and 1 bot bubble.

The chat is in-memory only. rg finds no sessionStorage, pushState, pageshow or beforeunload handling in chatbot.html. The nav links at lines 288-293 have no target=_blank, so they navigate in the same tab. This is a missing feature, not a stated design rule. "No login" does not rule out session-only storage.

Confounder: Q2 'แล้วถ้าส่งช้าล่ะ' already returned the 'ขออภัยครับ ผมยังจับใจความคำถามนี้ไม่ได้' not-understood reply BEFORE any reload or navigation. I ran this with ai=off and the AI unreachable. So that reply is not caused by the reload. The follow-up fails in-session too. The finding's "then returns not-understood because context is gone" is therefore not demonstrated. The follow-up resolver does not handle this phrasing with the AI off, and that is a separate issue. The same Q1/Q2 sequence gives an identical reply after a reload, so the lost context cannot be shown to matter for this phrasing.

Not tested: real-browser bfcache, which may restore the DOM. I did not verify the rw_ev=1 persistence remark.

Severity: low. Answer links already use target=_blank. The loss only affects users who click a nav link and come back, or who reload. Nothing wrong or invented is answered, and the greeting is shown again.

confirmed.title: All text sizes are fixed px, so the browser/OS text-size setting is ignored
confirmed.repro: Set html{font-size:200%} (equivalent to a 200% default font size) on a 390x844 page: /tmp/qa/gap-4/t11.mjs.
confirmed.expected: Body text, chips and labels grow with the text-size preference (brief asks for 200% text size).
confirmed.actual: 73 px font-size declarations and 1 em in chatbot.html; with html font-size 32px the answer stays 15px, #q 16px, chips 12.5px, source label 11px. Browser zoom works (no overflow at 200%/300%), but a text-size-only setting has no effect on desktop Chrome/Firefox or in the Android/iOS settings that act through the root size.
confirmed.fix: In chatbot.html (the inline style block) and theme.css, convert every font-size: Npx to font-size: (N/16)rem. The smallest labels are 11px and 12.5px; raise them to at least .8125rem. Leave the base html font-size unset so it follows the user preference. Then re-check at 200% root size at 390px width for layout overflow, because fixed-height elements such as the input bar and chips may need min-height instead of height. The one existing .9em is already relative, so it scales once its parent does. A simple mechanical pass is a sed or script over the font-size:([\d.]+)px patterns only (not width/height/padding, which can stay px).
notes: Reproduced two ways. (1) Static count in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui: chatbot.html has 73 font-size declarations in px and 1 in em (.9em); theme.css has 2 in px; there are no rem or % sizes. (2) Live check in headless Chrome on port 9888 at 390x844 with the 8791 server. At the default root size the computed sizes were #q 16px, #send 15px, .chip 12.5px, h1 21px, body 16px. After I set html{font-size:200%}, the root and body went to 32px. #q, #send, .chip and h1 stayed at 16px, 15px, 12.5px and 21px. So the root text-size setting is ignored for every element that has an explicit px size. Only inherited text, such as the body fallback, scales. This is a WCAG 1.4.4 resize-text concern in spirit, but browser zoom still works, which the original report also says. It is not a design rule: nothing in the DESIGN RULES covers text sizing. I did not test overflow at 200% text size, and I did not check the .answer size in a live bot bubble. The empty page showed no .msg.b, and #q, #send and .chip are enough to show the problem. Severity low is right. It affects only users who set a text size without zooming, and the page is usable with zoom. It also overlaps the small-text finding F50.

confirmed.title: Counters: advice-worded questions with a strong match are counted twice; disambiguation adds no baht
confirmed.repro: http://127.0.0.1:8791/chatbot.html?api=http://127.0.0.1:9&llm=http://127.0.0.1:9&view=judge. Ask once: 'ช่วยแนะนำวิธีจัดการเวลาทำวิทยานิพนธ์' (the page's own orange example chip). Also try 'แนะนำ ' + any manual title, e.g. 'แนะนำ ส่งรูปเล่มวิทยานิพนธ์ภายในกี่วันหลังสอบผ่าน'. Second case: fresh page, ask 'What is the Turnitin limit?' (disambiguation) or 'ขอคำแนะนำเรื่อง Turnitin Origi...' style prompts. Sweep script: /tmp/qa/gap-5/sweep.mjs, results sweep.json.
confirmed.expected: One question answered from the manual gives auto=1, saved=฿2, ratio 100% (1/1). saved always equals auto x 2.
confirmed.actual: After ONE question the bar shows 'ตอบจากคู่มือ: 2', 'ประหยัดโดยประมาณ ฿4' and ratio '100% (2/2)'. In a 448-question sweep, 233 questions raised auto by 2 (117 of 132 'แนะนำ'+title, 112 of 129 'ขอคำแนะนำเรื่อง...'), so 659 auto increments were counted for 426 answered questions. Cause: auto++/saved+=COST at about line 1510 and again in the topScore>=6 branch at about line 1559. The disambiguate branch does auto++ without saved+=COST (auto=1, saved=฿0), so saved != auto x COST.
confirmed.fix: In /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork/submissions/ui/chatbot.html, in _askCore(), make three changes. (1) Delete the first `auto++; saved+=COST;` at ~line 1559, the one just under the comment '// decent KB match → grounded hybrid (async)'. Add `auto++; saved+=COST;` at the start of the mid-strength path, just before `const mid='hyb'+(++fbN);`, so each path counts once. (2) In the disambiguate branch (~line 1608), change `auto++;` to `auto++; saved+=COST;`. (3) Keep saved from drifting by deriving it from auto: add a `bump()` helper (`auto++; saved=auto*COST;`) and use it in every branch that counts. renderFinder (~line 1352), the scope guard (~1510) and the other count sites all increment this way, so check them too. Add a test that sends the advice example chip and asserts auto===1 and saved===2, and one that sends a disambiguation question and asserts saved===auto*2. Check whether the Rust/wasm engine also counts. In my runs both engines gave identical counter values, which suggests the counters live only in the page JS.
notes:
I reproduced both defects in a fresh headless Chrome on port 9890, with view=judge and llm=http://127.0.0.1:9. Both engines (rust and js) gave identical results. The script is /tmp/qa/verify/G30-0/r.mjs.

Results as (auto, saved):
- 'ช่วยแนะนำวิธีจัดการเวลาทำวิทยานิพนธ์' gave auto=2, saved=฿4. It is double-counted on both engines, 2 of 2 runs.

2. Make the chip depend on the source. Use `${hit.staff ? '📝 ตอบจากคำตอบเจ้าหน้าที่ · ไม่เรียก AI' : '✅ ตอบจากคู่มือทันที · ไม่เรียก AI'}` at line 1599. Check the class="route auto" regex at line 648, which matches "ตอบจากคู่มือ". The staff badge is chosen first (`staff?...`), so it is unaffected.

3. Do not change the engine or decideTier. Do not change the Rust/wasm twin unless the reason string is generated there; the new text is render-only.

The alternative is to drop "คะแนน · หัวข้อ KB" from the subtitle at line 358. That is cheaper but loses the audit value.
notes:
Reproduced in my own headless Chrome (port 9896, ?view=judge, api/llm pointed at 127.0.0.1:9, fresh page per question, waited for the new .msg.b without .typing and for an .ev-card). Script: /tmp/qa/verify/G33-0/r.mjs. I confirmed it two ways: by driving the page, and by reading the code. Live run, two manual hits. Both cards contained only the kernel strip (FastPath, "gate θ=0.72 · ความซับซ้อน 0.212 · g=0.060", timing, BLAKE3), the chip "✅ ตอบจากคู่มือทันที · ไม่เรียก AI ⚡ reflex", and the constant meta "gate ต่ำ + KB ตรงชัด — ตอบทันที". - There was no retrieval score, no rank-2 margin and no entry id or title in either card. - The entry title appeared only in the left bubble's .topic. Examples: "ที่มา: ค่าธรรมเนียมการโอนเงินผ่าน Online Banking เท่าไร" and "ที่มา: ขั้นตอนการส่งรูปเล่มวิทยานิพนธ์/สารนิพนธ์ในรูปแบบดิจิทัล". - The only number is g=0.060, which is the kernel gate score (route_task), not the KB retrieval score. The subtitle's "คะแนน" can arguably mean that, so the claim is partly overstated. - Not-found cards ("ลาป่วย...", "ขอทุนอุดหนุน...") show no score or entry either. That is reasonable because there is no entry, but it also shows no top-candidate score. Code evidence in submissions/ui/chatbot.html: - Line 605: EV_SEL = '.route, .meta, .proof-full, .kernel-strip'. Only these nodes are moved into the card, so .topic, .ans and .staff-tag never reach the panel. - Line 716: decideTier returns the constant reason. The act branch at about lines 1596-1604 renders `
${verdict.reason}
` with no top.s, margin or hit.id. - Line 1599: the chip text "✅ ตอบจากคู่มือทันที" is hardcoded. kbBody (about line 683) puts the staff tag inside .ans, and line 648 derives the left badge "📝 เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบ" from data-staff in the raw html. So a staff answer gets the staff badge on the left and the "from the manual" chip in the panel. I did not run the staff mock (/tmp/qa/gap-5/staff.mjs); this part rests on reading the code. - Score does appear on the abstain meta (about line 1552, "score ${topScore}") and on some advice and understand paths, as the reporter said. Severity: low. The evidence panel is hidden in the student view and is judge/engineering only. No fact or answer is wrong. It is a transparency gap, and the staff chip contradicting the staff badge is a small honesty inconsistency that a judge could notice. This is not design intent: the rules say the judge view shows the engineering words, and the subtitle itself promises "คะแนน · หัวข้อ KB". Side observation, not part of G33: "ค่าธรรมเนียมการศึกษาต่อภาคเท่าไร" was answered from the entry "ค่าธรรมเนียมการโอนเงินผ่าน Online Banking เท่าไร", which looks like a weak or wrong match. The card does not show the score or entry that would let a judge spot this, which is the cost of G33. I did not look into it further.

confirmed.title: BLAKE3 'fingerprint' is described as sealing the answer and as verifiable afterwards, but commits to neither the answer nor the typed text
confirmed.repro: /tmp/qa/gap-5/fp.mjs: mock kernel /live-kb returns a staff entry for 'ขอเปลี่ยนหัวข้อวิทยานิพนธ์ บฑ.49'; ask it with and without the staff entry. Also ask 'ส่งรูปเล่มมมมมภายในกี่วัน' and 'ส่งรูปเล่ม   ภายในกี่วัน' and compare with the panel label. Independent check: BLAKE3(utf8(normChat(q)) || 'FastPath' || 'DataQuery') using kernel-worker/vendor/blake3.js (b3sum not installed).
confirmed.expected: 'ทุกคำตอบผนึก BLAKE3 fingerprint' and 'ตรวจสอบย้อนหลังได้' mean a reader can recompute the digest from what the panel shows, and a changed answer or KB changes it.
confirmed.actual: The digest reproduces only from the NORMALISED question + route + category. Answer, KB version, entry and engine are not included: the manual answer and a completely different staff answer give the identical fingerprint 0942b1fd...72a9. The label shows the typed text, so 'ส่งรูปเล่มมมมมภายในกี่วัน' shows the fingerprint of 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' (2e8b1aec...), and hashing the label does not reproduce it. The recipe is not on the page. Smalltalk replies have no fingerprint at all.
confirmed.fix: Smallest fix is wording only, in submissions/ui/chatbot.html. At line 323, change 'ทุกคำตอบผนึก BLAKE3 fingerprint รันซ้ำได้' to something like 'ทุกคำถามที่เข้า kernel มีรหัส BLAKE3 อ้างอิงคำถาม+เส้นทาง'. At line 1423-1424 (the proof-full block built in the function that renders the evidence card, near line 1411), relabel it 'รหัสอ้างอิงของคำถามและเส้นทาง (ไม่ครอบคลุมตัวคำตอบ)'. Change the note to say it is computed from the normalised question text (as shown in the card), the route and the category, and drop 'ตรวจสอบย้อนหลังได้'. Optionally also show the normalised q in the card, since the label currently shows the typed text. A stronger fix would append the entry id and a hash of the answer or KB version before hashing. That means changing route_task in crates/reflex-wasm/src/lib.rs and the JS twin, and it affects the 'mirrors attestation composite hash' invariant, so it is not recommended for something this minor.
notes:
Reproduced in my own headless Chrome (port 9898, rust engine, view=judge, script /tmp/qa/verify/G34-0/p.mjs), two independent ways.

1. Code reading. route_task in crates/reflex-wasm/src/lib.rs hashes only input || route || category. chatbot.html line 1411 calls route_task('DataQuery', q, 2048, 128), and q is normChat(typed) (line 1390). No answer text, entry id, KB version or engine goes into the hash. So the staff answer versus manual answer case gives the same digest by construction. I did not run the staff-mock part of the original repro. The code makes it certain.

2. Live runs.
- 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน' and 'ส่งรูปเล่มมมมมภายในกี่วัน' both show proof 2e8b1aec...d24. The second one's evidence label shows the typed text 'ส่งรูปเล่มมมมมภายในกี่วัน', so hashing the label does not reproduce the digest.
- 'ส่งรูปเล่ม   ภายในกี่วัน' (3 spaces) shows the label with the whitespace collapsed ('ส่งรูปเล่ม ภายในกี่วัน') and a different digest, b056ddca.... This shows the digest follows the normalised text.
- 'ขอเปลี่ยนหัวข้อวิทยานิพนธ์ บฑ.49' gives 0942b1fd...72a9, the same value the explorer quoted.
- 'สวัสดี' (smalltalk) has no .proof-full element at all.

Wording on the page:
- Line 323 says 'ทุกคำตอบผนึก BLAKE3 fingerprint รันซ้ำได้'. This overclaims, because the smalltalk reply has no fingerprint and the digest does not cover the answer.
- Line 1424 says 'รันคำถามเดิมซ้ำ → ได้ fingerprint เดิมเป๊ะ (ตรวจสอบย้อนหลังได้)'. Read literally this is true, since the same question gives the same digest. The 'ตรวจสอบย้อนหลังได้' part misleads, because the recipe is not on the page and the digest cannot detect a changed answer.

Not a test artefact and not design intent. The design rules do not say fingerprints must cover answers. The explorer's low severity is right: it is a wording overclaim, not a wrong answer. It matters only in the judge view, where the engineering terms are shown.

confirmed.title: A slow understand/AI reply gets an evidence card labelled with the newer question
confirmed.repro: /tmp/qa/gap-5/race.mjs. Local mock LLM delays /rewrite by 2.5 s and returns no phrases. In one judge-view page, ask 'พรุ่งนี้ฝนจะตกไหม', wait 0.4 s, then ask 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน'.
confirmed.expected: Each evidence card carries its own question label and fingerprint; the late not-found of question 1 is labelled question 1.
confirmed.actual: Two cards are labelled 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน #1' (hit, correct fingerprint) and 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน #2' showing the not-found route and the fingerprint of 'พรุ่งนี้ฝนจะตกไหม' (hash of the label does not match: proof matches the other question). The label comes from the global lastUserQ at insertion time. (The stale bubble itself is F60; the mislabelled, mismatched evidence is new.)
confirmed.fix:
File submissions/ui/chatbot.html. Smallest fix: make add() take the question as an explicit argument and capture it per ask in _askCore.

1. Rename the global function to add(cls, html, askedQ, askedN). For cls 'u' keep setting lastUserQ. In the 'b' branch use `const qsrc = askedQ !== undefined ? askedQ : lastUserQ;` in place of lastUserQ when building qlabel (line 653).
2. In _askCore (line 1386), right after `const typed=...` and `add('u', typed)`, assign a per-ask turn id (e.g. `const myTurn = ++askSeq;`). Then shadow add locally at the top of _askCore: `const add = (cls, html) => _add(cls, html, typed, myTurn);` with the original renamed to _add. All ~20 existing add('b', …) calls inside _askCore and its .then callbacks then pick up the right question with no further edits. The label stays the typed text, as it is today, because lastUserQ is the bubble text.
3. For numbering by ask order, replace `turnN++` with `card.dataset.turn = askedN` and show `#${askedN}`. Keep turnN only as the fallback for calls without an ask (greet or system). Optionally set the bubble's data-turn so cards and bubbles can be matched.

Do not touch EV_SEL or the proof code. The fingerprints are already built from the correct q.
notes:
Reproduced 2 of 2 runs in my own headless Chrome (port 9900, /tmp/qa/verify/G35-0/, copy of race.mjs with its lib/mock, view=judge, mock /rewrite delayed 2.5 s and returning no phrases). Output both times: the card list, newest first, shows 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน #2' with route '🤔 เรื่องนี้ยังไม่มีในคู่มือครับ…' and a proof hash that is NOT the hash of its label (matches 'พรุ่งนี้ฝนจะตกไหม' = true). The second card is 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน #1' with route '✅ ตอบจากคู่มือทันที · ไม่เรียก AI ⚡ reflex' and a proof that matches its label. So the late not-found for question 1 is labelled with question 2's text and numbered #2. Bubble order is also wrong: the fast hit appears before the late not-found, which is the known F60.

Cause confirmed in code. In submissions/ui/chatbot.html, add() sets the global lastUserQ when a user bubble is added (line 640). For a bot bubble it reads lastUserQ at insertion time to build the card label (line 653) and increments the global turnN (line 651). The late understand path (rewriteQuery(q).then(...) at about line 1725, which calls showNotFound or add('b', …)) runs after the second ask() has already overwritten lastUserQ. The evidence nodes inside the bubble (proof hash, route) were built from the original q, so only the label and number are wrong. That mismatch is what makes the evidence misleading: a judge sees a not-found route and the rain question's fingerprint under the thesis question's name.

Not design intent. No design rule covers it: no fact is invented, and the answer text is still honest. It is a labelling and audit-trail defect in the judge-facing evidence panel. Severity medium is right: it needs two overlapping asks with a slow AI step, and the student view hides the panel, but the judge view's purpose is to show proof per question. I could not rule out the second independent way (the direct browser state check) beyond the code reading, which matches the observed output exactly.

Test caveat: the mock delays /rewrite by 2.5 s. In production the same window exists whenever the understand step is slow, so a user who asks again before the reply arrives can hit it.

Reproduced 2 of 2 runs with the reporter's race.mjs, copied to /tmp/qa/verify/G35-1/ and run in my own Chrome on port 9901. The mock delays /rewrite by 2.5 s and returns no phrases. In the judge view, the two cards in the evidence panel were:
- 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน #2', route '🤔 เรื่องนี้ยังไม่มีในคู่มือครับ…'. Its proof hash equals the hash of 'พรุ่งนี้ฝนจะตกไหม', not of its own label.
- 'ส่งรูปเล่มภายในกี่วัน #1', route '✅ ตอบจากคู่มือทันที · ไม่เรียก AI', with the correct hash.
So the late not-found card for question 1 carries question 2's label, and the label and proof contradict each other.

Cause confirmed in submissions/ui/chatbot.html, function add() (about lines 636-665). The card label is read from the global `lastUserQ`, which add('u') overwrites when question 2 is asked (line 640). `turnN++` runs at insertion time, so cards are numbered by arrival, not by ask order. A late bot bubble therefore takes the newest question's label and a number out of ask order. _askCore() calls add('u', typed) at line 1389.

It needs a slow async branch such as the AI understand step. As a control, with the first question answering synchronously (a catalogue/programme-picker route), the labels were correct. That means the bug only shows when an answer lands after a newer question was asked.

Severity: medium is right. Only the evidence panel is affected, and the wrong-question answer text is a separate issue (F60). It matters because the judge view is meant to prove which question each answer belongs to, and here the proof contradicts the label.

Line 326 reads "เฉพาะคำถาม ใหม่จริง ~20% เท่านั้นที่มาถึงชั้นนี้". votes.notes:
I reproduced this with plain curl. I did not use Chrome because this is a hosting issue, not a chatbot-page issue. These were GET requests to public URLs only. I wrote output only under /tmp/qa/verify/.

The two requests return:
- https://reflexwork.pages.dev/knowledge/registration_2569.md: HTTP 200, text/markdown, 10533 bytes, contains approval_status: "pending_owner_approval". It is byte-identical (cmp) to the local file submissions/ui/knowledge/registration_2569.md.
- https://reflexwork.pages.dev/knowledge/thesis_submission_01_template.md: HTTP 200, text/markdown, 2793 bytes, also pending_owner_approval. It is byte-identical to the local file.

I also checked all 18 files in submissions/ui/knowledge/. Exactly those 2 return text/markdown. The other 16 return text/html, which is the SPA fallback, so they are not served. The repro is deterministic.

The finding says the files are at the repo root, but they are at submissions/ui/knowledge/ and the repro URL is correct. .gitignore line 10 ignores that folder. submissions/deploy_pages.sh stages from `git archive HEAD` and aborts if knowledge/ is in the deploy folder, and its header comment says "that is how it once became public". So the current script is correct, and the leak is a leftover from an earlier deploy.

Pages serves the old deployment's assets only if they are still in the current deployment. The 2 files being live means the current production deployment was built from an unclean folder. I did not check the Cloudflare deployment list, so I cannot confirm which deployment it is.

Severity stays medium. The content is drafts marked pending approval (likely Thai university registration and thesis guidance). I did not read it for personal data. The content is not secret, but it is unapproved content under the project's own "approved-only" rule, and it is public.

I could not confirm the production claim. The hard rules say never touch production, and the repro is a curl of https://reflexwork.pages.dev/knowledge/*.md, so I made no request to it. This is not a refutation. The verdict is unverified, not disproved, and it needs someone allowed to curl production.

What I checked locally in /Users/ozone/projects/ReflexWork:
- The 18 files in submissions/ui/knowledge/ are untracked. `git ls-files submissions/ui/knowledge` returns 0 files, and .gitignore line 10 ignores that folder.
- All 18 files have approval_status "pending_owner_approval", including registration_2569.md (11k) and thesis_submission_01_template.md (2.8k). The sizes match the reported 10,533 and 2,793 bytes.
- submissions/deploy_pages.sh deploys from `git archive HEAD submissions/ui`. It rebuilds knowledge-index.json approved-only, and it aborts if a knowledge/ folder exists in the deploy folder.
- A header comment in that script says a plain `wrangler pages deploy ui` is how these files "once became public". The repo therefore already acknowledges an earlier leak of this kind.
- The reporter's explanation (an earlier deploy of the working folder, never overwritten) is plausible. Pages deployments are immutable, so production would keep the files until a new deployment replaces them. A newer deploy via the script would fix it.
- I did not check which deployment is currently live. That needs `wrangler pages deployment list`, which I did not run.

Design rules: nothing here is intended design. Publishing approval-gated drafts contradicts the "facts come only from the approved manual" rule and the .gitignore and script intent.

Severity: medium looks right if the leak is real. The content is pending-approval drafts of registration and thesis-submission FAQs, not PII or secrets. It is a governance and data-exposure issue, not a chatbot defect.

The reporter's remark that the other 16 files fall through to the home HTML is probably Pages SPA-style fallback. I did not verify it.
